lessons.title: First day at the office
lessons.description: Introduce yourself as an intern, handle an internal call and read office instructions without confusing humble and honorific actors.
lessons.canDo: Identify the right office contact and introduce myself with appropriate modest language

grammar.title: Modest language for your own side
grammar.formation: 言う → 申す; 行く/来る → 参る; する → いたす; いる → おる. Asking/visiting a respected person: 伺う; viewing a respected person's material: 拝見する. General humble action directed towards a respected person: お + Japanese verb ます-stem + する; ご + suitable Sino-Japanese action noun + する. Not every verb takes these patterns; use established special forms where needed.
grammar.explanation: Use modest forms for yourself or your own side. 申す・参る・いたす・おる can make speech formal to the listener without implying that every action is directed towards them. 伺う and 拝見する lower your action in relation to a respected person or their material. Do not call a visitor's action humble on their behalf. おります is common formal 'am/is here'; unit 7's いらっしゃいます raises the other actor. For a message directed to a respected person, お伝えします lowers your conveying action. ご説明します is a noun-based example. These are action-relative humble patterns, not self-honorific お～になる.
grammar.example: 実習に参りました。
grammar.translation: I've come for the internship training (modest).

examples.ja: バオと{申|もう}します。
examples.en: My name is Bao (modest).

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}を{拝見|はいけん}します。
examples.en: I'll look at the materials (humble).

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}に{用件|ようけん}をお{伝|つた}えします。
examples.en: I'll convey the matter to the teacher (humble).

grammar.mistake: Use your own name + と申します. 先生がおります lowers the teacher rather than respecting them; use 先生はいらっしゃいます when respect is intended.

grammar.title: Put a question inside a sentence; name something
grammar.formation: Question word + plain clause + か + main verb. Yes/no plain clause + かどうか. Noun + という + noun. Before embedded か, noun/な-adjective present affirmative normally omits だ.
grammar.explanation: どの会議室を使うか確認します means checking which meeting room is used. There is one main statement, not two independent questions. 会議があるかどうか asks whether there is a meeting. ～という introduces a name or label: 青葉システムという会社. These constructions do not confirm the embedded proposition; someone can check whether a meeting exists without saying it does.
grammar.example: どの会議室を使うか確認します。
grammar.translation: I'll check which meeting room we will use.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}が{誰|だれ}か{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I'll check who is in charge.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}があるかどうか{聞|き}きます。
examples.en: I'll ask whether there is a meeting.

examples.ja: {青葉|あおば}システムという{会社|かいしゃ}です。
examples.en: It is a company called Aoba Systems (fictional course company).

grammar.mistake: An embedded question does not need a question mark after か. Use 誰か here, not 誰だか in the formal pattern practised in this unit. という labels a name, not an ability or permission.

grammar.title: Easy to do, hard to do, without doing
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい / にくい, conjugated as い-adjectives. Verb negative ない-form + で + following action.
grammar.explanation: 読みやすい describes something as easy to read; 使いにくい describes difficulty of use. These forms concern ease rather than your permission to do the action. ～ないで describes doing an action without another: 教科書を見ないで答えます. Distinguish this from ～なくてもいい, which removes an obligation, and from ～ないでください, a request not to do something.
grammar.example: 名前を確認しないで、電話をかけないでください。
grammar.translation: Please don't make the call without checking the name.

examples.ja: この{資料|しりょう}は{読|よ}みやすいです。
examples.en: These materials are easy to read.

examples.ja: この{電話|でんわ}は{使|つか}いにくいです。
examples.en: This phone is difficult to use.

examples.ja: {教科書|きょうかしょ}を{見|み}ないで、{答|こた}えます。
examples.en: I'll answer without looking at the textbook.

grammar.mistake: Use 読みやすい, not 読むやすい. ～ないで is not ～なくてもいい: 'without doing' and 'needn't do' describe different things.

lessons.title: A changed meeting room
lessons.description: Distinguish a passive event from a prepared state, report an interruption and read a room-change notice.
lessons.canDo: Identify who was affected by an event and what has been deliberately prepared

grammar.title: An event from the affected person's viewpoint
grammar.formation: Group 1 final u → a + れる (う → われる): 呼ぶ → 呼ばれる. Group 2 drop る + られる: 起こす is Group 1 → 起こされる. する → される; 来る → 来られる. Affected person は actor に passive verb.
grammar.explanation: 森さんに呼ばれました describes being called by Mori. A direct passive need not express annoyance. A suffering passive can make the affected person the subject even if the event was not done directly to them: 雨に降られました means being inconvenienced by rain. With another person's object-related action, retain the object with を: 隣の人に電気を消されました. Context, not the passive ending alone, establishes inconvenience. Some られる forms also express potential or respect; use the actor and situation to interpret them.
grammar.example: 森さんに呼ばれました。
grammar.translation: I was called by Mori.

examples.ja: {森|もり}さんに{呼|よ}ばれました。
examples.en: I was called by Mori.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}に{起|お}こされました。
examples.en: I was woken by my younger brother.

examples.ja: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}に{電気|でんき}を{消|け}されて、{困|こま}りました。
examples.en: The person next to me turned off the light, which caused me trouble.

grammar.mistake: 呼ぶ → 呼ばれる, not 呼ぶられる. Passive does not automatically mean the speaker was angry; do not infer annoyance from a neutral report of being called.

grammar.title: A deliberately prepared state; an event during an interval
grammar.formation: Transitive verb て-form + ある; the prepared object commonly takes が. Verb plain form + 間に; noun + の間に; な-adjective + な間に. い-adjective final い → く + する; な-adjective + にする.
grammar.explanation: 資料が置いてあります points to materials deliberately placed and left ready. It differs from simply describing where someone is or the automatic state of a door. 間に places an event or completion within an interval: 会議の間に電話がありました. 間 without に can describe an action continuing throughout the interval. 明るくする and 静かにする describe making something bright or quiet, rather than just observing that it is so.
grammar.example: 机に資料が置いてあります。
grammar.translation: The materials have been placed on the desk and are ready there.

examples.ja: ドアに{知|し}らせが{貼|は}ってあります。
examples.en: A notice has been put up on the door.

grammar.title: What I want someone to do; recognize casual shortening
grammar.formation: Person に verb て-form + ほしい; negative ないでほしい. ている → てる; でいる → でる. ておく → とく; でおく → どく. なければ → なきゃ (an obligation ending may be omitted conversationally).
grammar.explanation: 森さんに確認してほしい says that I want Mori to check, rather than that Mori wants to check. Requests with ほしい can sound direct; do not replace professional requests to senior colleagues mechanically with this pattern. In casual conversation, 読んでる means 読んでいる and 書いとく means 書いておく. In 行かなきゃ, the obligation ending is understood. Learn these as recognition forms; careful notices and senior-directed messages retain complete polite wording.
grammar.example: 担当の人に確認してほしいです。
grammar.translation: I want the person in charge to check.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}の{人|ひと}に{確認|かくにん}してほしいです。

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}、{書|か}いとくね。
examples.en: I'll write the name in advance (casual contraction).

grammar.mistake: ～てほしい names your desired action by someone else; ～たい names your own desired action. 読んでいる contracts to 読んでる, not 読んでてる.

grammar: てる / とく / なきゃ
watch.prompt: Optionally save five lines from your own media. Separate a passive event from a deliberate prepared state; expand any contracted endings. Do not label every passive as anger or suffering.

exercises.prompt: What has changed?
options: The room, from A to B
The time, from ten to noon
The materials contact, from Mori to Satō
exercises.explain: Mori keeps the time at ten and names room B.

exercises.prompt: Where have the materials been prepared?
exercises.explain: Bの机に置いてあります states their prepared location.

exercises.prompt: Who answered the call?
exercises.explain: Mori says 私が出ました in Mori's own turn.

exercises.context: While you were reading, a person next to you turned off the light and inconvenienced you. Choose the suffering-passive description from your viewpoint.
exercises.line: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}に{電気|でんき}を＿＿、{困|こま}りました。
exercises.explain: 消されて is the passive of the transitive 消す. 電気 remains the を-marked affected object; the person acting takes に. 困りました supplies the adverse effect.

exercises.context: Mori called you. Report that event from your viewpoint; Mori is the actor.
exercises.line: {私|わたし}は{森|もり}さんに＿＿。
exercises.explain: 呼ばれました makes you the called person and Mori the に-marked actor.

exercises.context: Describe a notice that someone intentionally posted and left ready on the door.
exercises.line: ドアに{知|し}らせが{貼|は}って＿＿。
exercises.explain: 貼ってあります presents a deliberate resulting state.

exercises.context: Ask someone to make the room brighter.
exercises.line: {部屋|へや}を＿＿してください。
exercises.explain: い-adjective → く + する: 明るくする.

exercises.context: Say you want the person in charge to check. You are describing your wish, not giving a senior a polite request.
exercises.line: {担当|たんとう}の{人|ひと}に{確認|かくにん}して＿＿です。
exercises.explain: てほしい expresses a desired action by the に-marked person.

exercises.line: {会議|かいぎ}は{中止|ちゅうし}ですか。
exercises.context: The meeting still happens at ten in B. Correct the cancellation assumption.
options: はい、{会議|かいぎ}はありません。
はい、{時間|じかん}は{十二時|じゅうにじ}です。
いいえ。{十時|じゅうじ}にBであります。
exercises.explain: The first reply denies cancellation and retains the stated time and room.

exercises.line: {資料|しりょう}はどこですか。
exercises.context: You placed the materials on the desk and left them there. Report that prepared state.
options: {机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。
まだ{置|お}いていません。
{客|きゃく}が{読|よ}んでいます。
exercises.explain: 置いてあります matches both the deliberate preparation and location.

exercises.meaning: There was a phone call during the meeting.
exercises.explain: 間に locates the event within the meeting interval.

exercises.context: Kenta casually says he will write the notice in advance. Recognize the contraction of 書いておく; this is not a formal office notice.
exercises.prompt: Which casual line means 'I'll write the notice in advance'?
exercises.line: {知|し}らせを{書|か}いておくね。

lessons.title: Let me try the presentation
lessons.description: Distinguish making someone act from letting them act, ask permission to present, and compare a guide's advice with a practice scene.
lessons.canDo: Ask to take an action politely and identify the purpose and conditions of a practice plan

grammar.title: Make or let someone act; ask to be allowed
grammar.formation: Group 1 u → a + せる (う → わせる): 書く → 書かせる. Group 2 drop る + させる: 食べる → 食べさせる. する → させる; 来る → 来させる (こさせる). Intransitive: causer は person を causative; transitive: causer は person に object を causative. Causative て-form + もらう/いただく. Causative て-form + あげる/くれる describes granting permission as a benefit with the giving viewpoints from unit 2.
grammar.explanation: The causative can mean making or allowing, depending on context; its ending alone does not decide. 森さんは私に資料を読ませました keeps 資料 as the を-marked object. 説明させていただけませんか asks a respected listener to allow your explanation. Do not use this phrase just to make any sentence sound fancy: it is practised here because Mori controls the presentation opportunity. させてもらいました describes receiving that permission, not making Mori do the work. 森さんが発表させてくれました presents Mori granting permission to me as a benefit. 友達に練習させてあげました presents me granting a friend permission. Avoid させてあげる about allowing a senior: it can imply that you control or favour them.
grammar.example: 私に説明させていただけませんか。
grammar.translation: Could you allow me to give the explanation?

examples.ja: {森|もり}さんは{私|わたし}に{発表|はっぴょう}させてくれました。
examples.en: Mori kindly allowed me to present.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}、{私|わたし}に{発表|はっぴょう}させていただけませんか。
examples.en: Could you let me present today?

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}に{練習|れんしゅう}させてあげました。
examples.en: I let my friend practise (presented as a benefit to them).

grammar.mistake: 読む → 読ませる, not 読むさせる. 'I was allowed to practise' is 練習させてもらいました; 練習してもらいました asks someone else to practise for you.

grammar.title: Conditions, unexpected contrast and firm instructions
grammar.formation: Group 1 u → e + ば; Group 2 drop る + れば; する → すれば; 来る → 来れば. い-adjective い → ければ; negative ない → なければ. Plain clause + のに (noun/な-adjective + なのに). Verb ます-stem + なさい.
grammar.explanation: 練習すれば describes a condition; it does not prove that practice guarantees success in real life. ～のに contrasts an outcome with what was expected and may convey disappointment. ～なさい is a firm direction used by a parent or teacher to someone under their guidance. It is not an office peer's neutral polite request. Where the first condition is an intentional action, do not mechanically attach any command to ～ば; the examples here use states/possibilities or descriptive consequences.
grammar.example: 練習したのに、緊張しました。
grammar.translation: Although I practised, I felt nervous.

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}があれば、もう{一度|いちど}{練習|れんしゅう}できます。
examples.en: If there is time, we can practise once more.

examples.ja: {練習|れんしゅう}したのに、{緊張|きんちょう}しました。
examples.en: Although I practised, I felt nervous.

examples.ja: まず、{見本|みほん}を{読|よ}みなさい。
examples.en: First, read the example (firm teacher instruction).

grammar.mistake: 静かなら and 静かであれば are possible conditions, but 静かければ is not. Before のに use 必要なのに for a な-adjective, not 必要のに.

grammar.title: Like a model: のように and のような
grammar.formation: Noun + のように + verb/adjective; noun + のような + noun.
grammar.explanation: 見本のように書く means write like the model. 見本のような説明 describes an explanation like the model. The phrase expresses resemblance; it does not assert that the two things are identical. This noun-linked pattern differs from a plain-clause ようだ inference taught later. Keep the noun and its の when it is the comparison standard.
grammar.example: 見本のように書いてください。
grammar.translation: Please write like the model.

examples.ja: {見本|みほん}のように{書|か}いてください。
examples.en: Please write like the model.

examples.ja: {森|もり}さんのように{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて{話|はな}したいです。
examples.en: I want to speak calmly like Mori.

examples.ja: {見本|みほん}のような{説明|せつめい}はわかりやすいです。
examples.en: An explanation like the model is easy to understand.

grammar.mistake: Before the noun 説明 use のような; before 書く use のように. Do not use 見本のように説明 when you mean 'an explanation like the model' as a noun phrase.

dialogues.title: Ask for a practice turn
dialogues.scene: Mori controls today's practice session. You ask permission to present. This practice is in room B after the earlier room change.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {森|もり}さん、{今日|きょう}は{私|わたし}に{発表|はっぴょう}させていただけませんか。
lines.romaji: Mori-san, kyō wa watashi ni happyō sasete itadakemasen ka.
lines.meaning: Mori, could you let me present today?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: いいですよ。{会議室|かいぎしつ}Bで{練習|れんしゅう}しましょう。{資料|しりょう}は{机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。
lines.romaji: Ii desu yo. Kaigishitsu bī de renshū shimashō. Shiryō wa tsukue ni oite arimasu.
lines.meaning: Certainly. Let's practise in meeting room B. The materials have been placed on the desk.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとうございます。{練習|れんしゅう}したのに、まだ{緊張|きんちょう}しています。

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: まず、{企画|きかく}の{目的|もくてき}を{伝|つた}えてください。{時間|じかん}があれば、もう{一度|いちど}できます。
lines.romaji: Mazu, kikaku no mokuteki o tsutaete kudasai. Jikan ga areba, mō ichido dekimasu.
lines.meaning: First explain the purpose of the proposal. If there's time, you can do it again.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{森|もり}さんのように、{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて{話|はな}したいです。
lines.romaji: Hai. Mori-san no yō ni, ochitsuite hanashitai desu.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {間違|まちが}いがあったら、あとで{直|なお}せます。{始|はじ}めましょう。

lines.meaning: If there is a mistake, you can correct it later. Let's start.

dialogues.title: After the practice
dialogues.scene: The practice has ended. Mori's feedback identifies a clear purpose but an unclear method. It does not claim a perfect result.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {目的|もくてき}はわかりやすかったです。でも、{方法|ほうほう}の{説明|せつめい}が{少|すこ}し{難|むずか}しかったです。

lines.meaning: The purpose was clear. But the explanation of the method was a little difficult.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {方法|ほうほう}の{説明|せつめい}を{直|なお}します。{順番|じゅんばん}も{確|たし}かめます。
lines.romaji: Hōhō no setsumei o naoshimasu. Junban mo tashikamemasu.
lines.meaning: I'll revise the method explanation. I'll also check the order.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: この{見本|みほん}をご{覧|らん}ください。{見本|みほん}のような{説明|せつめい}を{考|かんが}えてください。
lines.romaji: Kono mihon o goran kudasai. Mihon no yō na setsumei o kangaete kudasai.
lines.meaning: Please look at this model. Think of an explanation like the model.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {資料|しりょう}に{書|か}いてから、もう{一度|いちど}{練習|れんしゅう}したいです。
lines.romaji: Shiryō ni kaite kara, mō ichido renshū shitai desu.
lines.meaning: I'd like to write it in the materials, then practise once more.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {今日|きょう}はもう{時間|じかん}がありません。{明日|あした}、{十時|じゅうじ}なら{練習|れんしゅう}できます。
lines.romaji: Kyō wa mō jikan ga arimasen. Ashita, jūji nara renshū dekimasu.
lines.meaning: There's no more time today. Tomorrow at ten you can practise.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: では、{明日|あした}お{願|ねが}いします。{練習|れんしゅう}させていただいて、ありがとうございました。
lines.romaji: Dewa, ashita onegai shimasu. Renshū sasete itadaite, arigatō gozaimashita.
lines.meaning: Then, tomorrow please. Thank you for allowing me to practise.

grammar: のように / のような
watch.prompt: Optionally save five lines from your own media and identify who performs each causative action. Expand the actor and object in English; do not assume the causative always means force.

exercises.prompt: What permission does Bao request?

exercises.prompt: What should Bao explain first?
exercises.explain: まず企画の目的 establishes the first focus.

exercises.prompt: Which part needs revision according to Mori?
exercises.explain: Mori contrasts the clear purpose with the difficult method explanation.

exercises.prompt: When is another practice possible?
exercises.explain: Today's time is gone; Mori offers tomorrow at ten.

exercises.context: Mori had you read the materials. Complete the causative form of 読む.
exercises.line: {森|もり}さんは{私|わたし}に{資料|しりょう}を＿＿。

exercises.context: Describe an explanation like the model; the comparison modifies the noun 説明.
exercises.line: {見本|みほん}＿＿{説明|せつめい}を{考|かんが}えます。
exercises.explain: Noun + のような + noun; のように would modify an action or adjective.

exercises.line: {練習|れんしゅう}した＿＿、{緊張|きんちょう}しました。

exercises.line: {私|わたし}に{説明|せつめい}させていただけませんか。
exercises.context: You control the practice session. Give permission for the learner to explain.

{私|わたし}が{説明|せつめい}します。
はい、{説明|せつめい}してください。

options: では、{明日|あした}お{願|ねが}いします。

{今日|きょう}は{時間|じかん}がたくさんありますね。

exercises.meaning: Please write like the model.

{発表|はっぴょう}してもらいました。

lessons.title: Choosing a better practice routine
lessons.description: Report being made to do something, distinguish a personal decision from an external arrangement, and compare study methods without treating persistence as guaranteed success.
lessons.canDo: Explain a chosen routine and identify what happened despite a condition

grammar.title: Being made to do something
grammar.formation: Passive of the causative: Group 1 u → a + せられる (う → わせられる); Group 2 drop る + させられる; する → させられる; 来る → 来させられる (こさせられる). Many Group 1 verbs shorten aせられる → aされる: 読ませられる → 読まされる; す-ending 話す retains 話させられる.
grammar.explanation: 私は先生に読まされました puts the person made to read in the subject position and the person causing the action in に. It often expresses unwillingness, but do not infer an entire relationship from a form alone. It differs from unit 10's 読ませてもらいました, where permission to read is received as a benefit. In this unit Kenta recalls one difficult classroom exercise; that does not establish that all teachers force unreasonable work.
grammar.example: 先生に長い文を読まされました。
grammar.translation: I was made to read a long sentence by the teacher.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}に{長|なが}い{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}まされました。
examples.en: The teacher made me read a long sentence.

examples.ja: {先輩|せんぱい}に{何度|なんど}も{説明|せつめい}させられました。
examples.en: My senior colleague made me explain repeatedly.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}に{待|ま}たされました。
examples.en: I was made to wait by my friend.

grammar.mistake: 待つ → 待たされる, not 待たれる (passive) or 待たせる (causative). 話す → 話させられる; do not shorten it to 話さされる in the standard pattern.

grammar.title: Make a decision; keep a rule; continue until
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary/ない form + ことにする (decide); + ことにしている (maintain a personal practice). Verb plain nonpast + まで; noun/time + まで.
grammar.explanation: 毎日復習することにしました reports your decision. 毎日復習することにしています describes a routine you choose to maintain. The later ことになる pattern describes an arrangement/result, so do not interpret every こと expression as personal choice. ～まで describes continuing until an endpoint; ～までに is a deadline for completing an action. Context and action determine the difference. A chosen practice is not evidence that someone already mastered the words.
grammar.example: 毎日、短い文を読むことにしました。
grammar.translation: I decided to read short sentences every day.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}、{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}むことにしました。
examples.en: I decided to read short sentences every day.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は、{休|やす}むことにしています。
examples.en: I make it my practice to rest when tired.

examples.ja: {森|もり}さんが{来|く}るまで、ここで{待|ま}ちます。
examples.en: I'll wait here until Mori comes.

grammar.mistake: A deadline for handing in a document is 金曜日までに, not automatically 金曜日まで. A planned habit expressed with ことにしている does not guarantee you never miss a day.

grammar.title: Even if; how to do something
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + も; い-adjective い → くても; noun/な-adjective + でも. AよりBの方が + adjective. Verb dictionary form + 方が for a general comparison of actions; verb past + 方がいい often gives advice. Verb ます-stem + 方 (かた): 読む → 読み方; 使う → 使い方; する → し方; 勉強する → 勉強の仕方. Noun objects commonly become の: 文を読む → 文の読み方.
grammar.explanation: 間違えても続けます means a mistake does not stop the chosen action. It differs from ～のに, which contrasts an actual situation with an unexpected result. 短い文の方が読みやすい compares readability in this context, not the value of all short and long texts. Rest advice is not a medical diagnosis. Forms like 休んだ方がいい advise an action; they do not report that someone already rested. 読み方 means how to read or a reading method; 方 is pronounced かた here. It is different from comparison 方 (ほう) in unit 5/N5 comparisons. Learn the noun-linked object: この文の読み方. Suru nouns use の仕方, as in 勉強の仕方.
grammar.example: 間違えても、もう一度読みます。
grammar.translation: Even if I make a mistake, I'll read it again.

examples.ja: {間違|まちが}えても、もう{一度|いちど}{読|よ}みます。
examples.en: Even if I make a mistake, I'll read it again.

examples.ja: この{文|ぶん}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: Please teach me how to read this sentence.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は、{少|すこ}し{休|やす}んだ{方|ほう}がいいです。
examples.en: When tired, it is better to rest a little.

grammar.mistake: For 静か use 静かでも, not 静かくても. ～ても does not assert that the hypothetical event has actually happened. For how to read, use 読み方 (よみかた), not 読む方 (よむほう), which names the reading alternative/person in a different context.

dialogues.title: A routine that is easier to keep
dialogues.scene: Kenta describes a past class exercise. You choose a short daily reading routine; no test result is claimed.

lines.line: {昨日|きのう}、{先生|せんせい}に{長|なが}い{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}まされたんだ。{疲|つか}れたよ。

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: いいね。{長|なが}い{文|ぶん}より、{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}の{方|ほう}が{読|よ}みやすいね。

lines.meaning: Good idea. Short sentences are easier to read than long ones.

exercises.prompt: What happened to Kenta in yesterday's class?
options: The teacher made him read a long sentence

exercises.prompt: Which routine has Bao chosen?

lessons.title: The internship handover
lessons.description: Combine polite requests, embedded questions, prepared states and personal decisions in an original internship handover. Course completion is a checkpoint, not an N4 certificate.
lessons.canDo: Find a document deadline, distinguish its owner and confirm a next-step arrangement

grammar.title: Choose the actor in a professional request
grammar.formation: Ask a senior to act: verb て-form + いただけませんか. Ask permission for your own action: causative て-form + いただけませんか. Describe your own viewing: 拝見する; respectfully describe another person's viewing: ご覧になる.
grammar.explanation: This is a consolidation of units 4, 7, 8 and 10. 報告書を確認していただけませんか asks Mori to check. 説明させていただけませんか asks to be allowed to explain yourself. The two expressions have different actors; longer language is not automatically more suitable. In this scenario a senior really controls the explanation slot, making the permission request meaningful. A polite request does not prove it was granted.
grammar.example: 報告書を確認していただけませんか。
grammar.translation: Could you check my report?

examples.ja: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{確認|かくにん}していただけませんか。
examples.en: Could you check my report?

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}で{説明|せつめい}させていただけませんか。
examples.en: Could you allow me to explain at the meeting?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}の{返事|へんじ}を{拝見|はいけん}しました。
examples.en: I read the teacher's reply (humble).

grammar.mistake: 確認させていただけませんか requests permission for you to check, not for Mori to check. Always identify the intended actor before choosing a form.

grammar.title: Confirm deadlines and prepared documents
grammar.formation: Question clause + か + 確認する; yes/no clause + かどうか. Completed action deadline + までに; continuing action + まで. Transitive verb て-form + ある for a deliberately prepared state.
grammar.explanation: This consolidates units 8, 9 and 11. いつ提出するか確認します asks for the submission timing without claiming it is known. 金曜日の三時までに提出する specifies completion by that deadline; 三時まで待つ describes waiting until then. 資料が置いてあります describes their ready state, while their presence alone does not show that an approval was granted. Read the actual approval statement separately.
grammar.example: 金曜日の三時までに提出します。
grammar.translation: I'll submit it by three on Friday.

examples.ja: いつ{提出|ていしゅつ}するか{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I'll check when to submit it.

examples.ja: {金曜日|きんようび}の{三時|さんじ}までに{提出|ていしゅつ}します。
examples.en: I'll submit it by three on Friday.

examples.ja: {返却|へんきゃく}の{案内|あんない}が{机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。
examples.en: The return instructions have been placed ready on the desk.

grammar.mistake: 'On the desk' does not mean 'approved'. Keep まで and までに distinct according to the action, not merely the clock time.

grammar.title: Separate a decision, a condition and an actual outcome
grammar.formation: Personal decision: dictionary/ない + ことにする; chosen routine: + ことにしている. Hypothetical concession: て-form + も. Actual unexpected contrast: plain + のに; noun/な-adjective + なのに.
grammar.explanation: This consolidates units 10 and 11. 毎日復習することにしました is a chosen plan, not an achieved proficiency level. 間違えても続けます gives a policy for a possible mistake. 練習したのに緊張しました reports both completed practice and the unexpected nervousness. Finishing this app's N4 units is course evidence; it is not an official JLPT result or proof of unaided listening comprehension.
grammar.example: 毎日復習することにしました。
grammar.translation: I decided to review every day.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{復習|ふくしゅう}することにしました。
examples.en: I decided to review every day.

examples.ja: {間違|まちが}えても、{練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}けます。
examples.en: Even if I make a mistake, I'll keep practising.

examples.ja: {練習|れんしゅう}したのに、{緊張|きんちょう}しました。
examples.en: Although I practised, I felt nervous.

grammar.mistake: A future routine is not a completed result. Translate a planned action as a plan, and do not infer success from either ことにした or ても.

dialogues.title: The final internship arrangements
dialogues.scene: Mori gives the internship's Friday handover requirements. The report and key have different destinations and deadlines.

readings.title: Mori's final-week email
paragraphs: バオさんへ。
{実習|じっしゅう}は{金曜日|きんようび}に{終了|しゅうりょう}します。

{報告書|ほうこくしょ}に{自分|じぶん}の{名前|なまえ}も{書|か}いてください。
{最初|さいしょ}に{目的|もくてき}を{伝|つた}えてください。
{方法|ほうほう}の{説明|せつめい}は、{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}でお{願|ねが}いします。
{金曜日|きんようび}の{三時|さんじ}までに、{私|わたし}に{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
{木曜日|もくようび}なら、{提出|ていしゅつ}する{前|まえ}に{確認|かくにん}できます。
{鍵|かぎ}は{金曜日|きんようび}の{五時|ごじ}までに、{受付|うけつけ}に{返却|へんきゃく}してください。
{返却|へんきゃく}の{案内|あんない}が{机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。
{受付|うけつけ}で{名前|なまえ}を{伝|つた}えてから、{鍵|かぎ}を{返却|へんきゃく}してください。
{質問|しつもん}があれば、{内線|ないせん}{二十番|にじゅうばん}に{連絡|れんらく}してください。
{実習|じっしゅう}のあとも、{復習|ふくしゅう}を{続|つづ}けてください。

watch.prompt: Optionally save five lines from your own media about handing over a task. Identify the responsible person, deadline and whether the line confirms a completed action or only a plan.

exercises.prompt: Who should receive the report, and by when?
exercises.explain: Mori says 私に提出 and gives Friday three as the deadline.

exercises.prompt: Where should the key go?
exercises.explain: 鍵は受付に返却 specifies a different destination from the report.

exercises.prompt: When can Mori check the report before submission?
exercises.explain: Mori offers 木曜日なら確認できます.

exercises.prompt: Which improvement does Bao say is already done?
exercises.explain: 方法の説明は直しました states one completed revision, not a proficiency claim.

exercises.context: Complete the deadline for finishing the report submission, not a period of waiting.
exercises.line: {金曜日|きんようび}の{三時|さんじ}＿＿、{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{提出|ていしゅつ}します。
exercises.explain: までに marks the submission completion deadline.

exercises.context: Say you will check when to submit the report; do not state a fixed time.
exercises.line: いつ{提出|ていしゅつ}する＿＿、{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: Question clause + か embeds the timing question.

exercises.context: The return instructions have been deliberately placed and left on the desk.
exercises.line: {返却|へんきゃく}の{案内|あんない}が{置|お}いて＿＿。
exercises.explain: てある describes the prepared result, not trying or wishing.

exercises.context: Report your own decision to continue daily review.
exercises.line: {毎日|まいにち}の{復習|ふくしゅう}を{続|つづ}ける＿＿。
exercises.explain: Dictionary form + ことにしました expresses a chosen action.

exercises.line: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{金曜日|きんようび}の{三時|さんじ}までに{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
exercises.context: Confirm the report deadline accurately.
options: はい、{金曜日|きんようび}の{五時|ごじ}までに{提出|ていしゅつ}します。
はい、{提出|ていしゅつ}は{来週|らいしゅう}です。
はい、{金曜日|きんようび}の{三時|さんじ}までに{提出|ていしゅつ}します。
exercises.explain: The five o'clock deadline belongs to the key, not the report.

exercises.line: {毎日|まいにち}の{復習|ふくしゅう}は{続|つづ}けますか。
exercises.context: State your plan to continue despite mistakes, while resting when tired.
options: はい。{間違|まちが}えても{続|つづ}けます。{疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は{休|やす}みます。
いいえ、もう{復習|ふくしゅう}しません。
はい。{疲|つか}れても{絶対|ぜったい}に{休|やす}みません。
exercises.explain: The first response includes both parts of Bao's plan.

exercises.meaning: I'll return the key after giving my name.
exercises.explain: てから makes the name step come first.

exercises.context: You ask senior Mori to check your report. Mori should do the checking; you are not asking permission to check it yourself.
exercises.prompt: Which polite request assigns the intended action to Mori?
options: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{確認|かくにん}させていただけませんか。
{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{確認|かくにん}していただけませんか。
{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{確認|かくにん}していただきました。
exercises.explain: ていただけませんか requests Mori's action; causative changes it to your permission, and the past form reports a completed favour.

exercises.prompt: Which item is due to reception by Friday at five?
exercises.explain: The email separates the key return from the three o'clock report submission.

exercises.prompt: Which three topics should the report include?
options: A test score, a room map and every colleague's address
exercises.explain: 経験、結果、次の課題 is the requested list.

exercises.prompt: What must happen before handing back the key?
exercises.explain: 名前を伝えてから establishes the return sequence.

exercises.prompt: What does the email establish about checking the report?
options: Mori can check it on Thursday before submission
exercises.explain: 確認できます states an available check. It does not state completed approval.

grammar.title: An ability or routine has changed
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast verb + ようになる. Use a potential verb for becoming able: 読む → 読めるようになる; する → できるようになる. A new routine can use an ordinary verb: 記録するようになる. Polite past: ～ようになりました.
grammar.explanation: Describe the resulting change, not merely your intention. A recording from last month and a recording from today can provide an observation to compare. The construction itself doesn’t quantify fluency. These community-N4 forms bridge gaps in this course before the N3 purpose contrast. Loss of an action/ability commonly uses ～なくなる; don’t mechanically turn every negative change into ないようになる.
grammar.example: 以前より短い文を速く読めるようになりました。
grammar.translation: I have become able to read short sentences faster than before.

examples.ja: {以前|いぜん}より{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}を{速|はや}く{読|よ}めるようになりました。
examples.en: I have become able to read short sentences faster than before.

examples.ja: {練習|れんしゅう}の{後|あと}で{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}すようになりました。
examples.en: I have started looking over my record after practice.

examples.ja: {落|お}ち{着|つ}いて{発表|はっぴょう}できるようになりたいです。
examples.en: I want to become able to present calmly.

grammar.mistake: 読めるようになりたい describes a wish; 読めるようになりました reports a change. Neither tells us that every text is now understood.

grammar.title: Make a conscious effort
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast/ない verb + ようにする. ～ようにしています describes ongoing effort; ～ようにしてください asks someone to take care to do/not do it.
grammar.explanation: Choose a practice behaviour that you can actually carry out. This expresses care or effort and doesn’t promise perfect performance. Compare a chosen effort (確認するようにしています) with an observed new routine (確認するようになりました). Do not confuse the noun-comparison pattern 見本のように with this clause construction.
grammar.example: 発音を確かめるようにしています。
grammar.translation: I make a point of checking my pronunciation.

examples.ja: {発音|はつおん}を{確|たし}かめるようにしています。
examples.en: I make a point of checking my pronunciation.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は{無理|むり}をしないようにしています。
examples.en: I try not to push myself when tired.

examples.ja: {提出|ていしゅつ}する{前|まえ}に{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{見直|みなお}すようにしてください。
examples.en: Please make a point of reviewing the report before submitting it.

grammar.mistake: ようにしている is an ongoing effort. It’s not evidence that an action is always carried out successfully.

grammar.title: Act so that a result becomes possible
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast or ない clause + ように + action. Common first clauses have potential/state verbs: 読める、聞こえる、忘れない. Each clause may have its own subject.
grammar.explanation: The first clause presents an ability, state or avoided outcome; the second describes the action aimed at it. ように doesn’t assert that the goal has already been achieved. The subject can change: everyone should be able to read the text, so one writer enlarges it. The pattern here is purpose, not resemblance.
grammar.example: 後ろの人にも見えるように、字を大きくしました。
grammar.translation: I enlarged the writing so that people at the back can also see it.

examples.ja: {後|うし}ろの{人|ひと}にも{見|み}えるように、{字|じ}を{大|おお}きくしました。
examples.en: I enlarged the writing so that people at the back can also see it.

examples.ja: {方法|ほうほう}を{忘|わす}れないように、{手順|てじゅん}を{記録|きろく}しました。
examples.en: I recorded the steps so I would not forget the method.

examples.ja: {短|みじか}い{会話|かいわ}を{聞|き}き{取|と}れるように、{音|おと}を{調整|ちょうせい}しました。
examples.en: I adjusted the sound so that I can catch the short conversation.

grammar.mistake: Do not use 見えるために in this beginner purpose contrast: 見える is the desired perceptual state, so practise 見えるように.

grammar.title: A deliberate goal: ために versus ように
grammar.formation: Purpose: dictionary-form volitional verb + ために; noun + のために. For a desired ability/state or avoided outcome, use plain nonpast/ない + ように. This unit teaches purpose ために; cause ために is deferred to unit 9.
grammar.explanation: ために connects a purposeful action to a deliberate goal, usually with the same actor controlling both. ように typically aims at a state such as being able to hear. These are useful learning tendencies, not a rule that every verb belongs in only one pattern. Read the context. 学ぶために names deliberate study as the goal; 聞き取れるように aims at listening ability. Do not interpret a practice plan as a completed result.
grammar.example: 新しい方法を学ぶために、講座に参加します。
grammar.translation: I’ll attend the course to learn a new method.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{方法|ほうほう}を{学|まな}ぶために、{講座|こうざ}に{参加|さんか}します。
examples.en: I’ll attend the course to learn a new method.

examples.ja: {発表|はっぴょう}のために、{練習|れんしゅう}の{時間|じかん}を{作|つく}りました。
examples.en: I set aside practice time for the presentation.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}が{聞|き}き{取|と}れるように、{短|みじか}く{区切|くぎ}って{聞|き}きます。
examples.en: I listen in short sections so I can catch the explanation.

grammar.mistake: Nouns need の: 発表のために. Distinguish the goal 発表するために from the observed outcome 発表できるようになった.

glosses.meaning: a course; a series of lessons
part of the grammar patterns taught here

grammar: ようになる / ようにする
purpose ように / ために
watch.prompt: Optionally use your own short vlog. Save a line describing a change and a line describing a purpose. Mark whether each line reports an outcome or a goal; don’t infer fluency from a goal.

exercises.prompt: What improvement does Bao report?
exercises.explain: Bao reports 短い文はすらすら読めるようになりました, then says long explanations are still difficult.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao make a point of doing after practice?
options: Watching a course recording before practice
exercises.explain: 練習の後で、記録を見直すようにしています specifies both action and timing.

exercises.prompt: What is the next task?
exercises.explain: 次の課題は、方法を短く説明することです states the next task.

exercises.context: Report an observed new ability, not a wish or an ongoing effort.
exercises.line: {短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}をすらすら{読|よ}める＿＿。
exercises.explain: ようになりました reports the changed ability; the other endings state an effort or wish.

exercises.context: State a current conscious habit of checking records. Do not report when the habit started.
exercises.line: {記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}す＿＿。
exercises.explain: ようにしています marks ongoing effort. The context asks for that meaning.

exercises.context: Answer Satō-sensei politely: the new habit’s reviewing the method record. Do not change the topic.
exercises.line: {以前|いぜん}と{比|くら}べて、{何|なに}をするようになりましたか。
options: {方法|ほうほう}の{説明|せつめい}は{来週|らいしゅう}です。
{記録|きろく}は{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}です。
{方法|ほうほう}の{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}すようになりました。
exercises.explain: The first reply identifies the changed routine. The others give a date or location.

exercises.context: Tell the teacher politely that you try not to push yourself when tired.
exercises.line: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は、どうしていますか。
options: {無理|むり}をしないようにしています。
{無理|むり}をするようにしています。
{疲|つか}れるために{練習|れんしゅう}しています。
exercises.explain: The negative しない expresses the intended avoidance. The other replies contradict the specified plan.

exercises.meaning: I make a point of looking over the record after practice.
tiles: {練習|れんしゅう}の{後|あと}で、
exercises.explain: The nonpast clause 見直す precedes ようにしています; 練習の後で gives the timing.

exercises.prompt: Why should the writing be enlarged?
options: So people at the back can see it
exercises.explain: Satō-sensei explicitly says 後ろの人にも見えるように.

exercises.prompt: Why will Bao attend next week’s course?
options: To submit an already completed exam result
exercises.explain: 新しい方法を学ぶために gives a deliberate goal, not a result already achieved.

exercises.context: Practise the purpose construction for a deliberate action: attending a course to learn a method.
exercises.line: {新|あたら}しい{方法|ほうほう}を{学|まな}ぶ＿＿、{講座|こうざ}に{参加|さんか}します。
exercises.explain: Dictionary-form 学ぶ + ために names the goal. のに is a concession and までに a deadline.

exercises.context: Aim for an ability, not a completed result. Complete the sentence about audio adjustment.
exercises.line: {説明|せつめい}が{聞|き}き{取|と}れる＿＿、{音|おと}を{調整|ちょうせい}します。
exercises.explain: 聞き取れるように gives the desired ability. のに gives contrast and ようになった would report a completed change.

exercises.meaning: I’ll display the steps for the presentation.
exercises.explain: A noun purpose uses のために. Displaying the steps is the action serving it.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer prioritise this week?
exercises.explain: 今週は速さより正確さを優先する explicitly states the priority.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

exercises.prompt: Which pair correctly separates a result from a future plan?
options: Can now read short sentences smoothly; will attend a course next week
Will attend a course; already understands every long explanation
Can now read every text; will stop reviewing
exercises.explain: The first paragraph reports a limited achieved change. The final paragraph schedules the course.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

exercises.prompt: What will the writer do on a tired day?
exercises.explain: 疲れた日は休む states the action directly.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

お茶が冷めないうちに飲みます。
短い休憩を取ります。
作業の進行を記録します。
移動する前に連絡します。
作業の中断を記録します。
休憩のあとで作業を再開します。
計画を実行します。

words.meaning: passage of time; progress of events
words.example: 一週間の経過を記録します。
接続が切れた瞬間に気付きました。
練習の方法を切り替えます。
再開の時間は未定です。

lessons.title: Before, during, and just after
lessons.description: Hear the stages of a task in a phone call, without confusing a plan with completion.
lessons.canDo: Identify the current stage and give a fitting reply

lessons.title: Use the time while it lasts
lessons.description: Distinguish a useful window from a gradual change; read a diary with a stated sequence.
lessons.canDo: Find a time window, an action taken and a change that developed

grammar.title: Locate an action in three stages
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + ところだ/です: just about to act. ている + ところだ/です: in the middle of acting. た + ところだ/です: just finished. A following noun uses the nominal modifier, e.g. 作業しているところ; a cause clause uses ところなので.
grammar.explanation: A phone reply should state the actual stage, not merely say that the activity exists. Distinguish preparation from action and completion. These editorial-N4 forms are bridge instruction missing from the installed core. Discovery たところ and a near miss with ところだった are different extensions, not inferred here.
grammar.example: これから作業を始めるところです。
grammar.translation: I’m just about to start the task.

examples.ja: これから{作業|さぎょう}を{始|はじ}めるところです。
examples.en: I’m just about to start the task.

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{作業|さぎょう}をしているところです。
examples.en: I’m working on the task right now.

examples.ja: たった{今|いま}、{作業|さぎょう}が{終|お}わったところです。
examples.en: The task has just finished.

grammar.mistake: 始めるところ is not 始めたところ. Choose from the actual before/during/after context, not the English word “now” alone.

grammar.title: Recency from the speaker’s viewpoint
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + ばかりだ/です. Before a noun: たばかりの + noun. Before a cause clause: たばかりなので, not たばかりだので.
grammar.explanation: The speaker treats an event as recent relative to the situation. There is no fixed number of minutes or days. たところ normally highlights the immediately finished stage, whereas たばかり can describe a longer interval that still feels recent. Immediately after an action, both can fit; don’t force a choice between them without a stated form or decisive context.
grammar.example: 昨日、新しい練習を始めたばかりです。
grammar.translation: I only started the new practice yesterday.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}、{新|あたら}しい{練習|れんしゅう}を{始|はじ}めたばかりです。
examples.en: I only started the new practice yesterday.

examples.ja: {買|か}ったばかりの{本|ほん}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}きます。
examples.en: I’ll write my name in the book I just bought.

examples.ja: {帰宅|きたく}したばかりなので、まだ{片付|かたづ}けをしていません。
examples.en: I only just got home, so I haven’t tidied up yet.

grammar.mistake: Do not invent a rule that ばかり becomes wrong after a fixed interval. The reading context and the speaker’s viewpoint matter.

grammar.title: Act before a useful state changes
grammar.formation: Noun + のうちに; な-adjective + なうちに; い-adjective + うちに; suitable plain nonpast/ない/ている clause + うちに, followed by an action to take within that window.
grammar.explanation: A temporary state makes the action timely: the drink is still hot, someone is available, or the detail is not yet forgotten. The text must actually state a restriction before a question can infer a deadline. A request describes what to do; it’s not evidence that the action has already happened.
grammar.example: お茶が熱いうちに飲んでください。
grammar.translation: Please drink the tea while it’s hot.

examples.ja: お{茶|ちゃ}が{熱|あつ}いうちに{飲|の}んでください。
examples.en: Please drink the tea while it’s hot.

examples.ja: {今週|こんしゅう}のうちにメモを{見直|みなお}します。
examples.en: I’ll look over the notes before the week is over.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かなうちに{録画|ろくが}します。
examples.en: I’ll record the video while it’s quiet.

grammar.mistake: Nouns need の and な-adjectives need な: 今週のうちに、静かなうちに. 冷めないうちに means before the drink cools, not after it has cooled.

grammar.title: A change emerges during an activity
grammar.formation: An ongoing/repeated plain verb clause + うちに, followed by an emerging change, e.g. 話しているうちに or 練習するうちに.
grammar.explanation: Repeated or ongoing activity can lead to a change without stating an intended deadline. Compare a gradual realisation with the deliberate useful-window instruction. Here, becoming accustomed to the method is reported; it doesn’t mean every phrase has been mastered. The interval patterns 間 and 最中 receive a later contrast.
grammar.example: 同じ文を繰り返すうちに、発音に慣れてきました。
grammar.translation: As I repeated the same sentences, I began getting used to the pronunciation.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すうちに、{発音|はつおん}に{慣|な}れてきました。
examples.en: As I repeated the same sentences, I began getting used to the pronunciation.

examples.ja: {手順|てじゅん}を{説明|せつめい}しているうちに、{問題|もんだい}に{気付|きづ}きました。
examples.en: While explaining the steps, I noticed a problem.

examples.ja: {練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}けるうちに、{少|すこ}しずつ{上達|じょうたつ}しました。
examples.en: As I continued practicing, I improved little by little.

grammar.mistake: An emerging result such as 慣れてきた is not a command to act before a deadline. Read the whole sentence; don’t label every うちに as “before”.

dialogues.title: A phone call before meeting Ren
dialogues.scene: After the internship, Bao and Ren meet to discuss a practice record. Ren checks whether Bao can leave yet. The three stages are explicitly stated.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせは{駅|えき}で{五時|ごじ}だよね。{今|いま}、{何|なに}をしているの。
lines.romaji: Machiawase wa eki de goji da yo ne. Ima, nani o shite iru no?
lines.meaning: We are meeting at the station at five, right? What are you doing now?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: まだ{作業|さぎょう}をしているところだよ。{復習|ふくしゅう}の{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}している。
lines.romaji: Mada sagyō o shite iru tokoro da yo. Fukushū no kiroku o minaoshite iru.
lines.meaning: I’m still in the middle of the task. I’m reviewing the practice record.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {手順|てじゅん}のメモは、もう{保存|ほぞん}した。
lines.romaji: Tejun no memo wa, mō hozon shita?
lines.meaning: Have you saved the notes on the steps yet?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: まだだよ。これから{保存|ほぞん}するところだ。
lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Kore kara hozon suru tokoro da.
lines.meaning: Not yet. I’m just about to save them.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: じゃあ、{終|お}わったら{電話|でんわ}を{折|お}り{返|かえ}して。
lines.romaji: Jā, owattara denwa o orikaeshite.
lines.meaning: Then call me back when you finish.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{最近|さいきん}{始|はじ}めたばかりの{練習|れんしゅう}だから、まだ{時間|じかん}がかかる。
lines.romaji: Un. Saikin hajimeta bakari no renshū da kara, mada jikan ga kakaru.
lines.meaning: Okay. It’s practice I only started recently, so it still takes time.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {無理|むり}はしないで。{続|つづ}けることが{大切|たいせつ}だよ。
lines.romaji: Muri wa shinai de. Tsuzukeru koto ga taisetsu da yo.
lines.meaning: Do not push yourself. Keeping it up matters.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとう。あ、メモの{保存|ほぞん}が{終|お}わったところだ。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. A, memo no hozon ga owatta tokoro da.
lines.meaning: Thanks. Oh, the notes have just finished saving.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: これで{作業|さぎょう}は{終|お}わりだね。
lines.romaji: Kore de sagyō wa owari da ne.
lines.meaning: So that’s the end of the task, then.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{片付|かたづ}けをしてから{出|で}るよ。
lines.romaji: Un. Katazuke o shite kara deru yo.
lines.meaning: Yes. I’ll leave after tidying up.

dialogues.title: A short break at the café
dialogues.scene: Hana and Bao review a practice record during a break. Tea, a five-minute window and a reported gradual change must be distinguished.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: お{茶|ちゃ}を{入|い}れたよ。{熱|あつ}いうちに{飲|の}んでね。
lines.romaji: Ocha o ireta yo. Atsui uchi ni nonde ne.
lines.meaning: I made tea. Drink it while it’s hot.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとう。{冷|さ}めないうちに{飲|の}むよ。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. Samenai uchi ni nomu yo.
lines.meaning: Thanks. I’ll drink it before it cools.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {休憩|きゅうけい}はあと{五分|ごふん}だね。{今|いま}のうちにメモを{見直|みなお}そう。
lines.romaji: Kyūkei wa ato gofun da ne. Ima no uchi ni memo o minaosō.
lines.meaning: We have five minutes of break left. Let’s review the notes while we can.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{昨日|きのう}の{通話|つうわ}では、{説明|せつめい}の{途中|とちゅう}で{接続|せつぞく}が{切|き}れた。
lines.romaji: Un. Kinō no tsūwa de wa, setsumei no tochū de setsuzoku ga kireta.
lines.meaning: Yes. In yesterday’s call, the connection dropped during the explanation.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {大切|たいせつ}な{手順|てじゅん}は{聞|き}けた。
lines.romaji: Taisetsu na tejun wa kiketa?
lines.meaning: Did you manage to hear the important steps?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {最初|さいしょ}の{手順|てじゅん}だけ。だから、{今日|きょう}もう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}する。
lines.romaji: Saisho no tejun dake. Da kara, kyō mō ichido kakunin suru.
lines.meaning: Only the first step. So I’ll check again today.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {練習|れんしゅう}の{方|ほう}はどう。
lines.romaji: Renshū no hō wa dō?
lines.meaning: How is the practice going?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {文|ぶん}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すうちに、{徐々|じょじょ}に{発音|はつおん}に{慣|な}れてきた。
lines.romaji: Bun o kurikaesu uchi ni, jojo ni hatsuon ni narete kita.
lines.meaning: As I repeated the sentences, I gradually began getting used to the pronunciation.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: よかったね。でも、{無理|むり}はしないで。
lines.romaji: Yokatta ne. Demo, muri wa shinai de.
lines.meaning: That’s good. But don’t push yourself.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{今日|きょう}は{短|みじか}い{練習|れんしゅう}だけにする。
lines.romaji: Un. Kyō wa mijikai renshū dake ni suru.
lines.meaning: Okay. Today I’ll keep the practice short.

readings.title: Two calls and a short break
paragraphs: {金曜日|きんようび}は{五時|ごじ}にレンと{駅|えき}で{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせをした。{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た{時|とき}、まだ{復習|ふくしゅう}の{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}しているところだった。メモを{保存|ほぞん}するところだと{伝|つた}え、{保存|ほぞん}が{終|お}わってから{折|お}り{返|かえ}した。{片付|かたづ}けのあとで{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。

{土曜日|どようび}の{休憩|きゅうけい}に、ハナとメモを{確認|かくにん}した。{休憩|きゅうけい}はあと{五分|ごふん}だったので、{今|いま}のうちに{大切|たいせつ}な{手順|てじゅん}を{見直|みなお}した。お{茶|ちゃ}は{冷|さ}めないうちに{飲|の}んだ。{昨日|きのう}の{通話|つうわ}では{接続|せつぞく}が{切|き}れたので、{聞|き}けなかった{手順|てじゅん}をもう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}した。
{新|あたら}しい{練習|れんしゅう}は{先週|せんしゅう}{始|はじ}めたばかりだ。まだ{長|なが}い{文|ぶん}は{難|むずか}しいが、{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すうちに、{少|すこ}しずつ{発音|はつおん}に{慣|な}れてきた。{時間|じかん}がある{時|とき}でも、{疲|つか}れたら{休|やす}むようにしている。

grammar: る / ている / たところ
watch.prompt: Optionally save one line locating an action in a stage and one useful-window instruction from your own clip. Keep them distinct from a gradual change. This is observation, not a scored proficiency task.

exercises.prompt: What is Bao doing when Ren first calls?
exercises.explain: Bao says 作業をしているところ and specifies reviewing the record.

exercises.prompt: Have the notes already been saved at the first mention?
options: No; Bao is about to save them
exercises.explain: まだ and これから保存するところ state the not-yet-started stage.

exercises.prompt: What will Bao do before leaving?
exercises.explain: The final line explicitly says 片付けをしてから出る.

exercises.context: The work is underway right now. Use the three-stage ところ construction to tell Ren that you are in the middle of the task.
exercises.line: {今|いま}、{作業|さぎょう}を＿＿ところだよ。
exercises.explain: ている places the action in progress; the other forms put it before or after.

exercises.context: Form practice: modify the noun メモ with 保存したばかり. Choose the nominal connector, not a different time expression.
exercises.line: {保存|ほぞん}したばかり＿＿メモを{読|よ}みます。
exercises.explain: The attributive たばかりの modifies a noun.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Satō-sensei. The record is still being reviewed now; the task has not finished.
exercises.line: {作業|さぎょう}はもう{終|お}わりましたか。
options: はい、{作業|さぎょう}は{終|お}わったところです。
はい、{昨日|きのう}{終|お}わりました。
いいえ、{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}しているところです。
exercises.explain: The negative answer and ongoing stage match the stated context; the other replies report completion.

exercises.meaning: I’m just about to save the notes on the steps.
exercises.explain: Dictionary form 保存する + ところです gives the just-before stage.

exercises.prompt: What does Hana ask Bao to do with the tea?
exercises.explain: 熱いうちに explicitly identifies the useful hot state.

exercises.prompt: Why must Bao check the steps again?
options: The connection dropped during the explanation
exercises.explain: Bao heard only the first step because the connection dropped.

exercises.prompt: What change emerged as Bao repeated the sentences?
exercises.explain: 慣れてきた is a gradual reported change, not a claim of total mastery.

exercises.context: Form practice: review the break record before this week ends. Select the connector required after the noun 今週.
exercises.line: {今週|こんしゅう}＿＿うちに、{休憩|きゅうけい}の{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}します。
exercises.explain: A noun attaches with のうちに; な belongs with な-adjectives.

exercises.context: The tea is still hot. Express drinking before it cools, using 冷める with うちに.
exercises.line: お{茶|ちゃ}が＿＿うちに{飲|の}みます。
exercises.explain: 冷めないうちに gives the before-it-cools window. The past form is not the requested meaning.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Hana: agree to review the notes within the remaining break.
exercises.line: {休憩|きゅうけい}はあと{五分|ごふん}だね。{今|いま}のうちにメモを{見直|みなお}そう。
options: うん、{明日|あした}まで{何|なに}もしないよ。
うん、メモは{捨|す}てよう。
うん、{今|いま}{確認|かくにん}しよう。
exercises.explain: The first reply agrees to immediate review; the others delay or discard the notes.

exercises.meaning: As I repeated the sentences, I began getting used to the pronunciation.
tiles: {発音|はつおん}に{慣|な}れてきました。
exercises.explain: Repeated activity precedes うちに; the developing result follows it.

exercises.prompt: Which sequence matches Friday’s diary?
options: Save the notes → call Ren back → tidy up → leave home
Leave home → call back → save the notes
Meet Hana → buy tea → call Ren
exercises.explain: The diary states 保存が終わってから折り返した and 片付けのあとで家を出た.
exercises.context: Use the diary’s stated order, not a guessed routine.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer review the important steps during Saturday’s break?
options: The next day is a national holiday
Only five minutes of the break remain
exercises.explain: The text explicitly gives the remaining five-minute window. No holiday or exam is mentioned.
exercises.context: Read the diary before answering.

lessons.title: What you saw, and what you heard
lessons.description: Meet Misaki; separate a preview impression, a report and a checked fact.
lessons.canDo: Identify a claim’s source and what still needs checking

lessons.title: A likeness is not an identity
lessons.description: Distinguish a costume, a fictional role and an actual person; describe traits with care.
lessons.canDo: Read resemblance and selected trait expressions without overclaiming

grammar.title: An impression from what you notice
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + そうだ/です; い-adjective minus final い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう. いい → よさそう. Use そうな + noun and そうに + action. Negative attachments need separate instruction; this lesson scores positive forms only.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the earlier appearance pattern using visible or perceptible clues. It presents an impression or an impending event; it doesn’t certify a fact. Stem 降りそう differs from reported plain 降るそう. A preview can look interesting without you having seen the full film.
grammar.example: この短い映像は面白そうです。
grammar.translation: This short video looks interesting.

examples.ja: この{短|みじか}い{映像|えいぞう}は{面白|おもしろ}そうです。
examples.en: This short video looks interesting.

examples.ja: {空|そら}が{暗|くら}くなって、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうです。
examples.en: The sky has darkened, and it looks as though it will rain.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かそうな{部屋|へや}で{練習|れんしゅう}します。
examples.en: I’ll practice in a room that looks quiet.

grammar.mistake: 面白そう is an impression; 面白いそう is a report. Do not remove the final い when reporting someone’s statement.

grammar.title: State what was reported, and by whom
grammar.formation: Hearsay: a plain verb/い-adjective proposition + そうだ; noun/な-adjective + だそうだ. Inferential/hearsay らしい follows plain clauses or noun/な-adjective stems directly. Characteristic noun + らしい is a different use.
grammar.explanation: Give the source when repeating a claim. そうだ reports information, while らしい can convey an inference or what you have heard. They overlap; there is no rigid certainty ranking and neither proves the report true. This unit contrasts the earlier N4 hearsay note with explicit source checking. Editorial sources disagree on the level of reported そうだ.
grammar.example: ハナの話では、映画は来週始まるそうです。
grammar.translation: According to Hana, the film starts next week.

examples.ja: ハナの{話|はなし}では、{映画|えいが}は{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうです。
examples.en: According to Hana, the film starts next week.

examples.ja: {案内|あんない}では、{入場|にゅうじょう}は{無料|むりょう}だそうです。
examples.en: According to the notice, admission is free.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}は{評判|ひょうばん}がいいらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently the new shop has a good reputation.

grammar.mistake: A noun or な-adjective keeps だ before hearsay そう: 無料だそう. らしい attaches directly: 無料らしい. A form task may request one construction, but context doesn’t always exclude the other.

grammar.title: Explain an inference from clues
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + ようだ/です; noun + のようだ; な-adjective + なようだ. Use ような + noun or ように + action when modifying. Purpose ように and changed ability ようになる are different constructions.
grammar.explanation: State what you notice and what you infer from it. A note on the door or a quiet room is a clue, not an absolute guarantee. ようだ is more formal than conversational みたい. Do not infer someone’s identity, feelings or a performance result with certainty from appearance alone.
grammar.example: 部屋が静かなので、作業は終わったようです。
grammar.translation: The room is quiet, so it appears the task has finished.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}が{静|しず}かなので、{作業|さぎょう}は{終|お}わったようです。
examples.en: The room is quiet, so it appears the task has finished.

examples.ja: ここは{練習|れんしゅう}のための{教室|きょうしつ}のようです。
examples.en: This appears to be a classroom used for practice.

examples.ja: {表情|ひょうじょう}から、{緊張|きんちょう}しているようです。
examples.en: From the facial expression, the person appears to be nervous.

grammar.mistake: Nouns need の and な-adjectives need な before よう. An inference is not confirmation; check the record if the distinction matters.

grammar.title: A conversational likeness or inference
grammar.formation: Plain clauses or noun/な-adjective stems + みたいだ/です; みたいな + noun; みたいに + action. This grammatical みたい is not 見たい meaning “want to see”.
grammar.explanation: Friends often use みたい for a likeness or inference. ようだ can describe the same situation more formally, so don’t assume that one must always be wrong. Compare the noun attachments: 教室みたい and 教室のよう. A costume can resemble a profession without making its wearer a member of it.
grammar.example: この衣装は先生の服みたいです。
grammar.translation: This costume looks like a teacher’s clothes.

examples.ja: この{衣装|いしょう}は{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいです。
examples.en: This costume looks like a teacher’s clothes.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}みたいな{部屋|へや}で{撮影|さつえい}します。
examples.en: We’ll film in a room resembling a classroom.

examples.ja: {通話|つうわ}が{切|き}れたみたいです。
examples.en: It seems the call has dropped.

grammar.mistake: Do not add の before みたい after a noun. 教室みたいな部屋 is a likeness, not proof that the room is officially a classroom.

grammar.title: A perceived trait, not an identity
grammar.formation: Selected established noun/stem + っぽい forms become い-adjectives: っぽく, っぽかった, っぽくない. Examples here: 黒っぽい、忘れっぽい、大人っぽい. This suffix is not freely attachable to every verb or adjective.
grammar.explanation: Describe a perceived colour, manner or tendency with care. 黒っぽい can be nearly black without being exactly black. 忘れっぽい describes a tendency, not a diagnosis. Compare a resemblance with the typical/characteristic noun + らしい use; neither justifies a stereotype about a group.
grammar.example: 黒っぽい衣装を選びました。
grammar.translation: I chose a dark, almost-black costume.

examples.ja: {黒|くろ}っぽい{衣装|いしょう}を{選|えら}びました。
examples.en: I chose a dark, almost-black costume.

examples.ja: {忘|わす}れっぽいので、{台詞|せりふ}のメモを{使|つか}います。
examples.en: I tend to forget, so I use notes for my lines.

examples.ja: この{登場人物|とうじょうじんぶつ}は{大人|おとな}っぽい{話|はな}し{方|かた}をします。
examples.en: This character speaks in a mature-sounding way.

grammar.mistake: Conjugate the new adjective: 黒っぽくない, not 黒っぽいじゃない. Learn established combinations instead of inventing new ones from any verb.

dialogues.title: Misaki checks the film rumour
dialogues.scene: Kenta introduces his friend Misaki to Bao. They discuss a student film preview and separate an impression from a report. The screening date is not independently verified in this scene.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: バオ、こちらは{友達|ともだち}の{美咲|みさき}だよ。{映画|えいが}が{好|す}きなんだ。
lines.romaji: Bao, kochira wa tomodachi no Misaki da yo. Eiga ga suki nan da.
lines.meaning: Bao, this is my friend Misaki. She likes films.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {美咲|みさき}です。よろしくね。あの{録画|ろくが}した{映像|えいぞう}、{面白|おもしろ}そうだね。
lines.romaji: Misaki desu. Yoroshiku ne. Ano rokuga shita eizō, omoshirosō da ne.
lines.meaning: I’m Misaki. Nice to meet you. That recorded video looks interesting.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {短|みじか}い{紹介|しょうかい}だけ{見|み}たよ。{映画|えいが}{全部|ぜんぶ}は、まだ{見|み}ていない。
lines.romaji: Mijikai shōkai dake mita yo. Eiga zenbu wa, mada mite inai.
lines.meaning: I saw only the short introduction. I haven’t seen the whole film yet.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ハナの{話|はなし}では、{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうだよ。
lines.romaji: Hana no hanashi de wa, raishū hajimaru sō da yo.
lines.meaning: According to Hana, it starts next week.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: その{情報|じょうほう}は、{確認|かくにん}した？
lines.romaji: Sono jōhō wa, kakunin shita?
lines.meaning: Have you checked that information?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: まだだよ。{評判|ひょうばん}はいいらしいけど、{日|ひ}にちは{確|たし}かめたい。
lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Hyōban wa ii rashii kedo, hinichi wa tashikametai.
lines.meaning: Not yet. Apparently its reputation is good, but I want to check the date.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {通話|つうわ}が{終|お}わったら、ハナに{案内|あんない}を{送|おく}ってもらおう。
lines.romaji: Tsūwa ga owattara, Hana ni annai o okutte moraō.
lines.meaning: When the call finishes, let’s ask Hana to send the notice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{案内|あんない}を{保存|ほぞん}しとくよ。{日|ひ}にちが{決|き}まったら{教|おし}えて。
lines.romaji: Un. Annai o hozon shitoku yo. Hinichi ga kimattara oshiete.
lines.meaning: I’ll save the notice. Let me know when the date’s settled.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {評判|ひょうばん}がいいから、{早|はや}く{見|み}たいね。{噂|うわさ}では{続編|ぞくへん}もあるらしいよ。
lines.romaji: Hyōban ga ii kara, hayaku mitai ne. Uwasa de wa zokuhen mo aru rashii yo.
lines.meaning: It’s getting good reviews, so I can’t wait to see it. I hear there might be a sequel too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃ、ハナの{返事|へんじ}を{待|ま}とう。{来週|らいしゅう}なら{土曜日|どようび}が{空|あ}いてるよ。
lines.romaji: Ja, Hana no henji o matō. Raishū nara doyōbi ga aiteru yo.
lines.meaning: Let’s wait for Hana’s reply. I’m free next Saturday.

dialogues.title: Costume, role, and the person wearing it
dialogues.scene: Later, Misaki shares a student film rehearsal. Clothing, a fictional role and a performer’s self-described tendency are separate things.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: これが{撮影|さつえい}で{使|つか}う{衣装|いしょう}だよ。{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいでしょう。
lines.romaji: Kore ga satsuei de tsukau ishō da yo. Sensei no fuku mitai deshō.
lines.meaning: This is the costume for filming. It looks like a teacher’s clothes, does it not?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん、{黒|くろ}っぽいね。{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}なの？
lines.romaji: Un, kuroppoi ne. Sensei no yaku na no?
lines.meaning: Yes, it’s dark, almost black. Is it a teacher’s role?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: そうだよ。{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}は{初|はじ}めてだから、ちょっと{緊張|きんちょう}してる。
lines.romaji: Sō da yo. Sensei no yaku wa hajimete da kara, chotto kinchō shiteru.
lines.meaning: Yes. It’s my first time playing a teacher, so I’m a little nervous.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {衣装|いしょう}、{似合|にあ}ってるね。{台詞|せりふ}はもう{覚|おぼ}えた？
lines.romaji: Ishō, niatteru ne. Serifu wa mō oboeta?
lines.meaning: The costume suits you. Have you learnt your lines yet?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{台詞|せりふ}は{短|みじか}いけど、{私|わたし}は{忘|わす}れっぽいから、メモを{使|つか}う。
lines.romaji: Un. Serifu wa mijikai kedo, watashi wa wasureppoi kara, memo o tsukau.
lines.meaning: Yes. The lines are short, but I tend to forget, so I use notes.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {台詞|せりふ}を{区切|くぎ}って{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すといいよ。
lines.romaji: Serifu o kugitte kurikaesu to ii yo.
lines.meaning: It helps to divide the lines into sections and repeat them.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: その{工夫|くふう}、{試|ため}してみる。{練習|れんしゅう}も{録画|ろくが}しよう。
lines.romaji: Sono kufū, tameshite miru. Renshū mo rokuga shiyō.
lines.meaning: I’ll try that idea. Let’s record the practice too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: あとで{保存|ほぞん}して、{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}せるね。
lines.romaji: Ato de hozon shite, hanashikata o minaoseru ne.
lines.meaning: We can save it afterward and review how you speak.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {休憩|きゅうけい}も{取|と}ろう。お{茶|ちゃ}が{冷|さ}めないうちに{飲|の}みたい。
lines.romaji: Kyūkei mo torō. Ocha ga samenai uchi ni nomitai.
lines.meaning: Let’s take a break too. I want to drink the tea before it cools.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: いいね。{休憩|きゅうけい}の{後|あと}で、{最初|さいしょ}の{場面|ばめん}から{撮|と}ってみよう。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Kyūkei no ato de, saisho no bamen kara totte miyō.
lines.meaning: Good idea. After the break, let’s try filming from the first scene.

readings.title: A message separating impressions and facts
paragraphs: レンへ。{今日|きょう}、ケンタの{友達|ともだち}の{美咲|みさき}と{話|はな}した。{映画|えいが}の{短|みじか}い{紹介|しょうかい}を{見|み}て、{面白|おもしろ}そうだと{思|おも}った。でも、{全部|ぜんぶ}はまだ{見|み}ていない。ハナの{話|はなし}では{来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まるそうだが、{日|ひ}にちはまだ{確認|かくにん}していない。{案内|あんない}をもらってから{予定|よてい}を{決|き}める。

{美咲|みさき}は{学生|がくせい}の{映画|えいが}で{先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}をする。{衣装|いしょう}は{黒|くろ}っぽく、{先生|せんせい}の{服|ふく}みたいだ。でも、{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}ではない。{忘|わす}れっぽいので、{台詞|せりふ}のメモを{使|つか}うと{言|い}っていた。{短|みじか}く{区切|くぎ}って{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す{練習|れんしゅう}を{勧|すす}めた。{録画|ろくが}を{保存|ほぞん}して、あとで{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}す。{見|み}た{目|め}の{印象|いんしょう}と{事実|じじつ}は{分|わ}けて{考|かんが}えたい。

glosses.meaning: doing; part of a compound action

grammar: inference ようだ / らしい
みたい / selected っぽい
watch.prompt: Optionally save a line reporting someone else’s information and a line describing an impression from your own clip. Note the stated source or clue. This observes language, not the truth of the fictional claim or your proficiency.

exercises.prompt: How much of the film has Bao seen?
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says only the short introduction, not the whole film.

exercises.prompt: Who is named as the source for next week’s start?
exercises.explain: Misaki says ハナの話では before the reported information.

exercises.prompt: Has Misaki independently checked the date?
options: Yes; she already holds a ticket
The scene says the screening ended
Not yet; she wants to check it
exercises.explain: まだだよ and 日にちは確かめたい state the remaining check.

exercises.context: Form practice: give an impression from a preview with appearance そう. Use 面白い, not the reported-statement construction.
exercises.line: この{紹介|しょうかい}は＿＿そうです。
exercises.explain: Appearance そう follows the adjective stem. The full adjective would give a report.

exercises.context: Form practice: relay a notice that says admission is free using hearsay そう. Choose the noun predicate form.
exercises.line: {案内|あんない}では、{入場|にゅうじょう}は＿＿そうです。
exercises.explain: The hearsay proposition keeps the copula だ after 無料.

exercises.context: Form practice: use ようだ to say the room appears to be a classroom. Select the nominal connector.
exercises.line: ここは{教室|きょうしつ}＿＿ようです。
exercises.explain: A noun uses のよう; a な-adjective would use なよう.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: you have not checked the information yet and will check the notice before deciding.
exercises.line: その{情報|じょうほう}、もう{確認|かくにん}した？
options: まだだよ。{案内|あんない}を{確認|かくにん}してから{決|き}める。
うん、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{確認|かくにん}した。
うん、{映画|えいが}は{昨日|きのう}{終|お}わった。
exercises.explain: Only the first reply preserves the explicitly unconfirmed state.

exercises.meaning: According to Hana, the film starts next week.
tiles: {来週|らいしゅう}{始|はじ}まる
exercises.explain: The reported plain clause 始まる precedes そう; the source is named first.

exercises.prompt: Which role is Misaki rehearsing?
options: Bao’s actual teacher at the university
exercises.explain: Misaki says 先生の役は初めて: it’s her first time portraying a teacher.

exercises.prompt: Why does Misaki use notes?
options: She has already memorised every line
She says she tends to forget the lines
exercises.explain: She says 忘れっぽいからメモを使う; this is a self-described tendency.

exercises.prompt: What practice method does Bao suggest?
options: Divide the lines into sections and repeat them
Throw away the notes before rehearsal
exercises.explain: Bao suggests 区切って繰り返す.

exercises.context: Form practice: say the room resembles a classroom using みたいな + noun. Select what follows the noun 教室 directly.
exercises.line: {教室|きょうしつ}＿＿{部屋|へや}で{撮影|さつえい}します。
exercises.explain: みたい attaches directly to the noun, then な modifies 部屋.

exercises.context: Form practice: negate the established adjective 黒っぽい. The costume is not dark or almost black.
exercises.line: この{衣装|いしょう}は＿＿です。
exercises.explain: The い-adjective negative is っぽくない; these distractors test form explicitly.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: acknowledge the teacher as a fictional role, without claiming she is a real teacher.
exercises.line: {先生|せんせい}の{役|やく}だよ。{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}じゃない。
options: うん、{映画|えいが}の{役|やく}なんだね。
うん、{本物|ほんもの}の{先生|せんせい}なんだね。
うん、{映画|えいが}には{出|で}ないんだね。
exercises.explain: The first reply preserves the role/reality distinction; the others contradict it.

exercises.meaning: I chose a dark, almost-black costume for filming.
exercises.explain: The characteristic adjective modifies 衣装; the purpose clause recycles unit 1.

exercises.prompt: Which statement preserves the message’s status of the screening date?
options: Next week is reported, but the calendar date is not yet checked
exercises.explain: ハナの話では…そうだ is a report, followed by 日にちはまだ確認していない.
exercises.context: Use the message, not an assumption about a rumour.

exercises.prompt: What does the message say about Misaki?
options: She has become Bao’s actual teacher
She will attend an exam as a teacher
She will portray a teacher in a student film
exercises.explain: 先生の役をする is explicitly separated from 本物の先生ではない.
exercises.context: Read the second paragraph.

exercises.prompt: Which pair of actions is recommended and then planned?
options: Repeat short sections; save and review the recording
Confirm an exam score; buy a costume
exercises.explain: The writer recommends short repeated sections, then plans saving and reviewing the recording.
exercises.context: Read the second paragraph; separate the two actions.

映画の推理を楽しみます。
これは推測で、確認した事実ではありません。
結論の根拠を説明します。
予定が変わる可能性があります。
確信があっても、記録を確認します。
日にちの情報に疑いがあります。
二つの説明に矛盾があります。
メモと記録の時間が一致しています。
名前の不一致を調べます。
記憶だけで決めず、メモも見ます。
目撃した人の話を聞きます。
撮影の現場に行きます。
雨の後で足跡が残っています。
かばんの持ち主を探します。

words.meaning: keep a promise; protect; observe a rule
words.example: 返す時間を守ります。
約束を破りたくありません。
問題の解決を目指します。
調査の結果を記録します。
映画で探偵の役をします。
物語の犯人はまだ分かりません。
