lessons.title: Expectation, conviction and a checked fact
lessons.description: Use an old note as a basis, then test the confident guess against a record.
lessons.canDo: Separate a grounded expectation from independent confirmation

lessons.title: Explain the result; choose the responsible action
lessons.description: Explain a missing costume and discuss the team’s return responsibility.
lessons.canDo: Read explanatory conclusions and strong recommendations in context

grammar.title: An expectation with grounds
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + はずだ/です; noun + のはず; な-adjective + なはず. A negative or past proposition can precede はず. A past expectation is はずだった. This is expectation, not advice.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the N4 pattern already met at the dinner visit. Give the schedule or record supporting your expectation, and separate it from what you actually checked. はず and に違いない can overlap; neither is a measured probability.
grammar.example: 昨日のメモでは、衣装は教室にあるはずです。
grammar.translation: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in the classroom.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のメモでは、{衣装|いしょう}は{教室|きょうしつ}にあるはずです。
examples.en: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in the classroom.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{撮影|さつえい}の{日|ひ}のはずです。
examples.en: Today should be the filming day.

examples.ja: {録画|ろくが}は{保存|ほぞん}したはずですが、もう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I believe I saved the recording, but I’ll check again.

grammar.mistake: The expectation may be wrong. 行くはず is an expected action; 行くべき is a recommendation, not the same English “should”.

grammar.title: Read a conviction without treating it as proof
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause or noun/な-adjective stem + に違いない/に違いありません. No present copula だ before に. Past verb clauses keep past form. Do not substitute 違わない.
grammar.explanation: The speaker is strongly convinced. A character can still be mistaken; check the subsequent events rather than deciding the story’s facts from this form alone. Do not assign a numerical confidence score or use someone’s clothes as proof of identity.
grammar.example: このメモは美咲のものに違いありません。
grammar.translation: I’m certain this note belongs to Misaki.

examples.ja: このメモは{美咲|みさき}のものに{違|ちが}いありません。
examples.en: I’m certain this note belongs to Misaki.

examples.ja: {衣装|いしょう}を{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: They must have moved the costume to another room.

examples.ja: {美咲|みさき}は、{記憶|きおく}が{正|ただ}しいに{違|ちが}いないと{思|おも}っています。
examples.en: Misaki is convinced her recollection is correct.

grammar.mistake: 美咲のものに違いない attaches directly to the noun phrase. Strong conviction is not independent confirmation and can be disproved.

grammar.title: A fact now has an explanation
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause + わけだ/です; な-adjective + なわけ. Nominal のわけ/であるわけ and explicit というわけ occur. Wider negative わけ constructions are taught separately.
grammar.explanation: Use a newly supplied reason to make an observed situation understandable. This can translate as “so that explains why”. It’s not simply any prediction or a noun meaning reason. State the fact and its explanation; avoid claiming that はず can never fit the same broad context.
grammar.example: 衣装を別の部屋に移したんですね。ここにはないわけです。
grammar.translation: So the costume was moved to another room. That explains why it’s not here.

examples.ja: {衣装|いしょう}を{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したんですね。ここにはないわけです。
examples.en: So the costume was moved to another room. That explains why it’s not here.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}を{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しているんですね。{上手|じょうず}なわけです。
examples.en: So you practice your lines every day. That explains why you are good at them.

examples.ja: メモの{日|ひ}にちが{古|ふる}かったんですね。{予定|よてい}が{違|ちが}ったわけです。
examples.en: So the note had an old date. That explains why the plans differed.

grammar.mistake: Use the attributive connector な for a な-adjective. The explanatory conclusion needs the supplied reason; it doesn’t independently verify a rumour.

grammar.title: Recommend a responsible action
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + べきだ/です. するべき and すべき both occur. Past judgment: べきだった. Negative recommendation: べきではない. Formal noun/な-adjective + であるべき, い-adjective + くあるべき; this lesson scores verb forms.
grammar.explanation: State the shared task, speaker and listener. べき makes a strong judgment about the appropriate action, not a prediction. A team can say it should check its own records; a softer たほうがいい suggestion may suit a friend better. This is communication practice, not a legal rule.
grammar.example: 借りた衣装は、約束の時間までに返すべきです。
grammar.translation: We should return the borrowed costume by the agreed time.

examples.ja: {借|か}りた{衣装|いしょう}は、{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}までに{返|かえ}すべきです。
examples.en: We should return the borrowed costume by the agreed time.

examples.ja: {根拠|こんきょ}を{確認|かくにん}せずに、{人|ひと}を{犯人|はんにん}だと{断定|だんてい}すべきではありません。
examples.en: We should not label someone the culprit without checking the grounds.

examples.ja: {移|うつ}す{前|まえ}に、{記録|きろく}を{残|のこ}すべきでした。
examples.en: We should have left a record before moving it.

grammar.mistake: Past judgment is 残すべきだった, not 残したべき. べきではない says not to do something; it’s not an expectation that the action will not happen.

dialogues.title: An old note and a missing costume
dialogues.scene: Before filming, Misaki and Bao check a costume. An old note creates an expectation; a confident guess is checked, not treated as proof. Nobody is accused of stealing.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}のメモでは、{衣装|いしょう}はこの{教室|きょうしつ}にあるはずだよ。
lines.romaji: Kinō no memo de wa, ishō wa kono kyōshitsu ni aru hazu da yo.
lines.meaning: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in this classroom.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: でも、ここにはないね。メモは{保存|ほぞん}してある。{日|ひ}にちを{見直|みなお}そう。
lines.romaji: Demo, koko ni wa nai ne. Memo wa hozon shite aru. Hinichi o minaosō.
lines.meaning: But it’s not here. The note is saved. Let’s recheck its date.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。そう{思|おも}うけど、まだ{確認|かくにん}していない。
lines.romaji: Betsu no heya ni utsushita ni chigai nai. Sō omou kedo, mada kakunin shite inai.
lines.meaning: They must have moved it to another room. That’s what I think, but I haven’t checked yet.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {記憶|きおく}だけでは{分|わ}からないね。{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}は{誰|だれ}？
lines.romaji: Kioku dake de wa wakaranai ne. Mochinushi wa dare?
lines.meaning: Memory alone doesn’t settle it. Who owns it?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {大学|だいがく}のものだよ。{担当者|たんとうしゃ}に{聞|き}こう。
lines.romaji: Daigaku no mono da yo. Tantōsha ni kikō.
lines.meaning: It belongs to the university. Let’s ask the person in charge.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {今|いま}、{作業|さぎょう}が{終|お}わったところ。どうしたの？
lines.romaji: Ima, sagyō ga owatta tokoro. Dō shita no?
lines.meaning: I have just finished the work. What is the matter?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {衣装|いしょう}がないんだ。{手掛|てが}かりになる{情報|じょうほう}はある？
lines.romaji: Ishō ga nai n da. Tegakari ni naru jōhō wa aru?
lines.meaning: The costume is missing. Do you have any information that could be a clue?

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {午前|ごぜん}に{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}へ{運|はこ}んだよ。{担当者|たんとうしゃ}にも{伝|つた}えた。
lines.romaji: Gozen ni betsu no heya e hakonda yo. Tantōsha ni mo tsutaeta.
lines.meaning: I carried it to another room this morning. I told the person in charge too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: あ、そうだったんだ。{古|ふる}いメモのままだったね。{新|あたら}しい{場所|ばしょ}を{書|か}いとこう。
lines.romaji: A, sō datta n da. Furui memo no mama datta ne. Atarashii basho o kaitokō.
lines.meaning: Oh, that’s what happened. The note was still out of date. Let’s write down the new location.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{見|み}つかってよかった。じゃ、{撮影|さつえい}に{戻|もど}ろう。
lines.romaji: Un. Mitsukatte yokatta. Ja, satsuei ni modorō.
lines.meaning: I’m glad we found it. Let’s get back to filming.

dialogues.title: Why it was missing, and what to do next
dialogues.scene: The team confirms the movement record. Satō-sensei discusses returning a borrowed costume and checking records responsibly. The detective role is fictional.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {先生|せんせい}、{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}しました。{衣装|いしょう}は{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}にありました。
lines.romaji: Sensei, kiroku o kakunin shimashita. Ishō wa betsu no heya ni arimashita.
lines.meaning: Teacher, we checked the record. The costume was in another room.

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: {午前|ごぜん}に{移|うつ}したんですね。もとの{教室|きょうしつ}にはないわけです。
lines.romaji: Gozen ni utsushita n desu ne. Moto no kyōshitsu ni wa nai wake desu.
lines.meaning: So it was moved this morning. That explains why it was not in the original classroom.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {古|ふる}いメモだけを{見|み}ていました。{新|あたら}しい{日|ひ}にちを{見落|みお}としました。
lines.romaji: Furui memo dake o mite imashita. Atarashii hinichi o miotoshimashita.
lines.meaning: I was looking only at the old note. I overlooked the new date.

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: {借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}す{責任|せきにん}は{私|わたし}たちにあります。{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきです。
lines.romaji: Karita mono o kaesu sekinin wa watashitachi ni arimasu. Yakusoku no jikan o mamoru beki desu.
lines.meaning: We are responsible for returning what we borrowed. We should keep the agreed time.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {返|かえ}すのは{五時|ごじ}ですね。{撮影|さつえい}が{終|お}わったら、{持|も}っていきます。
lines.romaji: Kaesu no wa goji desu ne. Satsuei ga owattara, motte ikimasu.
lines.meaning: The return time is five, right? We’ll take it back when filming finishes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今日|きょう}は{探偵|たんてい}の{役|やく}も{練習|れんしゅう}します。この{台詞|せりふ}、{少|すこ}し{変|か}えてもいいですか？
lines.romaji: Kyō wa tantei no yaku mo renshū shimasu. Kono serifu, sukoshi kaete mo ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: I’m rehearsing the detective’s role today too. Could I change this line a little?

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: いいですよ。ただ、{犯人|はんにん}が{分|わ}かる{台詞|せりふ}は、{最後|さいご}まで{言|い}うべきではありません。
lines.romaji: Ii desu yo. Tada, hannin ga wakaru serifu wa, saigo made iu beki de wa arimasen.
lines.meaning: Of course. But you shouldn’t reveal who the culprit’s until the end.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。じゃあ、その{台詞|せりふ}は{最後|さいご}の{場面|ばめん}に{残|のこ}します。
lines.romaji: Hai. Jā, sono serifu wa saigo no bamen ni nokoshimasu.
lines.meaning: Okay. I’ll keep that line for the final scene.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {練習|れんしゅう}を{録画|ろくが}して{保存|ほぞん}します。{後|あと}で{見|み}てもらえますか？
lines.romaji: Renshū o rokuga shite hozon shimasu. Ato de mite moraemasu ka?
lines.meaning: I’ll record and save the rehearsal. Could you watch it afterward?

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: {移|うつ}す{前|まえ}に、メモを{更新|こうしん}すべきでしたね。{次|つぎ}は{一緒|いっしょ}に{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
lines.romaji: Utsusu mae ni, memo o kōshin subeki deshita ne. Tsugi wa issho ni kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: We should have updated the note before moving it. Let’s check it together next time.

readings.title: From an expectation to a checked record
paragraphs: {撮影|さつえい}の{前|まえ}、{衣装|いしょう}がもとの{教室|きょうしつ}になかった。{昨日|きのう}のメモでは、そこにあるはずだった。{美咲|みさき}は{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いないと{言|い}ったが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していなかった。ケンタに{聞|き}くと、{午前|ごぜん}に{運|はこ}んだと{分|わ}かった。{記録|きろく}も{確認|かくにん}し、{衣装|いしょう}を{見|み}つけた。もとの{部屋|へや}にはないわけだ。

{大学|だいがく}から{借|か}りた{衣装|いしょう}は{五時|ごじ}までに{返|かえ}す。{先生|せんせい}は、{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきだと{言|い}った。{新|あたら}しいメモを{見落|みお}としたので、{次|つぎ}は{日|ひ}にちも{慎重|しんちょう}に{確認|かくにん}したい。{探偵|たんてい}の{役|やく}の{台詞|せりふ}も、{根拠|こんきょ}を{考|かんが}えて{練習|れんしゅう}する。{推測|すいそく}と{事実|じじつ}を{分|わ}け、{録画|ろくが}を{保存|ほぞん}して{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}す。

watch.prompt: Optionally save one expectation and one recommendation from your own clip. Note what is confirmed in the story and what the speaker only believes. This observes usage, not an exam result.

exercises.prompt: What supports Misaki’s initial expectation?
options: A new confirmation from the owner
exercises.explain: The first line names yesterday’s note; the costume is absent when they check.

exercises.prompt: Before asking Kenta, has Misaki confirmed that it moved?
options: Yes; she has inspected the movement record
No; she says she has not checked
Yes; she is holding the costume
exercises.explain: Her confident に違いない is followed by まだ確認していない.

exercises.prompt: Who owns the costume?
exercises.explain: Misaki explicitly answers 大学のもの.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta report doing?
options: Carrying it to another room in the morning
Destroying the old note at night
Returning it to Misaki last week
exercises.explain: Kenta gives the action, destination and morning time.

exercises.context: Form practice: give an expectation with the noun 撮影の日 + はず. Choose the nominal connector.
exercises.line: {今日|きょう}は{撮影|さつえい}の{日|ひ}＿＿はずです。
exercises.explain: A noun takes の before はず. This expectation doesn’t confirm that filming has started.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the expressly requested に違いない construction after the noun phrase 美咲のもの.
exercises.line: このメモは{美咲|みさき}のもの＿＿{違|ちが}いない。
exercises.explain: The noun phrase connects directly with に; no present copula だ is inserted.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: acknowledge the guess but say you still need to check the record.
exercises.line: {別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。
options: そうかもしれないね。まず{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}しよう。
うん、もう{記録|きろく}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{確認|かくにん}したよ。
うん、{衣装|いしょう}は{昨日|きのう}{返|かえ}したよ。
exercises.explain: Only the first keeps the check pending; the others invent completed actions.

exercises.meaning: We’ll reach a conclusion after checking the facts.
exercises.explain: The check precedes the conclusion; してから marks the sequence.

exercises.prompt: What explains the costume’s absence from the original classroom?
options: It was moved to another room that morning
It had already been returned at five
exercises.explain: The first two lines confirm the movement record and give the explanation.

exercises.prompt: What return time does Bao confirm?
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says 五時; filming finishing is the planned trigger for taking it back.

exercises.prompt: What does Satō say the team should have done before moving it?
exercises.explain: The final line states 更新すべきでした and then a plan to check together next time.

exercises.context: Form practice: explain an observed skill with the な-adjective 上手 + わけ. Choose its attributive connector.
exercises.line: {毎日|まいにち}{台詞|せりふ}を{練習|れんしゅう}しているんですね。{上手|じょうず}＿＿わけです。
exercises.explain: A な-adjective takes な before わけ. This task practices the named form, not a unique synonym choice.

exercises.context: Form practice: say the team should have kept the agreed time. Put past judgment on べき, not on the verb.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を＿＿べきでした。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 守る precedes べき; でした places the judgment in the past.

exercises.context: Reply politely to your teacher: accept the five-o’clock return responsibility and say what you will do after filming.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきです。
options: はい。{撮影|さつえい}が{終|お}わったら、{五時|ごじ}までに{返|かえ}します。
はい。{明日|あした}まで{借|か}りることにしました。
はい。もう{衣装|いしょう}を{捨|す}てました。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the agreed deadline and a pending return.

exercises.meaning: We should not label someone the culprit without checking the grounds.
tiles: {根拠|こんきょ}を{確認|かくにん}せずに、
{人|ひと}を{犯人|はんにん}だと
exercises.explain: The negative judgment belongs after べき. This is advice, not a prediction of an action.

exercises.prompt: Which sequence matches the diary?
options: Record check → loss at midnight → exam result
Old note → unconfirmed guess → Kenta’s account → record check and finding the costume
Confirmed return at five → throwing away the note → filming last week
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly gives these four stages.
exercises.context: Read the event sequence.

exercises.prompt: What commitment does the diary make?
options: Return the costume only after an exam
Return the university costume by five
exercises.explain: 大学から借りた衣装は五時までに返す states ownership and deadline.
exercises.context: Use the second paragraph.

exercises.prompt: What will the writer check more carefully next time?
options: Whether Misaki is an actual detective
exercises.explain: 新しいメモを見落としたので、次は日にちも慎重に確認したい states the change.
exercises.context: Read the planned change; don’t infer a professional identity from a role.

lessons.title: Topic, target and two viewpoints
lessons.description: Hear why Bao reads first and Kenta listens first; respond to both.
lessons.canDo: Identify the topic and target of an opinion without inventing consensus

lessons.title: A survey has a scope
lessons.description: Separate shared requests, preferences and a pending screen comparison.
lessons.canDo: Read a viewpoint and what a result depends on

grammar.title: Name the topic of a discussion
grammar.formation: Noun/noun phrase + について + verb. Noun + についての + noun. Nominalise an action with こと/の when needed; no direct dictionary verb + について.
grammar.explanation: State what you discuss, ask about or research. A topic is not the same thing as the standpoint from which somebody evaluates it. Earlier notices exposed について with support; this note teaches its attachments explicitly.
grammar.example: 字幕について感想を話します。
grammar.translation: We’ll share our impressions about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}について{感想|かんそう}を{話|はな}します。
examples.en: We’ll share our impressions about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}についてのメモを{読み返|よみかえ}します。
examples.en: We’ll reread the note about the subtitles.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むことについて{話|はな}します。
examples.en: We’ll discuss reading the lines.

grammar.mistake: Do not attach it straight to 読む: make the action a noun phrase, 読むことについて. About the subtitles doesn’t mean from the subtitles’ viewpoint.

grammar.title: A response has a target; a contrast has two sides
grammar.formation: Target noun + に対して; target noun + に対する + noun. For contrast: plain verb/い-adjective clause + のに対して; な-adjective/noun + なのに対して (noun であるの also occurs).
grammar.explanation: Mark who or what receives a reaction. This need not be hostility: a considerate response has a target too. A separate contrast use compares two stated sides; read what is compared rather than assuming opposition.
grammar.example: 質問に対して、理由を説明します。
grammar.translation: We’ll explain the reason in response to the question.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}に{対|たい}して、{理由|りゆう}を{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.en: We’ll explain the reason in response to the question.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}に{対|たい}する{評価|ひょうか}をメモします。
examples.en: We’ll note the assessment of the subtitles.

examples.ja: ケンタは{先|さき}に{聞|き}くのに{対|たい}して、バオは{先|さき}に{読|よ}みます。
examples.en: Whereas Kenta listens first, Bao reads first.

grammar.mistake: When directly modifying the noun 評価, use に対する評価, not に対して評価. A contrasting clause needs nominalising の; don’t add の to every ordinary target noun.

grammar.title: Evaluate from a stated viewpoint
grammar.formation: Standpoint noun + にとって (は/も) + evaluation. Usually written in kana. Used for a person/group’s standpoint, not every beneficiary or purpose.
grammar.explanation: Name whose priorities make something useful, difficult or valuable. Several people can legitimately evaluate the same subtitles differently. This marks a judgment’s perspective, not the topic of discussion or an action’s recipient.
grammar.example: バオにとって、字幕は読む練習になります。
grammar.translation: For Bao, the subtitles provide reading practice.

examples.ja: バオにとって、{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になります。
examples.en: For Bao, the subtitles provide reading practice.

examples.ja: ケンタにとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.en: For Kenta, time to listen first is important too.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めて{見|み}る{人|ひと}にとって、このメモは{役|やく}に{立|た}ちます。
examples.en: For first-time viewers, this note is useful.

grammar.mistake: Do not use にとって as a general “for”: giving a note to somebody uses a recipient construction. 私について話す discusses me; 私にとって大切 evaluates something from my standpoint.

grammar.title: Read what によって connects
grammar.formation: Noun + によって/により + clause; noun + による + noun. Noun + による at the end can mean depend on. Context distinguishes variation, method, cause and a passive agent.
grammar.explanation: A changing condition can produce different outcomes. A survey can be the method for finding something, a named event can cause a result, or a creator can be the agent of a passive verb. により is common in formal writing. These are related uses, not one interchangeable English translation; reporting によると is separate.
grammar.example: 字幕の読みやすさは画面によって変わります。
grammar.translation: How easy the subtitles are to read varies with the screen.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}の{読|よ}みやすさは{画面|がめん}によって{変|か}わります。
examples.en: How easy the subtitles are to read varies with the screen.

examples.ja: アンケートによって、{三人|さんにん}の{要望|ようぼう}が{分|わ}かりました。
examples.en: Through the questionnaire, we learned the three people’s requests.

examples.ja: {大雨|おおあめ}による{予定|よてい}の{変更|へんこう}を{確認|かくにん}しました。
examples.en: We checked the schedule change caused by heavy rain.

examples.ja: この{台詞|せりふ}は{作者|さくしゃ}によって{書|か}かれました。
examples.en: This line was written by the author.

grammar.mistake: Before a noun, use による変更, not によって変更. Do not turn every ordinary tool expression with で into によって, or confuse a condition with a reporting source によると.

dialogues.title: The same subtitles, two priorities
dialogues.scene: After the student-film rehearsal, Bao and Kenta compare how they use Japanese subtitles. Misaki asks them to state viewpoints and check conditions; nobody claims a survey of all learners.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {字幕|じまく}について、{今日|きょう}の{感想|かんそう}を{聞|き}かせて。
lines.romaji: Jimaku ni tsuite, kyō no kansō o kikasete.
lines.meaning: Tell me your impressions today about the subtitles.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {私|わたし}にとって、{日本語|にほんご}の{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になる。{台詞|せりふ}を{目|め}で{追|お}いたいんだ。
lines.romaji: Watashi ni totte, Nihongo no jimaku wa yomu renshū ni naru. Serifu o me de oitai n da.
lines.meaning: For me, Japanese subtitles give reading practice. I want to follow the lines with my eyes.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {俺|おれ}にとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}だよ。{最初|さいしょ}は{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}したい。
lines.romaji: Ore ni totte wa, saki ni kiku jikan mo taisetsu da yo. Saisho wa jimaku o keshitai.
lines.meaning: For me, time to listen first is important too. At first I want to turn the subtitles off.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: じゃ、{一回|いっかい}{字幕|じまく}なしで{見|み}て、その{後|あと}で{出|だ}すのはどう？
lines.romaji: Ja, ikkai jimaku nashi de mite, sono ato de dasu no wa dō?
lines.meaning: How about watching once without subtitles, then turning them on?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃあ、{字幕|じまく}を{出|だ}すか{消|け}すか、{選|えら}べるといいね。
lines.romaji: Jā, jimaku o dasu ka kesu ka, eraberu to ii ne.
lines.meaning: Then it would be good to let people choose whether to display or hide them.

lines.speaker: Kenta

dialogues.title: What three responses actually tell us
dialogues.scene: Later the three collaborators fill in a short questionnaire and discuss a subtitle policy. The votes apply to this team, not the public. A separate check of screen readability is still pending.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {他|ほか}の{人|ひと}にも{聞|き}いてみたいね。{来週|らいしゅう}の{会|かい}で{頼|たの}んでみようかな。

readings.title: Three opinions are not everybody’s opinion
paragraphs: {日本語|にほんご}の{字幕|じまく}について、{三人|さんにん}で{話|はな}した。{私|わたし}にとって、{字幕|じまく}は{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になる。ケンタにとっては、{先|さき}に{聞|き}く{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}だ。{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}には、{三人|さんにん}とも{賛成|さんせい}した。{共通|きょうつう}の{要望|ようぼう}があっても、{個人|こじん}の{好|この}みは{違|ちが}う。

アンケートの{対象|たいしょう}は{私|わたし}たちだけだ。この{結果|けっか}を{全|すべ}ての{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}だと{断定|だんてい}すべきではない。{美咲|みさき}は、{要望|ようぼう}に{対|たい}して{画面|がめん}を{確認|かくにん}したいと{言|い}った。{読|よ}みやすさは{画面|がめん}によって{変|か}わる。{次|つぎ}は{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}で{比較|ひかく}し、{結果|けっか}と{根拠|こんきょ}を{記録|きろく}する。{支持|しじ}の{数|かず}も、{理由|りゆう}も{大切|たいせつ}にしたい。

watch.prompt: Optionally save an opinion from your own clip. Name its topic, whose viewpoint it states, and any conditions. Do not equate a character’s preference with every listener’s opinion.

recycling.reason: Friends choose a subtitle setting; evidence and survey-scope lectures were removed instead of padding the conversation.

exercises.prompt: Why does Bao want Japanese subtitles?
options: To practice reading and follow the lines visually
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly connects subtitles with reading practice and following the lines.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta want to do at first?
options: Hide the subtitles and listen first
exercises.explain: Kenta says 最初は字幕を消したい after explaining his listening priority.

exercises.prompt: Which proposal does Kenta support?
options: Force every viewer to hide subtitles
Claim all generations have the same preferences
Let viewers choose whether subtitles display
exercises.explain: Kenta’s それには賛成 refers to the immediately preceding selectable-subtitles proposal.

exercises.context: Form practice: modify メモ with the explicitly requested 字幕についての construction.
exercises.line: {字幕|じまく}について＿＿メモを{読み返|よみかえ}します。
exercises.explain: についての modifies a following noun; this is an attachment task.

exercises.context: Form practice: use に対する directly before the noun 評価. Choose the requested attributive form.
exercises.line: {字幕|じまく}に＿＿{評価|ひょうか}をメモします。
exercises.explain: に対する modifies 評価 directly; に対して would require a different sentence structure.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta: acknowledge his wish to listen first and support a choice of displaying or hiding subtitles.
exercises.line: {最初|さいしょ}は{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}したい。
options: うん。みんな{必|かなら}ず{先|さき}に{読|よ}むべきだね。
うん。もう{全国|ぜんこく}の{人|ひと}に{聞|き}いたよ。
うん。{出|だ}すか{消|け}すか、{選|えら}べるといいね。
exercises.explain: Only the first acknowledges a choice. The others impose one method or invent an unperformed survey.

exercises.meaning: Please tell me your impressions about the subtitles.
exercises.explain: について marks the topic; 感想 is the object of the request.

exercises.prompt: Who was surveyed?
exercises.explain: The first line explicitly limits the target to 私たち三人だけ.

exercises.prompt: Which action is still pending after the voting?
options: Checking readability on the different screens
Agreeing whether viewers may choose subtitles
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says the screen comparison check is not completed.

exercises.context: Form practice: give Bao’s evaluation from Bao’s standpoint using the named にとって pattern.
exercises.line: バオ＿＿、{字幕|じまく}は{読|よ}む{練習|れんしゅう}になります。
exercises.explain: The standpoint noun connects with にとって. This is not a topic or recipient question.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the cause modifier 大雨による directly before 変更.
exercises.line: {大雨|おおあめ}に＿＿{予定|よてい}の{変更|へんこう}を{確認|かくにん}しました。
exercises.explain: による modifies the following noun phrase. によって/により normally connects to a clause here.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Misaki: recognise that the result covers only this team and refuse to claim it represents everyone.
exercises.line: アンケートによると、{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べる{案|あん}が{人気|にんき}だったよ。{答|こた}えたのは、{私|わたし}たち{三人|さんにん}だけだけどね。
options: はい。{全国|ぜんこく}の{全員|ぜんいん}が{賛成|さんせい}しています。
はい。{全|すべ}ての{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}だとは{断定|だんてい}しません。
はい。{画面|がめん}の{確認|かくにん}も{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わりました。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the stated scope; neither a public consensus nor a completed screen check has been established.

exercises.meaning: Through the questionnaire, we learned the three people’s requests.
exercises.explain: The questionnaire is the method; the requests are what became known.

exercises.prompt: What do all three agree on?
options: Listening and reading in exactly the same order
exercises.explain: 字幕を選べる案には、三人とも賛成した states their shared request.
exercises.context: Find the shared proposal, not a preference that differs.

exercises.prompt: Which claim does the writer reject?
options: That this result represents everybody’s opinion
That the survey was for three collaborators
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly warns against treating the limited result as everyone’s views.
exercises.context: Read the limit on what can be concluded.

exercises.prompt: What will the team do next?
options: Replace the writer without reading any responses
Compare under the same conditions and record results with grounds
Claim the screen comparison has already finished
exercises.explain: 次は同じ条件で比較し、結果と根拠を記録する states the pending action.
exercises.context: Read the planned comparison.

lessons.title: An arrangement and a personal choice
lessons.description: Read what was agreed at the café, and what Bao chose to check tonight.
lessons.canDo: Separate a decision from its pending execution

lessons.title: No need, and requested advice
lessons.description: Hear why a duplicate call is unnecessary, then divide the remaining work.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish reassurance from prohibition and firm advice

grammar.title: A decision is not its completed action
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことにする. ことにした/しました reports a decision. ことにしている describes a chosen continuing practice.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the decision/routine taught in N4 units 11/12. State who chooses and whether execution is pending. A decision made yesterday can concern work tonight; a past した doesn’t prove that work is finished.
grammar.example: 今夜、字幕を確認することにしました。
grammar.translation: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.

examples.ja: {今夜|こんや}、{字幕|じまく}を{確認|かくにん}することにしました。
examples.en: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.

examples.ja: {記憶|きおく}だけに{頼|たよ}らないことにしました。
examples.en: I decided not to rely only on memory.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}の{後|あと}でメモを{見直|みなお}すことにしています。
examples.en: I make a practice of reviewing the note after meetings.

grammar.mistake: 行かないことにする decides not to go. 行くことにしない negates deciding to go and is not automatically the same decision. Do not mark a planned check as completed.

grammar.title: Report the arrangement and its grounds
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことになる. ことになった/なりました reports a decided arrangement or result; it can still be future. Attributive adjective + ことになる can express a resulting situation rather than an enacted decision.
grammar.explanation: Present what the discussion or circumstances have led to. Give the stated source of the arrangement: here the café team and the manager’s permission. ことになる can also indirectly present the speaker’s own choice, so identify the actor from the scene rather than treating it as a grammar-only external-agency rule.
grammar.example: 会議で、土曜日に映画を見ることになりました。
grammar.translation: At the meeting, it was agreed that we would watch the film on Saturday.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}で、{土曜日|どようび}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ることになりました。
examples.en: At the meeting, it was agreed that we would watch the film on Saturday.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{店|みせ}を{使|つか}わないことになりました。
examples.en: It has been arranged that we’ll not use the café tomorrow.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}が{変|か}わって、{私|わたし}が{確認|かくにん}することになりました。
examples.en: After the assignment changed, it was arranged that I would do the check.

grammar.mistake: Both ことにする and ことになる can fit some real decisions. Do not score a context-free choice between them. A rule expressed by ことになっている needs its own established-rule context.

grammar.title: No need is not a prohibition
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + ことはない/ありません. With reassuring context, no need to act. In other contexts, an event doesn’t occur. Past experience たことがない is a different pattern.
grammar.explanation: Use the stated situation to decide what is unnecessary. Bao has already received the requested message, so a duplicate call is not needed. The construction doesn’t ban calls or prove that an action has never happened. Keep the grounds for reassurance explicit.
grammar.example: 連絡はもう届きました。同じ内容で電話することはありません。
grammar.translation: The message has arrived. There is no need to phone with the same information.

examples.ja: {連絡|れんらく}はもう{届|とど}きました。{同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはありません。
examples.en: The message has arrived. There is no need to phone with the same information.

examples.ja: {期限|きげん}は{明日|あした}です。{今|いま}、{焦|あせ}ることはありません。
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow. There is no need to rush anxiously now.

examples.ja: この{週|しゅう}の{会議|かいぎ}は{店|みせ}で{開|ひら}きます。{大学|だいがく}で{会|あ}うことはありません。
examples.en: This week’s meeting is held at the café. We’ll not be meeting at the university.

grammar.mistake: Dictionary + ことはない here is not past + ことがない (“have never”). No need to call is not “you must not call”; context can instead describe no occasions of meeting.

grammar.title: Recognise firm advice from a requested mentor
grammar.formation: Dictionary or ない verb + ことだ/です for advisory use. The speaker takes an authoritative stance. Not every clause + ことです is advice; it may simply identify an action.
grammar.explanation: After Bao asks how to handle the work, the manager can advise dividing tasks and not taking everything on alone. This is firmer than a casual suggestion. Recognise it in the stated relationship; don’t turn it into a general request directed at a supervisor. Publisher level tags disagree N3/N2, so later advice practice retrieves it.
grammar.example: 一人で全部引き受けないことです。
grammar.translation: You should not take everything on alone.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないことです。
examples.en: You should not take everything on alone.

examples.ja: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。
examples.en: First, you should divide the work.

examples.ja: {理由|りゆう}が{分|わ}からないときは、{確認|かくにん}することです。
examples.en: When you don’t understand the reason, you should check.

grammar.mistake: Negative advice uses verb ない + ことです, not dictionary + ことではありません. For a polite request to a manager, use a request form rather than ordering them with ことだ.

dialogues.title: A café plan and Bao’s choice
dialogues.scene: Bao, Kenta and their host Yamamoto meet at the café about showing their student film. A permitted Saturday arrangement is separate from Bao’s future subtitle check. Kenta’s registration work is not yet done.

lines.meaning: Today’s agenda item is the film gathering at the café. Permission has been obtained.

lines.romaji: Jimaku no hōshin wa, miru hito ga eraberu yō ni suru koto desu ne.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {俺|おれ}は{申|もう}し{込|こ}みの{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}する。{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}だね。

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}です。{困|こま}ったら{早|はや}めに{相談|そうだん}してください。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kigen wa kin’yōbi desu. Komattara hayame ni sōdan shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: That’s right; the deadline’s Friday. Let me know early if you run into trouble.

dialogues.title: A duplicate call and shared work
dialogues.scene: The next morning Bao has completed the subtitle comparison. A reply from the organizer already confirms the deadline. Bao asks for procedural advice, and Yamamoto recommends sharing the remaining work.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {昨夜|さくや}、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}で{字幕|じまく}を{比較|ひかく}しました。{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}でも、{小|ちい}さい{方|ほう}は{読|よ}みにくかったです。
lines.romaji: Sakuya, futatsu no gamen de jimaku o hikaku shimashita. Onaji jōken de mo, chiisai hō wa yominikukatta desu.
lines.meaning: Last night I compared subtitles on two screens. Even under the same conditions, the smaller one was hard to read.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: ありがとう。じゃ、{大|おお}きい{方|ほう}を{使|つか}いましょう。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. Ja, ōkii hō o tsukaimashō.
lines.meaning: Thanks. Let’s use the bigger one, then.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {店長|てんちょう}に{期限|きげん}を{確認|かくにん}するメールを{送|おく}りました。{返事|へんじ}はもう{届|とど}きました。
lines.romaji: Tenchō ni kigen o kakunin suru mēru o okurimashita. Henji wa mō todokimashita.
lines.meaning: I emailed the manager to confirm the deadline. The reply has already arrived.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはありません。{返事|へんじ}を{保存|ほぞん}してください。
lines.romaji: Onaji naiyō de denwa suru koto wa arimasen. Henji o hozon shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: There is no need to phone with the same information. Please save the reply.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。{準備|じゅんび}が{多|おお}いので、{焦|あせ}っています。どう{進|すす}めたらいいですか？
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Junbi ga ōi no de, asette imasu. Dō susumetara ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: Understood. There is a lot to prepare, so I feel pressed. How should I proceed?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないことです。
lines.romaji: Mazu, shigoto o buntan suru koto desu. Hitori de zenbu hikiukenai koto desu.
lines.meaning: First, you should divide the work. You should not take everything on alone.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。ケンタは{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}します。{私|わたし}は{字幕|じまく}の{見直|みなお}しをします。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kenta wa uketsuke o tantō shimasu. Watashi wa jimaku no minaoshi o shimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. Kenta handles registration. I’ll review the subtitles.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}も{減|へ}らしましょう。{同|おな}じメモを{二枚|にまい}{印刷|いんさつ}することはありません。
lines.romaji: Yobun na sagyō mo herashimashō. Onaji memo o nimai insatsu suru koto wa arimasen.
lines.meaning: Let’s reduce extra work too. There is no need to print the same note twice.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。{字幕|じまく}の{文字|もじ}をもう{少|すこ}し{大|おお}きくしてみます。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Jimaku no moji o mō sukoshi ōkiku shite mimasu.
lines.meaning: Okay. I’ll try making the subtitle text a little bigger.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{金曜日|きんようび}の{期限|きげん}は{変|か}わりません。{今日|きょう}は{二人|ふたり}で{準備|じゅんび}を{進|すす}めましょう。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kin’yōbi no kigen wa kawarimasen. Kyō wa futari de junbi o susumemashō.
lines.meaning: Yes. The Friday deadline is unchanged. Let’s have the two of you move the preparation forward today.

readings.title: Decided yesterday; carried out last night
paragraphs: {店長|てんちょう}の{許可|きょか}を{取|と}り、{土曜日|どようび}の{三時|さんじ}に{店|みせ}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ることになった。{字幕|じまく}は{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べる{方針|ほうしん}だ。{私|わたし}は、{今夜|こんや}{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比較|ひかく}することにした。{会議|かいぎ}では{決|き}めただけで、まだ{確認|かくにん}していなかった。{申|もう}し{込|こ}みの{受付|うけつけ}はケンタが{担当|たんとう}し、{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}だ。

{翌朝|よくあさ}、{比較|ひかく}した{結果|けっか}と{根拠|こんきょ}を{報告|ほうこく}した。{店長|てんちょう}からの{返事|へんじ}も{届|とど}いたので、{同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で{電話|でんわ}することはない。{準備|じゅんび}について{相談|そうだん}すると、まず{分担|ぶんたん}することだと{助言|じょげん}された。{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{引|ひ}き{受|う}けない。{余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}を{減|へ}らし、{二人|ふたり}で{責任|せきにん}を{確認|かくにん}しながら{進|すす}める。

glosses.meaning: it was arranged that we would watch

glosses.kana: ひかくすることにした
でんわすることはない

watch.prompt: Optionally save a decision or reassuring line from your own clip. Record who chose, whether the action has happened and what gives the speaker grounds. Recognition is not completion or proficiency.

exercises.prompt: When and where will the gathering take place?
options: Saturday at three, at the café
Friday at midnight, at the university
exercises.explain: The meeting explicitly agrees Saturday at three and Yamamoto confirms the café arrangement.

exercises.prompt: At the meeting, is Bao’s subtitle comparison complete?
options: Yes; Bao finished before the meeting
No; Bao has decided and will check tonight
Yes; Kenta has already checked both screens
exercises.explain: Bao says まだだよ and contrasts the decision with 今夜する.

exercises.prompt: What will Kenta handle?
exercises.explain: Kenta explicitly takes registration and confirms Friday as its deadline.

exercises.context: Form practice: express an explicit decision not to rely only on memory. Put ない before ことにしました.
exercises.line: {記憶|きおく}だけに＿＿ことにしました。
exercises.explain: Negative 頼らない precedes こと; the chosen action is not to rely on memory alone.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named arrangement 使わないことになりました with the plain negative verb.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}は{店|みせ}を＿＿ことになりました。
exercises.explain: Use the plain negative before nominalising こと, not a polite finite form.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta: the comparison is still pending and you will do it tonight.
exercises.line: {確認|かくにん}はもう{終|お}わった？
options: うん、{昨日|きのう}{全部|ぜんぶ}{終|お}わったよ。
うん、{店|みせ}の{会|かい}はもう{中止|ちゅうし}になったよ。
まだだよ。{今夜|こんや}、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}で{字幕|じまく}を{確認|かくにん}する。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the pending check. The other replies invent completion or cancellation.

exercises.meaning: I decided to check the subtitles tonight.
exercises.explain: The past decision ending doesn’t move the planned 今夜 action into the past.

exercises.prompt: Why is a duplicate phone call unnecessary?
options: The reply has already arrived with the same information
Bao has never used a phone
exercises.explain: Bao says the reply arrived; Yamamoto refers to calling with 同じ内容.

exercises.prompt: What advice does Yamamoto give after Bao asks how to proceed?
options: Divide the work and don’t take everything on alone
Delay the gathering until next year
exercises.explain: The two consecutive ことです advice clauses state the division and the negative recommendation.

exercises.prompt: Has the registration deadline changed?
exercises.explain: The last line explicitly says Friday’s deadline doesn’t change.

exercises.context: Form practice: use dictionary verb + ことはありません for no need to phone; this is not a past-experience sentence.
exercises.line: {同|おな}じ{内容|ないよう}で＿＿ことはありません。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 電話する completes the requested no-need construction.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete negative advice 引き受けないことです with ない before こと.
exercises.line: {一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}＿＿ことです。
exercises.explain: Negative advice uses the plain negative; it’s not a polite finite verb before こと.

exercises.context: Reply politely to your manager: accept shared responsibilities, with Kenta handling registration and you reviewing subtitles.
exercises.line: まず、{仕事|しごと}を{分担|ぶんたん}することです。
options: はい。{私|わたし}が{全部|ぜんぶ}{一人|ひとり}でします。
はい。{映画|えいが}はもう{昨年|さくねん}{見|み}ました。
はい。ケンタは{受付|うけつけ}を{担当|たんとう}し、{私|わたし}は{字幕|じまく}を{見直|みなお}します。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts the proposed division; the others reject it or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: We’ll reduce extra work after confirming responsibilities.
tiles: {余分|よぶん}な{作業|さぎょう}を
exercises.explain: Checking the division precedes the reduction; this is a future action, not reported completion.

exercises.prompt: Which sequence matches the message?
options: Decision at the meeting → screen check at night → report the next morning
Completed check → meeting next year → no report
Phone ban → canceled gathering → discarded record
exercises.explain: 今夜 at the meeting and 翌朝 with 比較した結果 establish the sequence.
exercises.context: Track relative time and the completed report.

exercises.prompt: Who handles registration, and what is its deadline?
exercises.explain: 申し込みの受付はケンタが担当し、期限は金曜日 explicitly states both.
exercises.context: Do not confuse the registration deadline with the gathering time.

exercises.prompt: What will the remaining preparation look like?
options: The group permanently bans phone calls
Two people share responsibilities and reduce extra work
exercises.explain: The last two sentences state shared responsibilities, reduced extra work and two people proceeding together.
exercises.context: Read the forward plan, not an invented completed event.

横断歩道を渡ると、銀行が見えます。
歩道を歩いて店に向かいます。
この通路は今日使えません。
道の分岐で地図を見ます。
道順を友達に伝えます。
青い看板が目印です。
矢印は右を指しています。
看板に店の名前が書いてあります。
地図の裏側も見ます。
店は銀行の向かいにあります。
駅に隣接する建物です。
駅から店までの距離を調べます。
目的地は映画を見る店です。
通路が閉まっているので、迂回します。

遅刻しないように、早めに出ます。

lessons.title: A route and its conditions
lessons.description: Follow landmarks, recognise a closed passage and form conditional attachments.
lessons.canDo: Identify a route and the condition that changes it

lessons.title: Preparation before; a message after
lessons.description: Use a stated travel plan for advance advice, then request a message after arrival.
lessons.canDo: Separate a premise from an after-arrival sequence

grammar.title: Describe a regular result or a discovery
grammar.formation: Nonpast dictionary/ない verb or い-adjective + と. Noun/な-adjective + だと; negative でないと. The result clause supplies tense.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 6. Use と for an explained route, an automatic response or a regular result. It can also introduce a discovery after an actual event. A conditional doesn’t certify a universal real-world guarantee. In this unit a route statement reports what is visible, while a one-off request after arrival uses たら.
grammar.example: 横断歩道を渡ると、青い看板が見えます。
grammar.translation: When you cross the pedestrian crossing, the blue sign is visible.

examples.ja: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}ると、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。
examples.en: When you cross the pedestrian crossing, the blue sign is visible.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{暗|くら}いと、{矢印|やじるし}が{見|み}えにくいです。
examples.en: When the road is dark, the arrow is difficult to see.

examples.ja: {地図|ちず}を{開|ひら}くと、{裏側|うらがわ}にも{説明|せつめい}がありました。
examples.en: When I opened the map, there were instructions on the reverse side too.

grammar.mistake: Do not use automatic-result と as the after-arrival link in a one-off instruction such as “when you arrive, please message me”. A past discovery is not a habitual result or a chosen action sequence.

grammar.title: Form the condition; check the subject and result
grammar.formation: Godan final u-row → e-row + ば; ichidan drop る + れば; する→すれば; 来る→来れば (くれば). い-adjective い→ければ, いい→よければ; negative ない→なければ. Noun/な-adjective + ならば/であれば; negative でなければ.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 10 and its earlier regret pattern. ば presents a condition for a result; it’s not an English “if and only if”. たら can overlap. Wishes/requests can follow state, potential or negative conditions, and different actors permit cases that a simplistic blanket ban would reject. For a single actor’s successive actions and a request, practice たら in lesson two.
grammar.example: 歩道を通れば、店に行けます。
grammar.translation: If you take the sidewalk, you can get to the café.

examples.ja: {歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}れば、{店|みせ}に{行|い}けます。
examples.en: If you take the sidewalk, you can get to the café.

examples.ja: {目印|めじるし}が{分|わ}からなければ、{地図|ちず}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.en: If you don’t know the landmark, please check the map.

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}があれば、{二|ふた}つの{経路|けいろ}を{比|くら}べたいです。
examples.en: If there is time, I would like to compare two routes.

grammar.mistake: 書く→書けば, not 書くば; 食べる→食べれば. Never mark ば wrong merely because the result includes a request: the type of condition and the actors matter. Scored form practice names the required pattern.

grammar.title: An action after arrival, or a hypothetical case
grammar.formation: Plain past + ら: た→たら and だ→だら. Noun/な-adjective だったら; い-adjective かったら; いい→よかったら; negative なかったら. Past morphology doesn’t itself set calendar time.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 5. たら can give a condition, an after-completion sequence, a one-off discovery, or a hypothetical situation. In the travel request, reaching the destination happens before sending the arrival message. For negative conditions, the sense is “if not”, not “after not doing”. The surrounding dates decide future or past.
grammar.example: 店に着いたら、メッセージを送ってください。
grammar.translation: When you arrive at the café, please send a message.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
examples.en: When you arrive at the café, please send a message.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}だったら、バスの{運行|うんこう}を{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: If the train service is suspended, I’ll check bus operations.

examples.ja: {終点|しゅうてん}で{降|お}りたら、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えました。
examples.en: When I got off at the last stop, the blue sign was visible.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate future 着いたら as “after you arrived yesterday”. The だ ending also occurs in verb past forms: 読んだ→読んだら. The train suspension in the scene is a contingency, not a reported fact.

grammar.title: Advice based on a stated plan
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + (の)なら. Noun/な-adjective + なら, with no inserted だ in simple 雨なら/便利なら. Clause + のなら adds a nominalised premise.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 1. Respond to the supplied plan or case: Misaki says she will take a bus, so Kenta recommends checking the timetable before boarding. The advice need not wait until the condition’s action happens. なら can also refer back to something already done; it’s not a universal future-only form.
grammar.example: バスで来るなら、乗る前に運賃を調べてください。
grammar.translation: If you are coming by bus, please check the fare before boarding.

examples.ja: バスで{来|く}るなら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
examples.en: If you are coming by bus, please check the fare before boarding.

examples.ja: {終点|しゅうてん}なら、{店|みせ}まで{歩|ある}けます。
examples.en: If you mean the last stop, you can walk to the café from there.

examples.ja: もう{確認|かくにん}したのなら、その{結果|けっか}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: If you have already checked, please tell me the result.

grammar.mistake: バスで来るなら can lead to advice before travel; バスで来たら can make that advice too late when it must precede boarding. Do not insert だ into the simple noun pattern or assume the journey has already happened.

dialogues.title: A route with a closed passage
dialogues.scene: On Friday Misaki asks Bao for directions to Saturday’s permitted café film gathering. Bao describes the station route and the current closed passage. This is route planning, not a report that Misaki has arrived.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {明日|あした}の{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る{会|かい}に{参加|さんか}したいです。{店|みせ}までの{道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてください。
lines.romaji: Ashita no eiga o miru kai ni sanka shitai desu. Mise made no michijun o oshiete kudasai.
lines.meaning: I would like to join tomorrow’s film gathering. Please tell me the route to the café.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {開始|かいし}は{三時|さんじ}です。{駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}から{出|で}てください。
lines.romaji: Kaishi wa sanji desu. Eki no higashiguchi kara dete kudasai.
lines.meaning: It starts at three. Leave through the station’s east exit.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {東口|ひがしぐち}の{前|まえ}にある{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}ですね。{地図|ちず}の{矢印|やじるし}は{右|みぎ}ですか？
lines.romaji: Higashiguchi no mae ni aru ōdanhodō desu ne. Chizu no yajirushi wa migi desu ka?
lines.meaning: It’s the crossing in front of the east exit, right? Does the map’s arrow point right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}って{右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がると、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。
lines.romaji: Hai. Ōdanhodō o watatte migi ni magaru to, aoi kanban ga miemasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. When you cross and turn right, the blue sign is visible.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: その{看板|かんばん}が{目印|めじるし}ですね。{店|みせ}はどこですか？
lines.romaji: Sono kanban ga mejirushi desu ne. Mise wa doko desu ka?
lines.meaning: That sign is the landmark, right? Where is the café?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {銀行|ぎんこう}の{向|む}かいです。{近|ちか}くの{通路|つうろ}は{閉|し}まっているので、{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}れば{行|い}けます。
lines.romaji: Ginkō no mukai desu. Chikaku no tsūro wa shimatte iru node, hodō o tōreba ikemasu.
lines.meaning: It’s opposite the bank. The nearby passage is closed, so you can get there by taking the sidewalk.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {通路|つうろ}を{使|つか}わずに{迂回|うかい}するんですね。{目印|めじるし}が{分|わ}からなければ、どうしますか？
lines.romaji: Tsūro o tsukawazu ni ukai suru n desu ne. Mejirushi ga wakaranakereba, dō shimasu ka?
lines.meaning: So I detour without using the passage. What should I do if I don’t know the landmark?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分|わ}からなければ、{電話|でんわ}してください。{近|ちか}くまで{迎|むか}えに{行|い}きますよ。
lines.romaji: Wakaranakereba, denwa shite kudasai. Chikaku made mukae ni ikimasu yo.
lines.meaning: If you get lost, give me a call. I’ll come and meet you nearby.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ありがとうございます。{道順|みちじゅん}、メモしておきます。
lines.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Michijun, memo shite okimasu.
lines.meaning: Thanks. I’ll write down the directions.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{来|こ}られなくなったら、{連絡|れんらく}してくださいね。
lines.romaji: Hai. Korarenaku nattara, renraku shite kudasai ne.
lines.meaning: Okay. Let me know if you can’t make it.

dialogues.title: Before boarding and after arrival
dialogues.scene: Still on Friday, Misaki tells Kenta she plans to take a bus tomorrow. Timetable, fare and boarding-point advice happens before travel. An arrival message happens after reaching the café. A stopped train is only a contingency.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {明日|あした}はバスで{来|こ}ようと{思|おも}っています。{時刻表|じこくひょう}はまだ{見|み}ていません。
lines.romaji: Ashita wa basu de koyō to omotte imasu. Jikokuhyō wa mada mite imasen.
lines.meaning: I’m thinking of coming by bus tomorrow. I haven’t looked at the timetable yet.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: バスで{来|く}るなら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{時刻表|じこくひょう}と{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
lines.romaji: Basu de kuru nara, noru mae ni jikokuhyō to unchin o shirabete kudasai.
lines.meaning: If you are coming by bus, please check the timetable and fare before boarding.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {乗|の}り{場|ば}も{先|さき}に{確認|かくにん}します。{終点|しゅうてん}で{降|お}りればいいんですね。
lines.romaji: Noriba mo saki ni kakunin shimasu. Shūten de orireba ii n desu ne.
lines.meaning: I’ll check the boarding point first too. I should get off at the last stop, right?

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: はい。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。{到着|とうちゃく}してからでいいですよ。
lines.romaji: Hai. Mise ni tsuitara, messēji o okutte kudasai. Tōchaku shite kara de ii desu yo.
lines.meaning: Yes. When you arrive at the café, please send a message. After arrival is fine.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。もし{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}だったら、バスの{運行|うんこう}を{確認|かくにん}します。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Moshi densha ga unkyū dattara, basu no unkō o kakunin shimasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. If the train service is suspended, I’ll check bus operations.

lines.speaker: Kenta

readings.title: Before travel; after arrival
paragraphs: {土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る{会|かい}は、{三時|さんじ}から{店|みせ}で{開|ひら}きます。バスで{来|く}るなら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{時刻表|じこくひょう}、{運賃|うんちん}、{乗|の}り{場|ば}を{確認|かくにん}してください。{終点|しゅうてん}で{降|お}りて、{駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}に{向|む}かいます。{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}って{右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がると、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。{店|みせ}は{銀行|ぎんこう}の{向|む}かいです。

{近|ちか}くの{通路|つうろ}は{閉|し}まっているので、{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}れば{行|い}けます。{目印|めじるし}が{分|わ}からなければ、{安全|あんぜん}な{場所|ばしょ}で{地図|ちず}を{見|み}てください。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。{道順|みちじゅん}を{調|しら}べるのは{出発|しゅっぱつ}する{前|まえ}、メッセージを{送|おく}るのは{到着|とうちゃく}した{後|あと}です。{映画|えいが}の{字幕|じまく}は、{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べます。

glosses.meaning: if you are coming; supplied plan

glosses.kana: かくにんしてください

glosses.meaning: when you arrive; after reaching it

watch.prompt: Optionally save a conditional line from your own clip. Note the actors, whether it’s a fact or hypothesis, and whether advice happens before or after the condition. Saved examples are evidence, not a proficiency score.

recycling.reason: Route guidance stays focused on travelling and arrival, without unrelated subtitle-policy and responsibility reminders.

exercises.prompt: Which route does Bao describe after leaving the east exit?
options: Cross the crossing, turn right and look for the blue sign
Turn left without crossing and enter the closed passage
Go to the university and wait until next month
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly gives the crossing, right turn and blue sign.

exercises.prompt: Why should Misaki take the sidewalk?
options: The film gathering has been cancelled
exercises.explain: Bao says the passage is closed and the sidewalk reaches the café.

exercises.prompt: Where is the café?
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says 銀行の向かい; the other places are not stated.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the dictionary form before route-result と. Do not choose between different valid conditionals.
exercises.line: {右|みぎ}に＿＿と、{青|あお}い{看板|かんばん}が{見|み}えます。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 曲がる attaches to と; polite ます and て don’t form this route construction.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named negative condition 分からなければ. Change ない to なければ.
exercises.line: {目印|めじるし}が＿＿、{地図|ちず}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
exercises.explain: 分からない→分からなければ. The request follows a negative condition; there is no blanket request ban.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Bao by accepting the stated closed-passage detour.
exercises.line: {近|ちか}くの{通路|つうろ}は{閉|し}まっています。
options: {分|わ}かりました。その{通路|つうろ}を{使|つか}います。
{分|わ}かりました。{映画|えいが}は{昨年|さくねん}{見|み}ました。
{分|わ}かりました。{歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}って{行|い}きます。
exercises.explain: Only the sidewalk reply accepts the route instruction; one contradicts it and one changes the subject.

exercises.meaning: When you cross the pedestrian crossing and turn right, the blue sign is visible.
tiles: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}を{渡|わた}って
exercises.explain: Crossing and turning precede the visible landmark; this is a route result.

exercises.prompt: What should Misaki check before boarding?
options: The timetable, fare and boarding point
The film ending and next year’s survey
exercises.explain: Kenta names timetable and fare, and Misaki explicitly adds the boarding point.

exercises.prompt: When should Misaki send the arrival message?
options: Before she has chosen any transport
Only after the film next year
exercises.explain: Kenta states 店に着いたら and 到着してから, making the sequence explicit.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of the stopped-train case?
options: It’s confirmed that every train is stopped
It proves that the bus is cancelled
It’s hypothetical; no current suspension message is reported
exercises.explain: Misaki considers what to do if trains stop; Kenta says there is no suspension notice at present.

exercises.prompt: What responsibility and deadline does Kenta confirm on Friday?
options: Kenta handles registration due today, and two people will check responsibilities
Bao alone handles registration next month
Misaki has already cancelled every registration
exercises.explain: The final line names 申し込み, says its 期限 is 今日 on Friday, and states 二人で責任を確認します.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the past-plus-ら arrival form 着いたら, for a future message after arrival.
exercises.line: {店|みせ}に＿＿、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
exercises.explain: 着く has plain past 着いた; adding ら gives 着いたら. The future plan fixes time.

exercises.context: Form practice: the stated plan is travel by bus. Supply the dictionary form before なら; check fares before boarding.
exercises.line: バスで＿＿なら、{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{運賃|うんちん}を{調|しら}べてください。
exercises.explain: 来るなら refers to the plan; the explicit 前 phrase locates preparation before travel.

exercises.context: Reply politely: accept timetable preparation before travel and a message after reaching the café.
exercises.line: バスで{来|く}るなら、{先|さき}に{時刻表|じこくひょう}を{見|み}てください。{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いたら、メッセージを{送|おく}ってください。
options: はい。{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に{確認|かくにん}して、{店|みせ}に{着|つ}いてから{送|おく}ります。
はい。{到着|とうちゃく}してから{初|はじ}めて{時刻表|じこくひょう}を{調|しら}べます。
はい。まだ{着|つ}いていませんが、{到着|とうちゃく}したと{送|おく}ります。
exercises.explain: The first preserves both stated steps. The others postpone preparation or falsely claim arrival.

exercises.meaning: If you are coming by bus, please check the timetable before boarding.
tiles: {確認|かくにん}してください。
exercises.explain: The advice depends on the stated plan but occurs before boarding, not after the journey.

exercises.prompt: Which sequence follows the guide?
options: Send a completed-arrival message → choose a bus → start travel
Check travel details → take the bus → reach the café → send a message
Reach the café → check the boarding point for the first time
exercises.explain: 乗る前 and 着いたら, then the final before/after comparison, state this order.
exercises.context: Read the timing, not only the familiar transport words.

exercises.prompt: Which location and landmark are stated?
options: Inside the university, with a red flag
At the first bus stop, with a yellow screen
Opposite the bank, with a blue sign
exercises.explain: The first paragraph states 青い看板 and 銀行の向かい.
exercises.context: Identify the actual route markers.

exercises.prompt: Which detail must readers look up because the guide doesn’t supply it?
options: The fare and timetable for their bus
Which way to turn after crossing
exercises.explain: The guide requests fare/timetable checks but gives no amounts or bus times; it states three o’clock and a right turn.
exercises.context: Separate supplied facts from a requested lookup.

lessons.title: A fact and an unmet expectation
lessons.description: Hear a complaint, identify its grounds and keep a condition separate from a promise.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish a visible fact from an expectation

lessons.title: Recognise blame; repair the conversation
lessons.description: Identify an accusing expression and use a calm explanation or apology between peers.
lessons.canDo: Recognise reproach without assuming private intention

grammar.title: An outcome that stays the same
grammar.formation: Verb て/で + も; い-adjective くても (いい→よくても); noun/な-adjective でも. Negative なくても, or nominal でなくても/じゃなくても.
grammar.explanation: Go beyond N4 permission and non-obligation. ても can express even-if or even-though: the outcome holds despite the condition. Facts and context determine whether the condition has happened. Here the group retains viewer choice even if preparation takes time; that promise is distinct from proving preparation complete.
grammar.example: 準備に時間がかかっても、字幕は選べるようにします。
grammar.translation: Even if preparation takes time, we’ll make the subtitles selectable.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、{字幕|じまく}は{選|えら}べるようにします。
examples.en: Even if preparation takes time, we’ll make the subtitles selectable.

examples.ja: {不公平|ふこうへい}でも、{相手|あいて}を{傷|きず}つける{言葉|ことば}は{使|つか}いたくありません。
examples.en: Even if it’s unfair, I don’t want to use words that hurt the other person.

examples.ja: {忙|いそが}しくなくても、{分担|ぶんたん}は{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: Even if we are not busy, we’ll check responsibilities.

grammar.mistake: Noun/な-adjective + でも, not だても. Negative verbs use なくても. A hypothetical inconvenience is not evidence that the inconvenience actually occurred.

grammar.title: A fact contrary to expectation
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause + のに. Present affirmative noun/な-adjective + なのに; past nominal だったのに; nominal negative ではないのに.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 unit 10. のに links an expectation to a contrary fact; it may convey surprise or disappointment. Misaki says she expected selectable subtitles but saw a screen with none. The later explanation identifies a temporary test; the complaint alone doesn’t prove someone broke the policy. Purpose のに is a different construction.
grammar.example: 字幕を選べると聞いたのに、今の画面にはありません。
grammar.translation: Although I heard we could choose subtitles, there are none on the current screen.

examples.ja: {字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べると{聞|き}いたのに、{今|いま}の{画面|がめん}にはありません。
examples.en: Although I heard we could choose subtitles, there are none on the current screen.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}なのに、{二人|ふたり}の{評価|ひょうか}が{違|ちが}います。
examples.en: Although the conditions are the same, the two people’s assessments differ.

examples.ja: {丁寧|ていねい}に{説明|せつめい}したのに、{意図|いと}が{伝|つた}わりませんでした。
examples.en: Although I explained carefully, my intention was not conveyed.

grammar.mistake: 条件なのに uses な, while noun + のくせに uses の in a different pattern. Do not turn the contrast into an unsupported claim about someone’s secret motive or use the purpose のに rule here.

grammar.title: Recognise blame; choose how to repair it
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + くせに; noun + のくせに; な-adjective + なくせに. Past verb clauses attach directly.
grammar.explanation: くせに presents a contradiction with reproach. It can sound insulting, even between friends. Recognise it in an accusation, then practice an explanation or neutral statement of what happened. The lesson doesn’t certify the accusation as true. It’s not a polite default addressed to a manager.
grammar.example: 「選べると言ったくせに」と、友達を責めました。
grammar.translation: I reproached my friend: “You said we could choose, and yet…”

examples.ja: 「{選|えら}べると{言|い}ったくせに」と、{友達|ともだち}を{責|せ}めました。
examples.en: I reproached my friend: “You said we could choose, and yet…”

examples.ja: 「{担当者|たんとうしゃ}のくせに」と{言|い}うと、{非難|ひなん}が{強|つよ}く{聞|き}こえます。
examples.en: Saying “despite being the person in charge” sounds strongly accusatory.

examples.ja: 「{冷静|れいせい}なくせに」という{言|い}い{方|かた}は、ここでは{使|つか}いません。
examples.en: We’ll not use the accusing expression “though you act calm” here.

grammar.mistake: Noun の versus な-adjective な is an attachment contrast. Do not use identity stereotypes as evidence of blame. For an ordinary factual disagreement, state the facts and request clarification.

grammar.title: Coexisting states, not two ordinary actions
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + ながらも; progressive ていながらも; い-adjective, な-adjective stem or noun + ながらも. Recognise established concessive state/awareness uses.
grammar.explanation: Contrast two qualities or states that coexist. 小さいながらも explains a limited-size café that still supports the activity; 不器用ながらも describes effort despite awkwardness. Ordinary 音楽を聞きながらメモする simply joins actions by one doer; it need not express a concession. Do not infer contrast from も alone.
grammar.example: 店は小さいながらも、二つの画面を比べられます。
grammar.translation: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}は{小|ちい}さいながらも、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比|くら}べられます。
examples.en: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.

examples.ja: {不器用|ぶきよう}ながらも、{気持|きも}ちを{丁寧|ていねい}に{伝|つた}えました。
examples.en: Despite being awkward, I conveyed my feelings carefully.

examples.ja: {緊張|きんちょう}していながらも、{冷静|れいせい}に{話|はな}しました。
examples.en: Although I was nervous, I spoke calmly.

grammar.mistake: Use the adjective or noun stem: 不器用ながらも, not 不器用なながらも. The set expression 残念ながら is not automatically a productive contrast with も. Read the two coexisting states.

dialogues.title: A screen and an incomplete explanation
dialogues.scene: On Saturday before the three-o’clock film gathering, Misaki sees a subtitle-free screen and believes viewer choice has been lost. Kenta says it’s a temporary test. The group has not started the film.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {歩道|ほどう}を{通|とお}って{来|き}ました。{目印|めじるし}も{分|わ}かりました。でも、{今|いま}の{画面|がめん}には{字幕|じまく}がありません。
lines.romaji: Hodō o tōtte kimashita. Mejirushi mo wakarimashita. Demo, ima no gamen ni wa jimaku ga arimasen.
lines.meaning: I came along the sidewalk and recognised the landmark. But there are no subtitles on the current screen.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {今|いま}は{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}した{状態|じょうたい}で、{画面|がめん}を{試|ため}しているんだ。
lines.romaji: Ima wa jimaku o keshita jōtai de, gamen o tameshite iru n da.
lines.meaning: Right now I’m testing the screen with the subtitles turned off.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {選|えら}べると{聞|き}いたのに、{字幕|じまく}がないと{不満|ふまん}があります。{読|よ}みたい{人|ひと}には{不公平|ふこうへい}です。
lines.romaji: Eraberu to kiita noni, jimaku ga nai to fuman ga arimasu. Yomitai hito ni wa fukōhei desu.
lines.meaning: Although I heard we could choose, I’m dissatisfied if there are no subtitles. It’s unfair to people who want to read.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {方針|ほうしん}は{変|か}わっていません。{準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、{字幕|じまく}は{選|えら}べるようにします。
lines.romaji: Hōshin wa kawatte imasen. Junbi ni jikan ga kakatte mo, jimaku wa eraberu yō ni shimasu.
lines.meaning: The policy has not changed. Even if preparation takes time, we’ll make the subtitles selectable.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}で{試|ため}したくて、{今|いま}だけ{消|け}していたんだ。
lines.romaji: Futatsu no gamen o onaji jōken de tameshitakute, ima dake keshite ita n da.
lines.meaning: I wanted to test the two screens under the same conditions, so I had turned them off just for now.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: それを{先|さき}に{説明|せつめい}してほしかったです。{決定|けってい}が{変|か}わったと{思|おも}いました。
lines.romaji: Sore o saki ni setsumei shite hoshikatta desu. Kettei ga kawatta to omoimashita.
lines.meaning: I wanted you to explain that first. I thought the decision had changed.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: ごめん。{先|さき}に{言|い}えばよかったね。{説明|せつめい}が{足|た}りなかったのは{反省|はんせい}してる。
lines.romaji: Gomen. Saki ni ieba yokatta ne. Setsumei ga tarinakatta no wa hansei shiteru.
lines.meaning: Sorry. I should’ve said something first. I realise I didn’t explain enough.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分担|ぶんたん}を{確認|かくにん}しましょう。{私|わたし}が{字幕|じまく}の{確認|かくにん}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けます。
lines.romaji: Buntan o kakunin shimashō. Watashi ga jimaku no kakunin o hikiukemasu.
lines.meaning: Let’s confirm the division of tasks. I’ll take on checking the subtitles.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {忙|いそが}しくても、{説明|せつめい}は{聞|き}きたいです。{私|わたし}も{口調|くちょう}を{穏|おだ}やかにします。
lines.romaji: Isogashikute mo, setsumei wa kikitai desu. Watashi mo kuchō o odayaka ni shimasu.
lines.meaning: Even if we are busy, I want to hear the explanation. I’ll keep my tone calm too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: うん。{三時|さんじ}の{開始|かいし}までに、{選|えら}べることを{確認|かくにん}しよう。
lines.romaji: Un. Sanji no kaishi made ni, eraberu koto o kakunin shiyō.
lines.meaning: Yes. Let’s check that people can choose before the three-o’clock start.

dialogues.title: A pointed remark and a repair
dialogues.scene: After a pointed exchange between these two scenes, Misaki quotes and apologises for her accusatory remark. Kenta explains his response, Bao distinguishes a stated fact from guessed intention, and the friends check selectable subtitles before the film begins.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: さっき、「{選|えら}べるって{言|い}ったくせに」と{責|せ}めてしまった。ごめん。
lines.romaji: Sakki, “Eraberu tte itta kuse ni” to semete shimatta. Gomen.
lines.meaning: A moment ago I reproached you: “You said we could choose, and yet…” Sorry.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {俺|おれ}も{強|つよ}く{言|い}ってしまった。ごめん。{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}したのは{俺|おれ}だよ。
lines.romaji: Ore mo tsuyoku itte shimatta. Gomen. Setsumei o shōryaku shita no wa ore da yo.
lines.meaning: I snapped too. Sorry. I was the one who skipped the explanation.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {二人|ふたり}とも、{映画|えいが}を{楽|たの}しみたいんだよね。{今|いま}、{字幕|じまく}を{出|だ}してみませんか？
lines.romaji: Futari tomo, eiga o tanoshimitai n da yo ne. Ima, jimaku o dashite mimasen ka?
lines.meaning: You both want to enjoy the film, right? Shall we try turning the subtitles on now?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{勝手|かって}に{決|き}めつけちゃったね。{何|なに}を{試|ため}してたのか、{聞|き}けばよかった。
lines.romaji: Un. Katte ni kimetsukechatta ne. Nani o tameshiteta no ka, kikeba yokatta.
lines.meaning: Yeah. I jumped to conclusions. I should’ve asked what you were testing.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {不器用|ぶきよう}ながらも、{気持|きも}ちは{丁寧|ていねい}に{伝|つた}えたい。{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しないようにするよ。
lines.romaji: Bukiyō nagara mo, kimochi wa teinei ni tsutaetai. Setsumei o shōryaku shinai yō ni suru yo.
lines.meaning: Although I’m awkward, I want to convey my feelings carefully. I’ll try not to leave out explanations.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: この{店|みせ}は{小|ちい}さいながらも、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比|くら}べられます。{冷静|れいせい}に{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
lines.romaji: Kono mise wa chiisai nagara mo, futatsu no gamen o kuraberaremasu. Reisei ni kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: Although this café is small, we can compare two screens. Let’s check calmly.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {確認|かくにん}できた。{字幕|じまく}を{出|だ}すかどうか、{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べるね。
lines.romaji: Kakunin dekita. Jimaku o dasu ka dō ka, miru hito ga eraberu ne.
lines.meaning: We have checked it. Viewers can choose whether to display subtitles, right?

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: うん。{分担|ぶんたん}も{確認|かくにん}できたし、これで{仲直|なかなお}りだね。
lines.romaji: Un. Buntan mo kakunin dekita shi, kore de nakanaori da ne.
lines.meaning: We’ve sorted out who’s doing what too. Friends again?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{本当|ほんとう}は{一緒|いっしょ}に{見|み}るの、すごく{楽|たの}しみにしてたんだ。
lines.romaji: Un. Hontō wa issho ni miru no, sugoku tanoshimi ni shiteta n da.
lines.meaning: Yeah. I was actually really looking forward to watching together.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {準備|じゅんび}ができました。{三時|さんじ}になったら、{映画|えいが}を{始|はじ}めましょう。
lines.romaji: Junbi ga dekimashita. Sanji ni nattara, eiga o hajimemashō.
lines.meaning: Preparation is ready. When it becomes three o’clock, let’s start the film.

readings.title: What the screen didn’t tell me
paragraphs: {土曜日|どようび}、{店|みせ}に{着|つ}くと、{画面|がめん}には{字幕|じまく}がなかった。{選|えら}べると{聞|き}いていたのに、{方針|ほうしん}が{変|か}わったと{思|おも}って{不満|ふまん}を{伝|つた}えた。ケンタは{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}で{試|ため}していたと{説明|せつめい}した。{先|さき}に{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}けばよかった。

{準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、{字幕|じまく}を{選|えら}べるという{方針|ほうしん}は{変|か}えない。「{言|い}ったくせに」と{責|せ}めたことを{謝|あやま}り、{仲直|なかなお}りした。{小|ちい}さいながらも、{二|ふた}つの{画面|がめん}を{比|くら}べられる{店|みせ}で、{冷静|れいせい}に{確認|かくにん}した。{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{選|えら}べることを{確|たし}かめてから、{三時|さんじ}に{映画|えいが}を{始|はじ}めた。{相手|あいて}の{本音|ほんね}は、{画面|がめん}だけでは{分|わ}からない。

glosses.meaning: you said so and yet; accusing quotation

watch.prompt: Optionally save a contrasting line from your own clip. Record what is stated, what is a speaker’s accusation, and how the listener responds. Do not turn tone or a saved line into a certified personality or proficiency score.

exercises.prompt: Why does Misaki express dissatisfaction?
options: She expected selectable subtitles but sees none on the current screen
She cannot find the blue sign
She has been told the gathering is next year
exercises.explain: Misaki explicitly contrasts what she heard with the subtitle-free screen; she already found the landmark.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta say he is doing?
options: Temporarily testing two screens under the same conditions
Moving the café to the university
exercises.explain: Kenta says 今だけ and 同じ条件; this is his explanation, not a secret-intention claim.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao say will remain true even if preparation takes time?
options: Registration no longer has a deadline
Viewers will be able to choose subtitles
exercises.explain: Bao retains the policy with 時間がかかっても; the later check has not yet happened.

exercises.context: Form practice: express even-if with the noun/na-adjective 不公平 and も; use でも.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{相手|あいて}を{傷|きず}つける{言葉|ことば}は{使|つか}いたくありません。
exercises.explain: The nominal/na-adjective concessive form is でも, not だても or なても.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun pattern 条件なのに; don’t choose between different concession constructions.
exercises.line: {同|おな}じ{条件|じょうけん}＿＿、{二人|ふたり}の{評価|ひょうか}が{違|ちが}います。
exercises.explain: In the standard pattern taught here, present nominal 条件 takes なのに.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Kenta: ask what he was testing, without assuming an excuse or a changed policy.
exercises.line: {今|いま}だけ、{字幕|じまく}を{消|け}していたんだ。
options: {説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}きません。{言|い}い{訳|わけ}だけですね。
{店|みせ}は{来年|らいねん}の{春|はる}に{開|ひら}きますね。
{何|なに}を{確認|かくにん}するために{消|け}したのか、{教|おし}えてください。
exercises.explain: The first asks for the actual test purpose. The others reject explanation or change the subject.

exercises.meaning: Even if preparation takes time, we’ll make the subtitles selectable.
tiles: {準備|じゅんび}に{時間|じかん}がかかっても、
exercises.explain: The preparation condition doesn’t change the promised viewer choice; this is a forward action.

exercises.prompt: Which earlier wording does Misaki apologise for?
options: Saying “You said we could choose, and yet…” with blame
Explaining that the bus fare must be checked
exercises.explain: The opening explicitly quotes 言ったくせに and says 責めてしまった and ごめん.

exercises.prompt: Who acknowledges leaving out the explanation?
options: A person not named in the scene
exercises.explain: Kenta says 説明を省略したのは俺だ.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao suggest after the apologies?
options: Try turning the subtitles on now
exercises.explain: Bao asks 今、字幕を出してみませんか, suggesting that they try displaying subtitles.

exercises.prompt: What is verified before starting the film?
options: Viewers can choose whether to display subtitles, and responsibilities are checked
The train suspension has been confirmed
The policy has permanently removed all subtitles
exercises.explain: Misaki checks viewer choice, and Kenta confirms the division and decision.

exercises.context: Recognition/form practice: in the quoted accusing expression 担当者のくせに, supply the noun attachment. This is not a recommended manager greeting.
exercises.line: 「{担当者|たんとうしゃ}＿＿くせに」という{言|い}い{方|かた}は{非難|ひなん}が{強|つよ}いです。
exercises.explain: A noun takes のくせに; a na-adjective takes なくせに.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the stated な-adjective concession 不器用ながらも with its stem.
exercises.line: ＿＿ながらも、{気持|きも}ちを{丁寧|ていねい}に{伝|つた}えました。
exercises.explain: 不器用 is the stem before ながらも, without な or だ.

exercises.context: Reply to your friend in casual Japanese: accept making up and acknowledge your blaming wording.
exercises.line: {仲直|なかなお}りしよう。
options: うん。{責|せ}める{言|い}い{方|かた}をして、ごめんね。
いや。{説明|せつめい}は{聞|き}かない。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{終点|しゅうてん}は{知|し}らない。
exercises.explain: The first accepts reconciliation and apologises for blame; the others reject or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: Although the café is small, we can compare two screens.
tiles: {店|みせ}は{小|ちい}さいながらも、
exercises.explain: Limited size and comparison capacity coexist; this is not a two-action while sentence.

exercises.prompt: What happens before the film starts at three?
options: They announce a permanent ban on subtitles
They apologise, make up and verify viewer subtitle choice
They cancel the café gathering until next year
exercises.explain: The message states apologising, reconciliation, the choice check, then 三時に映画を始めた.
exercises.context: Find the completed sequence rather than an earlier complaint.

exercises.prompt: What conclusion does the writer explicitly avoid?
options: Reporting that subtitles were missing on the first screen
Claiming to know private feelings from the screen alone
exercises.explain: The closing 本音は、画面だけでは分からない limits the inference; the other two are stated facts/reports.
exercises.context: Separate observation, someone’s explanation and private intention.

exercises.prompt: Which policy is kept even if preparation takes time?
options: No viewer may ever see subtitles
exercises.explain: 時間がかかっても introduces the unchanged viewer-choice policy.
exercises.context: Track what the concession leaves unchanged.

words.example: 運行の復旧を確認します。
設備の修復には時間がかかりました。
停電のため、朝の電車は運休でした。
この地区では断水が続いています。
災害への対策を話し合います。
被害の内容を確認します。
店の損害を調べます。
時間の損失を減らしたいです。
乗り場の混雑で、発車が遅れました。
積雪のため、通路が使えません。
豪雨の被害を確認しました。
昨夜は雷の音を聞きました。
強風で看板が倒れました。
天候の情報を確認します。
事故の予防について学びます。
混雑の防止のために、入口を分けます。
地域の支援について記事を読みます。
救助の状況を報告しました。
町の復興には時間がかかります。
必要な援助を確かめます。
要因を一つずつ調べます。
因果を考えるときは、記録を確認します。
確認の手間を省きません。
設備の状態を調べます。
不具合の原因は調査中です。
点検が終わってから、設備を使います。
状況が困難でも、冷静に話します。
因果関係があるかどうかは、まだ分かりません。
停電が発生した時刻を調べます。
避難の情報を読みます。
