lessons.title: A reason, a thank-you and an accusation
lessons.description: Follow a disrupted route and distinguish appreciative or negative attribution.
lessons.canDo: Identify a reason and the speaker’s stance

lessons.title: A report keeps what is still unknown
lessons.description: Read the update time, the event sequence and the limit of a cause claim.
lessons.canDo: Separate a reported reason from an unproved cause

grammar.title: Credit a benefit; notice sarcasm
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + おかげで; noun のおかげで; な-adjective なおかげで. Past/negative clauses keep their conjugation.
grammar.explanation: Usually credits a helpful cause with appreciation. Misaki thanks a friend for showing an alternative route. Negative sarcastic use also exists: wording, context and delivery matter. A thankful sentence states the speaker’s attribution; it doesn’t prove that no other factors helped.
grammar.example: 道順を教えてくれたおかげで、無事に着きました。
grammar.translation: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely.

examples.ja: {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてくれたおかげで、{無事|ぶじ}に{着|つ}きました。
examples.en: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely.

examples.ja: {点検|てんけん}が{丁寧|ていねい}なおかげで、{不具合|ふぐあい}に{気|き}づきました。
examples.en: Thanks to the careful inspection, we noticed the problem.

examples.ja: 「{君|きみ}のおかげで{遅刻|ちこく}したよ」は、ここでは{皮肉|ひにく}です。
examples.en: “Thanks to you I was late” is sarcastic here.

grammar.mistake: Noun + の, na-adjective + な. Do not label every おかげで result positive, or infer sole causation from a thank-you. Sarcasm is labelled recognition here, not the default way to thank someone.

grammar.title: Hear a negative attribution without certifying blame
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + せいで; noun のせいで; な-adjective なせいで. Sentence-final せいだ/せいです.
grammar.explanation: Normally attributes an unwanted result to a cause, sometimes blaming someone. The scene identifies transport disruption, then refuses to assume that a particular worker caused the electrical problem. A speaker’s せいで claim may be justified or mistaken; the grammar alone cannot settle responsibility.
grammar.example: 乗り場が混雑したせいで、発車が遅れました。
grammar.translation: Because the boarding point became crowded, departure was delayed.

examples.ja: {乗|の}り{場|ば}が{混雑|こんざつ}したせいで、{発車|はっしゃ}が{遅|おく}れました。
examples.en: Because the boarding point became crowded, departure was delayed.

examples.ja: {強風|きょうふう}のせいで、{看板|かんばん}が{倒|たお}れました。
examples.en: The sign fell because of the strong wind.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}が{不十分|ふじゅうぶん}なせいで、{戸惑|とまど}いました。
examples.en: I was confused because the explanation was insufficient.

grammar.mistake: Use nominal のせいで rather than だせいで. Undesirable attribution is the usual use, not a universal ban on all other nuances. Do not treat a quoted blame claim as a checked cause.

grammar.title: Read ため as cause or purpose in context
grammar.formation: Attributive verb/い-adjective clause + ため(に); noun のため(に); な-adjective なため(に). Past and negative clauses are allowed; に is often omitted in notices.
grammar.explanation: Purpose ために was taught in unit 1. Here an outage is given as the reason for cancelled morning service. Causal ため often occurs in reports with completed events, but present states and negative causes also work. Identify the relation between the clauses rather than deciding by tense alone. Neutral wording doesn’t independently certify the reported cause.
grammar.example: 停電のため、朝の電車は運休でした。
grammar.translation: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.

examples.ja: {停電|ていでん}のため、{朝|あさ}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{運休|うんきゅう}でした。
examples.en: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.

examples.ja: {設備|せつび}が{使|つか}えないため、{開始|かいし}{時刻|じこく}を{変|か}えます。
examples.en: Because the equipment cannot be used, we’ll change the start time.

examples.ja: {混雑|こんざつ}を{防止|ぼうし}するために、{入口|いりぐち}を{分|わ}けます。
examples.en: We separate the entrances to prevent crowding.

grammar.mistake: Noun + のため, na-adjective + なため. The third example is deliberate purpose; the first two are cause. Past tense is a clue, not a complete purpose/cause rule.

grammar.title: Give a reason for a request
grammar.formation: Plain/polite clause + から; plain present noun/な-adjective + だから. Attributive clause + ので; present noun/な-adjective + なので; polite ですので. Past/negative clauses conjugate before the connector.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve から and ので. Both can give reasons for an action or a suitable request. ので often presents a softer explanation, while から can foreground the speaker’s reason; these are tendencies. Neither proves that the explanation is objectively true. The task names the form when testing attachment and states the listener when requesting help.
grammar.example: 運休なので、別の経路を教えてください。
grammar.translation: Since the service is cancelled, please tell me another route.

examples.ja: {運休|うんきゅう}なので、{別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: Since the service is cancelled, please tell me another route.

examples.ja: {点検|てんけん}が{終|お}わりましたので、{運行|うんこう}を{再開|さいかい}します。
examples.en: The inspection has finished, so we’ll resume service.

examples.ja: {渋滞|じゅうたい}が{心配|しんぱい}だから、{早|はや}く{出|で}よう。
examples.en: I’m worried about traffic congestion, so let’s leave early.

grammar.mistake: Nominal 運休なので needs な; 運休だから has だ. ので is not restricted to statements without requests, and から is not automatically rude. Do not force a unique synonym choice when both fit.

dialogues.title: A disrupted route and a thank-you
dialogues.scene: Monday morning, after Saturday’s film gathering, a line is out of service following a Sunday-night outage. Misaki takes a bus and walks. This is an original fictional scenario, not real transport advice.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {月曜日|げつようび}の{朝|あさ}、{停電|ていでん}のために{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}していると{知|し}りました。
lines.romaji: Getsuyōbi no asa, teiden no tame ni densha ga unkyū shite iru to shirimashita.
lines.meaning: On Monday morning I learned that trains were out of service because of a power outage.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {日曜日|にちようび}の{夜|よる}に{起|お}きた{停電|ていでん}だね。{土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}は{予定|よてい}どおり{終|お}わったよ。
lines.romaji: Nichiyōbi no yoru ni okita teiden da ne. Doyōbi no eiga wa yotei dōri owatta yo.
lines.meaning: That’s the outage that occurred Sunday night. Saturday’s film ended as scheduled.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {乗|の}り{場|ば}の{混雑|こんざつ}と{渋滞|じゅうたい}のせいで、バスの{発車|はっしゃ}も{遅|おく}れました。
lines.romaji: Noriba no konzatsu to jūtai no sei de, basu no hassha mo okuremashita.
lines.meaning: The bus departure was delayed too because of crowding at the boarding point and traffic congestion.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: バスを{降|お}りた{後|あと}の{経路|けいろ}を{送|おく}ります。{曲|ま}がり{角|かど}の{看板|かんばん}を{目印|めじるし}にしてください。
lines.romaji: Basu o orita ato no keiro o okurimasu. Magarikado no kanban o mejirushi ni shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: I’ll send the route for after you get off the bus. Use the sign at the corner as a landmark.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてくれたおかげで、{無事|ぶじ}に{目的地|もくてきち}に{着|つ}きました。ありがとう。
lines.romaji: Michijun o oshiete kureta okage de, buji ni mokutekichi ni tsukimashita. Arigatō.
lines.meaning: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely at the destination. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {電車|でんしゃ}はまだ{運休|うんきゅう}してるんだね。{帰|かえ}りもバスにする？
lines.romaji: Densha wa mada unkyū shiteru n da ne. Kaeri mo basu ni suru?
lines.meaning: The trains are still stopped, then. Are you taking the bus home too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {帰|かえ}る{前|まえ}に、{運行|うんこう}の{情報|じょうほう}を{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
lines.romaji: Kaeru mae ni, unkō no jōhō o kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: Let’s check the service update before you head home.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {午前|ごぜん}の{説明会|せつめいかい}は、{午後|ごご}{四時|よじ}に{変|か}わったんですね。
lines.romaji: Gozen no setsumeikai wa, gogo yoji ni kawatta n desu ne.
lines.meaning: The morning information session has been moved to four in the afternoon, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。その{決定|けってい}を{参加者|さんかしゃ}に{伝|つた}えました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Sono kettei o sankasha ni tsutaemashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. I have told the participants that decision.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: じゃ、{四時|よじ}まで{少|すこ}し{休|やす}もう。バス、{混|こ}んでて{疲|つか}れたでしょ。
lines.romaji: Ja, yoji made sukoshi yasumō. Basu, kondete tsukareta desho.
lines.meaning: Let’s rest a bit until four. That crowded bus must’ve been tiring.

dialogues.title: An update with a limited claim
dialogues.scene: Monday at three in the afternoon, Bao and Yamamoto prepare a short fictional update. Service restoration is reported, the electrical cause remains under investigation, and the information session has not yet started.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}です。{運行|うんこう}が{復旧|ふっきゅう}したという{発表|はっぴょう}を{確認|かくにん}しました。
lines.romaji: Gogo sanji desu. Unkō ga fukkyū shita to iu happyō o kakunin shimashita.
lines.meaning: It’s three in the afternoon. I have checked the announcement that service has been restored.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {点検|てんけん}が{終|お}わったので、{運行|うんこう}を{再開|さいかい}したという{説明|せつめい}ですね。
lines.romaji: Tenken ga owatta node, unkō o saikai shita to iu setsumei desu ne.
lines.meaning: The explanation is that service resumed because the inspection was completed, right?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{設備|せつび}に{不具合|ふぐあい}が{発生|はっせい}したそうですが、その{要因|よういん}はまだ{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}です。
lines.romaji: Hai. Setsubi ni fuguai ga hassei shita sō desu ga, sono yōin wa mada chōsa chū desu.
lines.meaning: Yes. A problem reportedly occurred with the equipment, but its contributing factors are still under investigation.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうなんですね。{再開|さいかい}した{時間|じかん}も、{記事|きじ}に{入|い}れた{方|ほう}がいいですか？
lines.romaji: Sō nan desu ne. Saikai shita jikan mo, kiji ni ireta hō ga ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: I see. Should I include the time service resumed in the article too?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: はい。{運行|うんこう}の{再開|さいかい}と、{説明会|せつめいかい}の{開始|かいし}{時刻|じこく}を{書|か}いてください。
lines.romaji: Hai. Unkō no saikai to, setsumeikai no kaishi jikoku o kaite kudasai.
lines.meaning: Yes. Include the service resumption and the start time of the information session.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分担|ぶんたん}どおり、{私|わたし}が{要約|ようやく}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けます。{別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}の{案内|あんない}も{入|い}れます。
lines.romaji: Buntan dōri, watashi ga yōyaku o hikiukemasu. Betsu no keiro no annai mo iremasu.
lines.meaning: As assigned, I’ll take on the summary. I’ll include guidance on the alternative route too.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto

lines.line: {参加者|さんかしゃ}にも、もう{一度|いちど}{連絡|れんらく}します。{四時|よじ}だと{分|わ}かるように{書|か}きますね。

readings.title: Service restored; the session still starts at four
paragraphs: {月曜日|げつようび}{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}の{更新|こうしん}。{日曜日|にちようび}の{夜|よる}に{発生|はっせい}した{停電|ていでん}のため、{朝|あさ}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{運休|うんきゅう}だった。バスの{乗|の}り{場|ば}も{混雑|こんざつ}した。{午後|ごご}には{点検|てんけん}が{終|お}わり、{運行|うんこう}が{復旧|ふっきゅう}したという{発表|はっぴょう}を{確認|かくにん}した。{設備|せつび}の{不具合|ふぐあい}の{要因|よういん}は、まだ{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だ。{同|おな}じ{夜|よる}に{雷|かみなり}があったが、それだけで{因果関係|いんがかんけい}があるとは{言|い}えない。

{午前|ごぜん}の{説明会|せつめいかい}は、{午後|ごご}{四時|よじ}に{変|か}わった。この{決定|けってい}は{復旧|ふっきゅう}{後|ご}も{変|か}えない。{参加者|さんかしゃ}には{連絡|れんらく}{済|ず}みで、{開始|かいし}{前|まえ}に{再|ふたた}び{案内|あんない}する。{土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}は{予定|よてい}どおり{終|お}わっており、{今回|こんかい}の{運休|うんきゅう}とは{別|べつ}の{出来事|できごと}だ。{分|わ}かっていることと{分|わ}からないことを{省略|しょうりゃく}せずに、{情報|じょうほう}を{要約|ようやく}した。

watch.prompt: Optionally save a cause or thank-you line from your own clip. Record the stated reason, the speaker’s stance and which causes remain unconfirmed. This is observation, not a scored causal experiment.

exercises.prompt: When did the outage occur?
options: Sunday night, after the Saturday film had ended

exercises.prompt: What does Misaki specifically thank Bao for?

A confirmed fault by a named employee
Crowding at the boarding point and traffic congestion

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the stated na-adjective pattern 丁寧なおかげで, with 丁寧 before the blank.
exercises.line: {点検|てんけん}が{丁寧|ていねい}＿＿おかげで、{不具合|ふぐあい}に{気|き}づきました。
exercises.explain: 丁寧 is a na-adjective, so its attributive attachment here is な.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun pattern 強風のせいで.
exercises.line: {強風|きょうふう}＿＿せいで、{看板|かんばん}が{倒|たお}れました。
exercises.explain: 強風 is a noun; の connects it to せいで.

exercises.context: You are speaking politely to the friend who offered an alternative route. Thank them and request it.
exercises.line: {別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{送|おく}ります。
options: {君|きみ}のせいだ。{道順|みちじゅん}は{聞|き}かない。
{土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}はまだ{始|はじ}まっていませんね。
ありがとうございます。{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}なので、{教|おし}えてください。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the offered help politely; the others accuse or contradict the stated Saturday chronology.

exercises.meaning: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely at the destination.
tiles: {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてくれたおかげで、
exercises.explain: Route guidance is the credited help, followed by the completed safe arrival.

exercises.prompt: What has Yamamoto checked at three in the afternoon?
options: An announcement that service has been restored
That a particular person caused the outage
That the session is already over
exercises.explain: The first line checks the restoration announcement, not private fault or the completed session.

exercises.prompt: Which point is still under investigation?
options: The factors behind the equipment problem
Whether Bao has been assigned the summary
exercises.explain: Yamamoto explicitly says 要因はまだ調査中.

exercises.prompt: What remains unchanged despite restoration?
options: The Saturday film will start on Monday
The information session starts at four
exercises.explain: 運行が復旧しても leaves the four-o’clock decision unchanged.

exercises.prompt: What work does Bao agree to take on?
options: Write the summary and include the alternative route
Send only a photograph of the equipment
exercises.explain: Bao accepts the summary task and says he will include guidance on the alternative route.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun-cause pattern 停電のため.
exercises.line: {停電|ていでん}＿＿ため、{朝|あさ}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{運休|うんきゅう}でした。
exercises.explain: 停電 is a noun followed by のため; the reported outcome is cancellation, not a goal to create an outage.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named nominal reason 運休なので, not a synonym choice between から and ので.
exercises.line: {運休|うんきゅう}＿＿ので、{別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{教|おし}えてください。
exercises.explain: The noun 運休 uses なので in this pattern; the suitable request is permitted.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto-san: confirm that your summary will retain what is still unknown.
exercises.line: {分|わ}からないことも{省略|しょうりゃく}しないでください。
options: はい。{不明|ふめい}な{点|てん}も{要約|ようやく}に{入|い}れます。
まだ{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}ですが、{原因|げんいん}は{絶対|ぜったい}に{雷|かみなり}です。
うん、{先生|せんせい}の{本音|ほんね}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるよ。
exercises.explain: The first confirms the organizer’s request politely. The second asserts an unproved cause; the third guesses private thoughts and fails the requested style.

exercises.meaning: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.
exercises.explain: The outage is the reported cause; the cancelled morning service is the completed consequence.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: At the time of this update, what is true about the session?
options: It finished at three before the update
It’s still scheduled for four; the update is at three
It has returned to the original morning time
exercises.explain: Three is the update time; four remains the start after service restoration.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: What conclusion does the report refuse to establish from the thunder alone?
options: That thunder occurred on the same night
That train service was cancelled in the morning
That it caused the equipment problem
exercises.explain: Same-night thunder is reported, but 因果関係 remains unsupported; the other two statements are explicit.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: Which action is still planned before the four-o’clock start?
options: Restoring the already completed Saturday film
exercises.explain: The report says 開始前に再び案内する; prior contact is already complete.

lessons.title: A span, an interruption and each update
lessons.description: Track a whole session, an event inside it and repeated checks.
lessons.canDo: Follow time spans and recurring events

lessons.title: A repeated habit and a slight state
lessons.description: Follow diary dates and choose a practical way to reduce omissions.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish a recurring tendency from a described state

grammar.title: Track what happens each time
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + たびに; event noun + のたびに.
grammar.explanation: Links an event to a response on each occurrence. Yamamoto checks the inspection record whenever a service update arrives. Compare a recurring event with a single completed Monday update. Emotional response is possible, not required; the expression is not an arbitrary clock interval.
grammar.example: 更新のたびに、点検の記録を確認します。
grammar.translation: Each time there is an update, I check the inspection record.

examples.ja: {更新|こうしん}のたびに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: Each time there is an update, I check the inspection record.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}むたびに、{新|あたら}しいことに{気|き}づきます。
examples.en: Each time I read the same sentence, I notice something new.

examples.ja: {予定|よてい}が{変|か}わるたびに、{参加者|さんかしゃ}に{伝|つた}えます。
examples.en: Whenever the schedule changes, I tell the participants.

grammar.mistake: Use 更新のたびに, not 更新たびに. A dictionary verb precedes たびに even when describing past repeated occasions; tense of the main clause can be past. One observation is not proof of a recurring habit.

grammar.title: A whole span, an event within it, and full progress
grammar.formation: Interval: attributive verb/い-adjective; noun の; な-adjective な + 間(に). Full progress: verb ている or noun の + 最中に; predicate 最中だ.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 intervals. 間 can frame activity continuing throughout a span; 間に places an event or completion inside it. 最中に emphasises being right in the middle of an action, often with an interruption. It need not always mean interruption. Another action taking some time inside the span is allowed; avoid a false instantaneous-only rule.
grammar.example: 説明会の間、私はずっとメモを取っていました。
grammar.translation: I took notes throughout the information session.

examples.ja: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、{私|わたし}はずっとメモを{取|と}っていました。
examples.en: I took notes throughout the information session.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{間|あいだ}に、{要約|ようやく}を{読|よ}み{終|お}えました。
examples.en: During the break, I finished reading the summary.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}している{最中|さいちゅう}に、{着信|ちゃくしん}がありました。
examples.en: An incoming call arrived right in the middle of the explanation.

grammar.mistake: Use ている最中, not dictionary-form 説明する最中 in the construction taught here. Name a construction when testing attachment; no claim that all near-synonyms are unacceptable.

grammar.title: Use a window before it changes; notice gradual change
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary/ている/ない + うちに; い-adjective + うちに; な-adjective な; noun の.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve unit 2: act while a condition persists or before it changes. Negative 忘れないうちに means before forgetting. In another use, a change gradually occurs while doing something repeatedly. うちに doesn’t always express a deliberate opportunity; read whether the main clause is a planned act or an emerging change.
grammar.example: 内容を忘れないうちに、要約を書きました。
grammar.translation: I wrote the summary before I forgot the content.

examples.ja: {内容|ないよう}を{忘|わす}れないうちに、{要約|ようやく}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote the summary before I forgot the content.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かなうちに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}みましょう。
examples.en: Let’s read the inspection record while it’s quiet.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}んでいるうちに、{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かるようになりました。
examples.en: As I continued reading the same sentence, I came to understand its meaning.

grammar.mistake: 静かなうちに uses な; noun + の. Do not translate 忘れないうちに as after forgetting. The gradual-change use need not imply an intentional deadline.

grammar.title: A recurring tendency is not an identity
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem/noun + がち; predicate がちだ/です; modifier がちな or がちの where idiomatic.
grammar.explanation: Describe a propensity, usually an unwanted one. Kenta reports repeatedly leaving things out when hurried, rather than just one Monday event. がち is often negative but not absolutely restricted to negative events. Dates and words such as よく clarify how often something happens. Its focus can overlap with 気味, so attachment tasks name the target.
grammar.example: 急ぐと、説明を省略しがちです。
grammar.translation: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.

examples.ja: {急|いそ}ぐと、{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しがちです。
examples.en: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.

examples.ja: {大切|たいせつ}なことを{忘|わす}れがちなので、メモを{取|と}ります。
examples.en: I tend to forget important things, so I take notes.

examples.ja: {欠席|けっせき}がちな{時期|じき}がありました。
examples.en: There was a period when I was often absent.

grammar.mistake: 省略します→省略しがち, not 省略するがち. Look for repeated events in the context. がち versus 気味 is not a universally exclusive choice.

grammar.title: A slight state or sign in the speaker’s account
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem/noun + 気味 (suffix read ぎみ); predicate 気味だ/です; common modifier 気味の and adverb 気味に.
grammar.explanation: Describes a mild sign, state or inclination. Kenta says he felt a little tired yesterday. That differs in focus from his repeated omission habit, but 気味 is not universally temporary and がち not universally permanent. Use the surrounding dates, repetition words and speaker’s description to follow the intended meaning.
grammar.example: 昨日は疲れ気味でした。
grammar.translation: I felt a little tired yesterday.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}でした。
examples.en: I felt a little tired yesterday.

examples.ja: {作業|さぎょう}は{遅|おく}れ{気味|ぎみ}ですが、{四時|よじ}までに{終|お}わります。
examples.en: The work is running a little behind, but it will finish by four.

examples.ja: {寝不足|ねぶそく}{気味|ぎみ}だったと、{本人|ほんにん}が{話|はな}しました。
examples.en: The person said they were somewhat short on sleep.

grammar.mistake: 疲れます→疲れ気味, not 疲れる気味. Read the suffix ぎみ; standalone 気味 has different readings/uses. Choose the named attachment, and retain self-report attribution.

dialogues.title: What happened during the session
dialogues.scene: Tuesday morning, Bao and Yamamoto review Monday’s information session, which began at four as announced. They distinguish ongoing note-taking from one phone call handled by a colleague.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}の{説明会|せつめいかい}は、{予定|よてい}どおり{四時|よじ}に{始|はじ}まりました。{今朝|けさ}は{記録|きろく}を{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}りましょう。
lines.romaji: Kinō no setsumeikai wa, yotei dōri yoji ni hajimarimashita. Kesa wa kiroku o furikaerimashō.
lines.meaning: Yesterday’s information session began at four as scheduled. Let’s review the record this morning.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、{私|わたし}はずっとメモを{取|と}っていました。
lines.romaji: Setsumeikai no aida, watashi wa zutto memo o totte imashita.
lines.meaning: I took notes throughout the session.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {設備|せつび}について{説明|せつめい}している{最中|さいちゅう}に、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}りましたね。
lines.romaji: Setsubi ni tsuite setsumei shite iru saichū ni, denwa ga narimashita ne.
lines.meaning: The phone rang right in the middle of the explanation about the equipment, didn’t it?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{別|べつ}の{人|ひと}が{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}てくれたので、メモを{続|つづ}けられました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Betsu no hito ga denwa ni dete kureta node, memo o tsuzukeraremashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. Someone else answered, so I could keep taking notes.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {休|やす}みの{間|あいだ}に、{要約|ようやく}を{読|よ}み{終|お}えたんですね。
lines.romaji: Yasumi no aida ni, yōyaku o yomioeta n desu ne.
lines.meaning: You finished reading the summary during the break, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{内容|ないよう}を{忘|わす}れないうちに、{不具合|ふぐあい}の{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だと{書|か}きました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Naiyō o wasurenai uchi ni, fuguai no yōin wa chōsa chū da to kakimashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. Before I forgot the content, I wrote that the factors behind the malfunction were under investigation.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {運行|うんこう}の{更新|こうしん}のたびに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}も{毎回|まいかい}{確認|かくにん}しています。
lines.romaji: Unkō no kōshin no tabi ni, tenken no kiroku mo maikai kakunin shite imasu.
lines.meaning: Each time there is a service update, I check the inspection record too, every time.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{再開|さいかい}した{時間|じかん}も{書|か}いておきました。{読|よ}んでいただけますか？
lines.romaji: Hai. Saikai shita jikan mo kaite okimashita. Yonde itadakemasu ka?
lines.meaning: I’ve included the resumption time too. Could you read it?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {連絡|れんらく}の{頻度|ひんど}も{記録|きろく}しましょう。{朝|あさ}の{確認|かくにん}は{日課|にっか}にしています。
lines.romaji: Renraku no hindo mo kiroku shimashō. Asa no kakunin wa nikka ni shite imasu.
lines.meaning: Let’s record the frequency of contact too. I make the morning check a daily routine.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとうございます。{同|おな}じ{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}んでいるうちに、{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かるようになりました。
lines.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Onaji bun o yonde iru uchi ni, imi ga wakaru yō ni narimashita.
lines.meaning: Thanks. As I kept reading the sentence, I started to understand it.

dialogues.title: A repeated habit and yesterday’s tiredness
dialogues.scene: Tuesday after lunch, Kenta and Misaki compare a repeated communication habit with Kenta’s description of yesterday. Bao suggests a concrete way to keep the summary complete.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {急|いそ}ぐと、{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しがちなんだ。{先週|せんしゅう}は{三日|みっか}{連続|れんぞく}で、{毎回|まいかい}{一|ひと}つずつ{抜|ぬ}けた。
lines.romaji: Isogu to, setsumei o shōryaku shigachi nan da. Senshū wa mikka renzoku de, maikai hitotsu zutsu nuketa.
lines.meaning: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations. Last week, for three consecutive days, I left one thing out each time.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {急|いそ}いでると、つい{忘|わす}れちゃうよね。メモを{置|お}いといたら？
lines.romaji: Isoideru to, tsui wasurechau yo ne. Memo o oitoitara?
lines.meaning: It’s easy to forget when you’re rushing. How about keeping a note nearby?

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: うん。{昨日|きのう}は{寝不足|ねぶそく}で、{疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}だったし。{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}りたいな。
lines.romaji: Un. Kinō wa nebusoku de, tsukare gimi datta shi. Kyō wa hayaku kaeritai na.
lines.meaning: Yeah. I was short on sleep yesterday and a bit tired too. I’d like to go home early today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {省略|しょうりゃく}を{減|へ}らすために、{要約|ようやく}を{送|おく}る{前|まえ}に、{確認|かくにん}する{項目|こうもく}を{読|よ}みましょう。
lines.romaji: Shōryaku o herasu tame ni, yōyaku o okuru mae ni, kakunin suru kōmoku o yomimashō.
lines.meaning: To reduce omissions, let’s read the checklist before sending the summary.

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {一回|いっかい}で{済|す}めば、{後|あと}が{楽|らく}だよ。{私|わたし}も{手伝|てつだ}うね。

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {日記|にっき}には、{休息|きゅうそく}を{取|と}った{時刻|じこく}と{間隔|かんかく}も{残|のこ}した。
lines.romaji: Nikki ni wa, kyūsoku o totta jikoku to kankaku mo nokoshita.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {作業|さぎょう}の{合間|あいま}に{書|か}いたんですね。{忙|いそが}しいのに、よく{覚|おぼ}えてましたね。

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: うん。{昨日|きのう}は{少|すこ}し{疲|つか}れていたけど、{四時|よじ}の{説明会|せつめいかい}には{参加|さんか}した。{欠席|けっせき}はしなかったよ。

lines.meaning: Yes. I was a little tired yesterday, but I attended the four-o’clock session. I didn’t miss it.

readings.title: A whole session; three days of omissions
paragraphs: {火曜日|かようび}の{日記|にっき}。{昨日|きのう}の{説明会|せつめいかい}は{四時|よじ}に{始|はじ}まった。{設備|せつび}の{説明|せつめい}の{最中|さいちゅう}に{着信|ちゃくしん}があったが、{応答|おうとう}は{別|べつ}の{人|ひと}が{担当|たんとう}した。{私|わたし}は{説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、ずっとメモを{取|と}った。{休|やす}みの{間|あいだ}に{要約|ようやく}を{読|よ}み{終|お}え、{忘|わす}れないうちに{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だと{書|か}いた。

{今日|きょう}の{昼|ひる}、ケンタは{先週|せんしゅう}{三日|みっか}{連続|れんぞく}で{説明|せつめい}を{一|ひと}つずつ{省略|しょうりゃく}したと{話|はな}した。{昨日|きのう}は{疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}だったが、{説明会|せつめいかい}には{参加|さんか}したとも{言|い}った。{要約|ようやく}を{送|おく}るたびに{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}することにした。{確認|かくにん}の{手間|てま}を{省|はぶ}かない{方法|ほうほう}だ。{相手|あいて}への{心|こころ}{配|くば}りを、{具体的|ぐたいてき}な{行動|こうどう}にしたい。

glosses.kana: かくにんすることにした

watch.prompt: Optionally save a time-span or habit line from your own clip. Mark the time clues and whether it describes one event, repetition, or a slight state.

exercises.prompt: Which activity did Bao continue throughout the session?
options: Reading the summary only after the session
exercises.explain: ずっとメモを取っていました states ongoing note-taking across the session.

exercises.prompt: Who answered the incoming call?
exercises.explain: Bao says 別の人が担当した, so he could continue taking notes.

exercises.prompt: What did Bao complete during the break?
options: Finding all causes of the malfunction
exercises.explain: 読み終えた marks the completed reading within the break, not all causes becoming known.

exercises.prompt: When does Yamamoto check the inspection record?
options: Each time there is a service update
Only after the four-o’clock session ends
Only on the day of the Saturday film
exercises.explain: 更新のたびに and 毎回 mark repeated checks.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named event-noun pattern 更新のたびに.
exercises.line: {更新|こうしん}＿＿たびに、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: The event noun 更新 connects with のたびに.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the verb pattern 説明している最中に, meaning right in the middle of explaining.
exercises.line: {設備|せつび}について{説明|せつめい}＿＿{最中|さいちゅう}に、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}りました。
exercises.explain: The taught progressive attachment is ている最中に.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto-san. Agree to write the summary before you forget the content.
exercises.line: {忘|わす}れないうちに、{要約|ようやく}を{書|か}いてください。
options: はい。{今|いま}、{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だと{書|か}きます。
{全部|ぜんぶ}{忘|わす}れた{後|あと}で、{初|はじ}めて{書|か}きます。
{要因|よういん}は{不明|ふめい}ですが、{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったと{書|か}きます。
exercises.explain: The first acts now before forgetting and retains the stated investigation status.

exercises.meaning: I took notes throughout the information session.
tiles: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{間|あいだ}、
メモを{取|と}っていました。
exercises.explain: 間 and ずっと frame the continuing note-taking across the session.

exercises.prompt: What repeated pattern does Kenta describe?
options: Leaving one explanation out each day for three consecutive days last week
Forgetting everything just once on Tuesday
exercises.explain: 先週は三日連続で、毎回一つずつ describes the recurrence.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta say about yesterday?
options: He omitted one explanation every hour
He was short on sleep and felt somewhat tired
exercises.explain: 寝不足 and 疲れ気味 report yesterday’s state, distinct from last week’s habit.

exercises.prompt: Did Kenta attend Monday’s session?
options: Yes, he attended at four despite feeling tired
The scene never states whether he attended
exercises.explain: He explicitly says 参加した and 欠席はしなかった.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 省略します with the named suffix がち, to express a tendency to omit explanations.
exercises.line: {急|いそ}ぐと、{説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}＿＿がちです。
exercises.explain: The ます-stem of 省略します is 省略し; remove ます.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 疲れます with the named suffix 気味 (ぎみ), to describe mild tiredness.
exercises.line: {昨日|きのう}は{疲|つか}れ＿＿でした。
exercises.explain: 疲れ is the stem; 疲れ気味 describes being somewhat tired.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Kenta. Suggest a concrete check before he sends the summary.
exercises.line: {説明|せつめい}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しがちなんだ。
options: {送|おく}る{前|まえ}に、{点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}と{要約|ようやく}を{比|くら}べよう。
{昨日|きのう}は{欠席|けっせき}したから、{記録|きろく}はないね。
{確認|かくにん}の{手間|てま}は{必|かなら}ず{省|はぶ}こう。
exercises.explain: The first suggests comparing the record and summary; the second contradicts his attendance and the third removes the needed check.

exercises.meaning: When I hurry, I tend to leave out explanations.
tiles: {省略|しょうりゃく}しがちです。
exercises.explain: The condition precedes the recurring tendency; the verb stem attaches to がち.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: Which event belongs to Monday rather than Tuesday?
options: Kenta’s lunchtime account of last week
exercises.explain: Yesterday refers to Monday in the Tuesday diary.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: Which statement describes repeated actions last week?
options: Bao finished the summary during one break
A single call arrived during Monday’s explanation
Kenta omitted one explanation on each of three consecutive days
exercises.explain: 三日連続 and 一つずつ establish recurrence; the other events happen once.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Tuesday diary. Follow the dates and the attributed statements.
exercises.prompt: What new practice has been decided?
options: Check the inspection record each time a summary is sent
Skip the checking effort when tired
State that all causes are now known
exercises.explain: 送るたびに…確認することにした connects each send to the decided check.

words.example: 主催者の承諾を得てから、発表します。
施設の認可について資料を読みます。
管理者は室内での閲覧を許しました。
仕事の委任について確認します。
私には公開を決める権限がありません。
参加は自由で、強制ではありません。
依頼と命令の違いを考えます。
管理者の指示に従います。
協力の要請を受けました。

words.meaning: to impose; to force onto someone
words.example: 自分の仕事を相手に押し付けません。

words.meaning: to take over; to hand over
words.example: 来週、担当者から仕事を引き継ぎます。
議事録に決まったことを書きます。
資料の配布は、まだ認められていません。
複写は一部だけ許されました。
閲覧は室内だけです。

words.meaning: to take out; to bring up
words.example: 記録を部屋の外へ持ち出しません。
使った資料は保管する場所へ戻しました。
名前を消した匿名の記録です。
この記録は非公開です。

words.meaning: public release; opening to the public
words.example: 公開する前に、管理者に確認します。
相手の同意を確かめます。
担当者に連絡しました。
管理者が閲覧の範囲を決めました。
主催者は森さんです。
今日の司会は私が担当します。
進行役が次の発表者を呼びました。

words.meaning: attending a lecture as a listener
words.example: 聴講の申し込みをしました。
開始時刻の記載を確認します。
内容を読んでから署名します。
この書類には署名だけでよく、押印は不要です。

words.meaning: to offer; to make a request
words.example: 発表したいと申し出ました。
記録の撮影は控えます。

lessons.title: Ask for the opportunity to act
lessons.description: Request a practice slot and follow the response and its limits.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish your permission request from a request for the listener’s action

lessons.title: Granted, completed, or made to do it
lessons.description: Follow the actors in a past report and recognize causative-passive speech.
lessons.canDo: Track who acts and whether permission or compulsion is expressed

grammar.title: Ask to do the action yourself
grammar.formation: Causative te-form + ください: 説明する→説明させてください; 読む→読ませてください; 見る→見させてください. The actor is identified in context; 私に can make the intended doer explicit.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve N4 causative formation in a real request. 説明させてください asks the organizer to let you explain. 説明してください asks the listener to explain. The request comes before the response, so it doesn’t itself establish permission. Polite wording can still sound direct; a permission question may better fit a formal request.
grammar.example: 明日の練習で、私に要約を説明させてください。
grammar.translation: Please let me explain the summary at tomorrow’s practice.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{練習|れんしゅう}で、{私|わたし}に{要約|ようやく}を{説明|せつめい}させてください。
examples.en: Please let me explain the summary at tomorrow’s practice.

examples.ja: {点検|てんけん}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませてください。
examples.en: Please let me read the inspection record.

examples.ja: {返事|へんじ}の{前|まえ}に、{少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えさせてください。
examples.en: Please let me think a little before answering.

grammar.mistake: 読む→読ませて, not 読むさせて. Do not swap the speaker’s requested action with the listener’s action. An omitted actor can be clear from context.

grammar.title: Ask for permission; report the granted opportunity
grammar.formation: Causative te-form + もらう/いただく. Formal question: いただけますか/いただけませんか. Past report: いただきました. 説明させてもらう→説明させていただく.
grammar.explanation: The speaker receives permission or the opportunity to act. In this unit Mori controls the practice slot and the manager controls document access. させていただく fits that permission and the speaker’s benefit. Its longer wording is not an automatic improvement over します/いたします; contextual or inferred permission affects how natural it sounds. Keep a request, a granted scope and a completed action separate.
grammar.example: 明日の練習で、説明させていただけませんか。
grammar.translation: Could you please allow me to explain at tomorrow’s practice?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{練習|れんしゅう}で、{説明|せつめい}させていただけませんか。
examples.en: Could you please allow me to explain at tomorrow’s practice?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}の{承諾|しょうだく}を{得|え}て、{発表|はっぴょう}させていただきました。
examples.en: With the teacher’s consent, I had the opportunity to give the presentation.

examples.ja: {室内|しつない}で{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませていただきました。
examples.en: I was allowed to read the record inside the room.

grammar.mistake: 読ませていただく describes your reading; 読んでいただく describes the other person reading for you. いただけませんか asks; いただきました reports a past opportunity.

grammar.title: Follow the grantor and the doer
grammar.formation: Retrieve causative: group 1 a-row + せる (う→わせる), group 2 drop る + させる, する→させる, 来る→こさせる. With an object: grantor は doer に object を causative. Passive: 許す→許される; agent に.
grammar.explanation: The causative can describe letting or making someone act. The manager’s actual approval makes the document example permission. In 管理者は私に記録を読ませました, the manager grants it and I read. In 閲覧は許されました, viewing is the permitted action; the actor is not specified by that passive clause alone. Identify the participants from the full message.
grammar.example: 管理者は私に記録を読ませました。
grammar.translation: The manager let me read the record.

examples.ja: {管理者|かんりしゃ}は{私|わたし}に{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませました。
examples.en: The manager let me read the record.

examples.ja: {匿名|とくめい}の{記録|きろく}の{閲覧|えつらん}は{許|ゆる}されました。
examples.en: Viewing of the anonymized record was permitted.

examples.ja: {複写|ふくしゃ}は{一部|いちぶ}だけ{許|ゆる}されました。
examples.en: Only one copy was permitted.

grammar.mistake: Keep the object を and doer に in the transitive pattern. A permission to view or make one copy doesn’t mean permission to distribute it.

grammar.title: Recognise being made to act
grammar.formation: Causative final る→られる: 読ませる→読ませられる, 見させる→見させられる, する→させられる, 来る→こさせられる. Common group 1 contraction: 待たせられる→待たされる. Do not apply that contraction to す-ending verbs, group 2 verbs or する. Causer に; doer は/が.
grammar.explanation: The viewpoint changes to the person made to perform an action, often against their wishes. Contrast voluntary permission with Kenta’s report of having to wait. Emotional responses can also be elicited: 考えさせられる can mean something makes you think, rather than someone issuing an order. Context determines that interpretation.
grammar.example: 先週、受付で一時間も待たされました。
grammar.translation: Last week, I was made to wait a whole hour at reception.

examples.ja: {先週|せんしゅう}、{受付|うけつけ}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たされました。
examples.en: Last week, I was made to wait a whole hour at reception.

examples.ja: {同|おな}じ{説明|せつめい}を{何度|なんど}も{読|よ}ませられました。
examples.en: I was made to read the same explanation over and over.

examples.ja: その{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{相手|あいて}への{心|こころ}{配|くば}りについて{考|かんが}えさせられました。
examples.en: Hearing that story made me think about consideration for others.

grammar.mistake: 待たされる is causative-passive, not 待たせてもらう (being allowed to wait). Full and contracted forms can both be grammatical; test the named form or the actor roles, not an unsupported register ban.

dialogues.title: A slot to explain; permission to consult
dialogues.scene: Tuesday afternoon, Bao asks Mori, the organizer, for a Wednesday practice slot. The administrator has already approved limited access to an anonymized inspection record; Mori conveys the limits.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {森|もり}さん、{明日|あした}の{練習|れんしゅう}で、{私|わたし}に{点検|てんけん}の{要約|ようやく}を{説明|せつめい}させていただけませんか。
lines.romaji: Mori-san, ashita no renshū de, watashi ni tenken no yōyaku o setsumei sasete itadakemasen ka.
lines.meaning: Mori-san, could you allow me to explain the inspection summary at tomorrow’s practice?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: いいですよ。{水曜日|すいようび}の{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}から、{十分|じゅっぷん}でお{願|ねが}いします。
lines.romaji: Ii desu yo. Suiyōbi no gogo sanji kara, juppun de onegai shimasu.
lines.meaning: Of course. Wednesday at three, for ten minutes, please.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとうございます。{設備|せつび}の{不具合|ふぐあい}の{要因|よういん}と、{連絡|れんらく}の{頻度|ひんど}を{省略|しょうりゃく}しないようにします。
lines.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Setsubi no fuguai no yōin to, renraku no hindo o shōryaku shinai yō ni shimasu.
lines.meaning: Thank you. I’ll try not to leave out the factors behind the equipment problem or the frequency of contact.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {要因|よういん}はまだ{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}です。{更新|こうしん}のたびに{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}する、という{日課|にっか}も{説明|せつめい}してください。
lines.romaji: Yōin wa mada chōsa chū desu. Kōshin no tabi ni kiroku o kakunin suru, to iu nikka mo setsumei shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: The factors are still under investigation. Also explain the routine of checking the record each time there is an update.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{準備|じゅんび}のために、{匿名|とくめい}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませていただけますか。
lines.romaji: Hai. Junbi no tame ni, tokumei no kiroku o yomasete itadakemasu ka.
lines.meaning: Yes. Could I be allowed to read the anonymized record to prepare?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {管理者|かんりしゃ}の{承諾|しょうだく}は{得|え}ています。{閲覧|えつらん}はこの{部屋|へや}の{中|なか}だけで、{複写|ふくしゃ}は{一部|いちぶ}だけです。
lines.romaji: Kanrisha no shōdaku wa ete imasu. Etsuran wa kono heya no naka dake de, fukusha wa ichibu dake desu.
lines.meaning: I have obtained the administrator’s consent. Viewing is only inside this room, and only one copy is allowed.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {分|わ}かりました。{外|そと}には{持|も}ち{出|だ}さず、{撮影|さつえい}も{控|ひか}えます。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Soto ni wa mochidasazu, satsuei mo hikaemasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. I’ll keep it in the room and won’t take photographs.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: この{記録|きろく}は{非公開|ひこうかい}です。{私|わたし}には{公開|こうかい}を{決|き}める{権限|けんげん}がないので、{配布|はいふ}はしないでください。
lines.romaji: Kono kiroku wa hikōkai desu. Watashi ni wa kōkai o kimeru kengen ga nai node, haifu wa shinai de kudasai.
lines.meaning: This record is not public. I don’t have authority to decide its release, so please don’t distribute it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{資料|しりょう}はここに{戻|もど}せばいいですか？
lines.romaji: Hai. Shiryō wa koko ni modoseba ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: Should I put the papers back here afterward?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい、ここで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。では、{明日|あした}の{説明|せつめい}をお{願|ねが}いします。
lines.romaji: Hai, koko de daijōbu desu. De wa, ashita no setsumei o onegai shimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes, here is fine. I’m looking forward to your explanation tomorrow.

dialogues.title: The completed presentation and the copied record
dialogues.scene: Thursday morning, Bao and Misaki review the Wednesday practice. Bao used the permitted record in the room and returned the copy. Misaki separately quotes Kenta’s account of a wait last week.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}の{練習|れんしゅう}はどうだった？ {三時|さんじ}から{説明|せつめい}したんだよね。
lines.romaji: Kinō no renshū wa dō datta? Sanji kara setsumei shita n da yo ne.
lines.meaning: How did yesterday’s practice go? You explained from three, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{森|もり}さんの{承諾|しょうだく}を{得|え}て、{十分|じゅっぷん}{発表|はっぴょう}させていただきました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Mori-san no shōdaku o ete, juppun happyō sasete itadakimashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. With Mori’s consent, I had the opportunity to present for ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {設備|せつび}の{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だって、{省略|しょうりゃく}せずに{伝|つた}えた？
lines.romaji: Setsubi no yōin wa chōsa chū datte, shōryaku sezu ni tsutaeta?
lines.meaning: Did you say, without leaving it out, that the factors behind the equipment issue are under investigation?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{点検|てんけん}の{要約|ようやく}に{入|い}れました。{管理者|かんりしゃ}は{私|わたし}に{匿名|とくめい}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませてくれました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Tenken no yōyaku ni iremashita. Kanrisha wa watashi ni tokumei no kiroku o yomasete kuremashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. I included it in the inspection summary. The administrator let me read the anonymized record.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {閲覧|えつらん}と{複写|ふくしゃ}は{許|ゆる}されたけど、{配布|はいふ}はまだだよね。
lines.romaji: Etsuran to fukusha wa yurusareta kedo, haifu wa mada da yo ne.
lines.meaning: Viewing and copying were permitted, but distribution still wasn’t, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{室内|しつない}で{一部|いちぶ}だけ{複写|ふくしゃ}し、{使|つか}った{後|あと}で{保管|ほかん}する{場所|ばしょ}へ{戻|もど}しました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Shitsunai de ichibu dake fukusha shi, tsukatta ato de hokan suru basho e modoshimashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. I made just one copy inside the room and returned it to its storage place after use.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {議事録|ぎじろく}にも{書|か}こう。ケンタは{先週|せんしゅう}、{受付|うけつけ}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たされたと{話|はな}していたよ。
lines.romaji: Gijiroku ni mo kakō. Kenta wa senshū, uketsuke de ichijikan mo matasareta to hanashite ita yo.
lines.meaning: Let’s record it in the minutes too. Kenta said he was made to wait a whole hour at reception last week.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {一時間|いちじかん}もですか。ずいぶん{待|ま}たされたんですね。
lines.romaji: Ichijikan mo desu ka. Zuibun matasareta n desu ne.
lines.meaning: A whole hour? They kept him waiting a long time.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{予定|よてい}より{遅|おそ}くなって、お{昼|ひる}も{食|た}べられなかったんだって。
lines.romaji: Un. Yotei yori osoku natte, ohiru mo taberarenakatta n datte.
lines.meaning: Yeah. It ran so late he couldn’t even have lunch, apparently.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: それは{大変|たいへん}でしたね。{待|ま}つ{人|ひと}のことも{考|かんが}えさせられました。
lines.romaji: Sore wa taihen deshita ne. Matsu hito no koto mo kangaesaseraremashita.
lines.meaning: That sounds rough. It made me think about the people left waiting.

readings.title: Thanks for the slot; the copy has been returned
paragraphs: {森|もり}さんへ。{木曜日|もくようび}の{朝|あさ}の{報告|ほうこく}です。{昨日|きのう}は{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}から{十分|じゅっぷん}、{点検|てんけん}の{要約|ようやく}を{発表|はっぴょう}させていただき、ありがとうございました。{設備|せつび}の{不具合|ふぐあい}の{要因|よういん}は{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}だと{伝|つた}えました。{更新|こうしん}のたびに{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}する{日課|にっか}も{説明|せつめい}しました。

{管理者|かんりしゃ}の{承諾|しょうだく}を{得|え}て、{室内|しつない}で{匿名|とくめい}の{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませていただきました。{複写|ふくしゃ}は{一部|いちぶ}だけ{行|おこな}い、{使用|しよう}{後|ご}に{保管|ほかん}する{場所|ばしょ}へ{戻|もど}しました。{外|そと}へは{持|も}ち{出|だ}していません。{非公開|ひこうかい}なので、{撮影|さつえい}も{配布|はいふ}もしていません。
{議事録|ぎじろく}の{記載|きさい}は、{送|おく}る{前|まえ}にもう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}します。{今後|こんご}も{指示|しじ}に{従|したが}い、{相手|あいて}への{心|こころ}{配|くば}りを{忘|わす}れずに{準備|じゅんび}します。バオ

glosses.meaning: having been allowed to present; linking

glosses.kana: よませていただきました

grammar: receiving permission させてもらう/いただく
watch.prompt: Optionally save a permission or causative line from your own clip. Identify who acts, who gives the permission, and whether the line asks, grants, or reports it.

exercises.prompt: Which slot does the organizer grant?
options: Wednesday at three for ten minutes
Monday at four for an hour
exercises.explain: The request is on Tuesday; Mori explicitly grants Wednesday afternoon three for ten minutes.

exercises.prompt: Who is asking to read the anonymized record?
options: Mori, asking Bao to read it for him
exercises.explain: Bao’s 読ませていただけますか requests permission for his own reading.

exercises.prompt: What access has the administrator approved?
options: Taking it outside and distributing unlimited copies
Photographing it and publishing it online
Viewing inside the room and making one copy
exercises.explain: Mori states room-only viewing and one copy; distribution and photography are excluded.

exercises.context: Form practice: request permission for your own explanation, using the named causative request 説明させてください.
exercises.line: {私|わたし}に{要約|ようやく}を{説明|せつめい}＿＿ください。
exercises.explain: する→させる→させて. してください would ask the listener to explain.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 読む in the named causative-te permission request 読ませていただけますか.
exercises.line: {記録|きろく}を{読|よ}＿＿せていただけますか。
exercises.explain: 読む is group 1: 読ませる, then 読ませて.

exercises.context: Mori asks YOU to explain the routine at practice. Confirm politely that you will do it.
exercises.line: {日課|にっか}も{説明|せつめい}してください。
options: では、{森|もり}さんが{私|わたし}の{代|か}わりに{発表|はっぴょう}するんですね。
{記録|きろく}は{自由|じゆう}に{公開|こうかい}できますね。
はい。{更新|こうしん}のたびに{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}すると{説明|せつめい}します。
exercises.explain: The first confirms your action. The second reverses the actor; the third enlarges permission beyond the stated scope.

exercises.meaning: Please let me explain the inspection summary at tomorrow’s practice.
tiles: {明日|あした}の{練習|れんしゅう}で、
{点検|てんけん}の{要約|ようやく}を
{説明|せつめい}させてください。
exercises.explain: The event and explicit actor precede the object and causative permission request.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao report as already completed?
options: The ten-minute Wednesday presentation with Mori’s consent
A new request for next Friday
A one-hour Thursday presentation without permission
exercises.explain: Yesterday in the Thursday scene is Wednesday; いただきました is the past report.

exercises.prompt: What happened to the single copy after use?
options: It was given to every participant
It was returned to its storage place
It was taken outside for photographs
exercises.explain: Bao says 使った後で…戻しました, after making one copy inside the room.

exercises.prompt: What does Misaki report about Kenta’s separate event last week?
options: He voluntarily received permission to publish the record
He omitted all explanations during Wednesday’s presentation
He was made to wait a whole hour at reception
exercises.explain: 待たされた describes the reported wait, distinct from the three-day omission story.

exercises.context: Form practice: after granted permission and a completed presentation, report the past opportunity using いただく.
exercises.line: {森|もり}さんの{承諾|しょうだく}を{得|え}て、{発表|はっぴょう}させて＿＿。
exercises.explain: いただきました is the past report; いただけませんか asks for permission.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named contracted causative-passive 待たされました from 待つ.
exercises.line: {受付|うけつけ}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}＿＿。
exercises.explain: 待たせられる contracts to 待たされる. The named form reports being made to wait, not receiving permission.

exercises.context: The administrator asks you to return the copy after use. Reply politely and confirm that you already returned it.
exercises.line: {使|つか}った{後|あと}で、{資料|しりょう}を{戻|もど}してください。
options: はい。{全員|ぜんいん}に{配布|はいふ}してから、{外|そと}へ{持|も}ち{出|だ}します。
いいえ。{読|よ}ませていただいたので、{返|かえ}す{必要|ひつよう}はありません。
はい。{使用|しよう}{後|ご}に、{保管|ほかん}する{場所|ばしょ}へ{戻|もど}しました。
exercises.explain: The first confirms the requested completed return; permitted reading doesn’t remove the return instruction.

exercises.meaning: The administrator let me read the anonymized inspection record.
tiles: {匿名|とくめい}の{点検|てんけん}{記録|きろく}を
exercises.explain: The grantor is topic, the doer に, the record object を, then causative plus granted favour.

exercises.context: Speak formally to the administrator who controls access. Ask permission for YOU to read the record; don’t ask them to read it.
exercises.line: {記録|きろく}を{読|よ}みたいです。
options: {記録|きろく}を{読|よ}ませていただけませんか。
{記録|きろく}を{読|よ}んでいただけませんか。
exercises.explain: The first is the stated formal permission request for your action. The second requests their reading; the third is casual.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Thursday report to Mori. Separate completed actions from future checks.
exercises.prompt: When did the presentation take place?
exercises.explain: The email is Thursday morning and calls the presentation 昨日.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Thursday report to Mori. Separate completed actions from future checks.
exercises.prompt: Which statement is supported by the report?
options: The record was distributed to the public
Photography was permitted by the organizer
One copy was made in the room and returned after use
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly states one copy, its return, and no photography or distribution.

exercises.context: Read Bao’s Thursday report to Mori. Separate completed actions from future checks.
exercises.prompt: Which action is still planned before sending the minutes?
exercises.explain: The final paragraph says 送る前にもう一度確認します; the other actions are completed or disallowed.

words.example: 日本語の音声で見るので、吹き替えは選びません。
早口の台詞をもう一度聞きます。
話し言葉には短い形もあります。
長い名前を略して書きました。
休む時間は縮めません。
大事な場面を見逃しました。
最後の言葉を聞き逃しました。
十秒だけ巻き戻します。
十分ごとに一時停止します。

words.example: 友達とは、くだけた話し方をします。

words.example: 時間を間違えたので、言い直します。
主役は小さな声でつぶやきました。

lessons.title: Hear what the short forms contain
lessons.description: Get ready for an episode with Misaki, miss a trailer, and ask for a replay.
lessons.canDo: Hear preparation, ongoing actions and obligations in a relaxed conversation.

lessons.title: Recall, wonder and respond among peers
lessons.description: Chat with Kenta the next morning and arrange another viewing.
lessons.canDo: Recall a plan, react with じゃん and follow repeated casual contractions.

grammar.title: Hear the full verb inside a short ending
grammar.formation: Vてしまう→Vちゃう; Vでしまう→Vじゃう. Past ちゃった/じゃった.
grammar.explanation: Casual ちゃう/じゃう can describe finishing completely or an unintended outcome. Regret comes from the situation, not every use. Start with the verb’s te-form: 書いて→書いちゃう, 読んで→読んじゃう. These are common peer-speech contractions, not a separate set of verbs.
grammar.example: 早口の返事を聞き逃しちゃった。
grammar.translation: I missed the rapidly spoken reply.

examples.ja: {早口|はやくち}の{返事|へんじ}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃった。
examples.en: I missed the rapidly spoken reply.

examples.ja: {短|みじか}い{記事|きじ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}んじゃった。
examples.en: I finished reading the whole short article.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}は{先|さき}にしちゃおう。
examples.en: Let’s finish the preparation first.

grammar.mistake: Do not attach ちゃう to the masu stem: 読みちゃう is not the contraction of 読んでしまう.

grammar.title: Preparation and a current state sound different
grammar.formation: ておく→とく; でおく→どく. ている→てる; でいる→でる. といて/どいて are contracted te-forms.
grammar.explanation: とく keeps the preparation or leave-ready meaning of ておく; てる keeps the ongoing/resulting/habitual meaning of ている. Preserve て/で: 読んでおく→読んどく, 読んでいる→読んでる. Past 読んどいた and 読んでた remain different. Context tells whether でる comes from でいる or is the verb 出る.
grammar.example: 予告を先に見とくね。
grammar.translation: I’ll watch the preview beforehand.

examples.ja: {予告|よこく}を{先|さき}に{見|み}とくね。
examples.en: I’ll watch the preview beforehand.

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}を{聞|き}いてる。
examples.en: I’m listening to spoken language now.

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}は{先|さき}に{読|よ}んどいて。
examples.en: Please read the material beforehand.

grammar.mistake: 見とく is preparing, while 見てる is watching or an ongoing/resulting state. Do not collapse both into one meaning.

grammar.title: Recognise a shortened obligation
grammar.formation: Vない: replace ない with なきゃ or なくちゃ. Often omit following いけない/ならない/だめ. する→しなきゃ; 来る→こなきゃ.
grammar.explanation: A friend can end with 確認しなきゃ to say they need to check. なきゃ comes from なければ and なくちゃ from なくては in necessity expressions. Both are available to different speakers. They express a required action; they are not the prohibition てはいけない.
grammar.example: 始める前に、音量を確認しなきゃ。
grammar.translation: I need to check the volume before starting.

examples.ja: {始|はじ}める{前|まえ}に、{音量|おんりょう}を{確認|かくにん}しなきゃ。
examples.en: I need to check the volume before starting.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{早|はや}く{起|お}きなくちゃ。
examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

examples.ja: {七時|しちじ}までに{来|こ}なきゃ。
examples.en: I have to come by seven.

grammar.mistake: しなきゃ means need to do, not must not do. Use the negative base, not するなきゃ.

grammar.title: Remember a plan; wonder about an answer
grammar.formation: Recall: Vた+っけ; V+んだっけ; N/na-adj+だっけ/だったっけ. Wonder: plain V/i-adj+かな; N/na-adj+かな.
grammar.explanation: っけ asks yourself or a familiar listener to retrieve something you once knew, including a future arrangement. かな wonders about an unresolved thought, though it can also soften an utterance to a listener. The taught nonpast verb recall uses んだっけ. A recalled date is not automatically a past event.
grammar.example: 視聴は何時からだったっけ？
grammar.translation: What time was the viewing from again?

examples.ja: {視聴|しちょう}は{何時|なんじ}からだったっけ？
examples.en: What time was the viewing from again?

examples.ja: {来週|らいしゅう}も{集|あつ}まるんだっけ？
examples.en: Were we getting together next week too?

examples.ja: {語尾|ごび}まで{聞|き}き{取|と}れるかな。
examples.en: I wonder whether I can catch the ending too.

grammar.mistake: Do not treat every っけ question as an event already completed. For the taught noun + かな pattern, don’t insert だ.

grammar.title: A shared point and an explanatory question
grammar.formation: Statement+じゃん. Question: plain V/i-adj+の?; N/na-adj+なの? (rising delivery).
grammar.explanation: じゃん presents a point, reaction or shared confirmation among peers. It doesn’t negate the preceding statement like predicate じゃない. Rising の? asks about an explanation or situation: 見てるの？. Nouns/na-adjectives take な: 好きなの？. The same written の can appear in explanatory statements; context and delivery matter.
grammar.example: もう始まってるじゃん。
grammar.translation: Look, it’s already started!

examples.ja: もう{始|はじ}まってるじゃん。
examples.en: Look, it’s already started!

examples.ja: {続編|ぞくへん}も{見|み}るの？
examples.en: Are you watching the sequel too?

examples.ja: この{主役|しゅやく}が{好|す}きなの？
examples.en: Do you like this lead character?

grammar.mistake: Do not translate affirmative いいじゃん as not good, or confuse explanatory の? with a possessive noun link.

dialogues.title: A short Saturday viewing session
dialogues.scene: Saturday evening at home. Misaki and Bao get ready for the main feature at seven thirty. Bao misses the trailer while answering a phone call; Misaki rewinds it. They agree on normal speed and a pause every ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {本編|ほんぺん}は{七時半|しちじはん}からだったっけ？ {予告|よこく}、{先|さき}に{見|み}とく？
lines.romaji: Honpen wa shichijihan kara datta kke? Yokoku, saki ni mitoku?
lines.meaning: We said seven thirty for the main feature, right? Shall we watch the trailer first?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。あ、もう{始|はじ}まってるじゃん。{携帯|けいたい}、しまわなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Un. A, mō hajimatteru jan. Keitai, shimawanakya.
lines.meaning: Yeah. Oh, it’s already started! I need to put my phone away.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今|いま}の{台詞|せりふ}、{早口|はやくち}だったね。{十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに{一時停止|いちじていし}しとく？
lines.romaji: Ima no serifu, hayakuchi datta ne. Juppun goto ni ichiji teishi shitoku?
lines.meaning: That line was fast. Shall we make a point of pausing every ten minutes?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうしよう。{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃうから、{止|と}めた{所|ところ}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}して、もう{一度|いちど}{再生|さいせい}しなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Sō shiyō. Kikinogashichau kara, tometa tokoro o makimodoshite, mō ichido saisei shinakya.
lines.meaning: Let’s do that. I miss things, so I need to rewind where we stop and play it again.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今日|きょう}は{倍速|ばいそく}にしないで{見|み}よう。{音量|おんりょう}、{小|ちい}さくしとくね。
lines.romaji: Kyō wa baisoku ni shinai de miyō. Onryō, chiisaku shitoku ne.
lines.meaning: Let’s keep it at normal speed today. I’ll turn the volume down a bit.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: あれ、{主役|しゅやく}は{誰|だれ}だったっけ？ {脇役|わきやく}の{人|ひと}も{出|で}てるじゃん。
lines.romaji: Are, shuyaku wa dare datta kke? Wakiyaku no hito mo deteru jan.
lines.meaning: Wait, who was the lead again? Look, the supporting actor’s in this too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: え、{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃったの？ {今|いま}の{所|ところ}、{戻|もど}しとくよ。
lines.romaji: E, yokoku o minogashichatta no? Ima no tokoro, modoshitoku yo.
lines.meaning: Oh, did you miss the trailer? I’ll rewind that bit for you.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん、{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}てたんだ。もう{切|き}ったよ。{字幕|じまく}ばっかり{読|よ}んじゃうから、{今度|こんど}は{声|こえ}も{聞|き}かなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Un, denwa ni deteta n da. Mō kitta yo. Jimaku bakkari yonjau kara, kondo wa koe mo kikanakya.
lines.meaning: Yeah, I was on the phone. I’ve hung up now. I keep just reading the subtitles, so this time I need to listen too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: いいじゃん。{日本語|にほんご}で{見|み}てるし、{吹|ふ}き{替|か}えにはしなくていいよね。{続編|ぞくへん}は{今日|きょう}も{見|み}るんだっけ？
lines.romaji: Ii jan. Nihongo de miteru shi, fukikae ni wa shinakute ii yo ne. Zokuhen wa kyō mo miru n da kke?
lines.meaning: Sounds good. We’re watching in Japanese, so we don’t need the dub, right? Were we watching the sequel today too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {続編|ぞくへん}はまた{今度|こんど}。{明日|あした}は{早|はや}く{起|お}きなきゃ。まず{予告|よこく}を{見|み}て、それから{本編|ほんぺん}にしよう。
lines.romaji: Zokuhen wa mata kondo. Ashita wa hayaku okinakya. Mazu yokoku o mite, sore kara honpen ni shiyō.
lines.meaning: The sequel can wait. I have to get up early tomorrow. Let’s watch the trailer first, then the main feature.

dialogues.title: Remembering the plan and the actual viewing
dialogues.scene: Sunday morning. Kenta asks about the film he missed. The friends discuss a confusing exchange, avoid spoiling the sequel and realise they still need to pick their next viewing day.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}は{何時|なんじ}から{見|み}たんだっけ？ {予告|よこく}だけ？
lines.romaji: Kinō wa nanji kara mita n da kke? Yokoku dake?
lines.meaning: What time did you start watching yesterday again? Just the trailer?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {七時半|しちじはん}から{本編|ほんぺん}も{見|み}たよ。{十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに{止|と}めてたから、{終|お}わるのが{遅|おそ}くなっちゃった。
lines.romaji: Shichijihan kara honpen mo mita yo. Juppun goto ni tometeta kara, owaru no ga osoku nacchatta.
lines.meaning: The main feature too, from seven thirty. We kept pausing every ten minutes, so we finished pretty late.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {二人|ふたり}で「うん」って{言|い}ってる{所|ところ}、どっちが{相|あい}づちで、どっちがつぶやきなのかな。{同|おな}じに{聞|き}こえちゃう。
lines.romaji: Futari de un tte itteru tokoro, docchi ga aizuchi de, docchi ga tsubuyaki na no kana. Onaji ni kikoechau.
lines.meaning: When they both say “mm,” I wonder which is a response and which is muttering. They sound the same to me.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: そこ、{面白|おもしろ}いじゃん。{前|まえ}の{台詞|せりふ}も{聞|き}いてみなきゃ。{僕|ぼく}、{予告|よこく}では{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃったんだ。
lines.romaji: Soko, omoshiroi jan. Mae no serifu mo kiite minakya. Boku, yokoku de wa kikinogashichatta n da.
lines.meaning: That’s interesting! We need to listen to the line before it too. I missed it in the trailer.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: じゃ、そこはメモに{残|のこ}しとくね。{続編|ぞくへん}は{昨日|きのう}も{見|み}てないよ。{結末|けつまつ}、{言|い}っちゃだめだからね。
lines.romaji: Ja, soko wa memo ni nokoshitoku ne. Zokuhen wa kinō mo mitenai yo. Ketsumatsu, itcha dame da kara ne.
lines.meaning: I’ll note that bit for later. We didn’t watch the sequel yesterday either. Don’t spoil the ending!

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうだ、{次|つぎ}に{集|あつ}まる{曜日|ようび}って、もう{決|き}めたっけ？ {決|き}めてないなら{連絡|れんらく}しなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Sō da, tsugi ni atsumaru yōbi tte, mō kimeta kke? Kimetenai nara renraku shinakya.
lines.meaning: Oh, did we decide which day to meet next? If we haven’t, we need to get in touch.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: まだじゃない？ {僕|ぼく}も{予定|よてい}を{見|み}とくよ。{昨日|きのう}の{音量|おんりょう}はどうだった？
lines.romaji: Mada ja nai? Boku mo yotei o mitoku yo. Kinō no onryō wa dō datta?
lines.meaning: I don’t think so. I’ll check my schedule too. How was the volume yesterday?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {小|ちい}さくしたけど、{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえてたよ。{倍速|ばいそく}にはしてない。バオが{合図|あいず}したら、{元|もと}の{場面|ばめん}に{戻|もど}してた。
lines.romaji: Chiisaku shita kedo, serifu wa kikoeteta yo. Baisoku ni wa shitenai. Bao ga aizu shitara, moto no bamen ni modoshiteta.
lines.meaning: It was low, but we could hear the lines. We didn’t use double speed. Whenever Bao signalled, I went back to the scene.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {途中|とちゅう}で{眠気|ねむけ}が{出|で}ちゃったけどね。{毎回|まいかい}、{短|みじか}い{休息|きゅうそく}も{入|い}れとくといいかも。
lines.romaji: Tochū de nemuke ga dechatta kedo ne. Maikai, mijikai kyūsoku mo iretoku to ii kamo.
lines.meaning: I did get sleepy halfway through, though. Maybe we should plan a short break each time too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: いいじゃん。{次|つぎ}は{僕|ぼく}も{見|み}たいな。{曜日|ようび}が{決|き}まったら{教|おし}えて。{忘|わす}れないようにメモしとく。
lines.romaji: Ii jan. Tsugi wa boku mo mitai na. Yōbi ga kimattara oshiete. Wasurenai yō ni memo shitoku.
lines.meaning: Sounds good. I’d like to watch next time too. Tell me when you pick a day. I’ll write it down so I don’t forget.

readings.title: A viewing record; the next day is not set
paragraphs: ケンタへ。{日曜日|にちようび}の{朝|あさ}に{話|はな}した{視聴|しちょう}の{記録|きろく}を{送|おく}るね。{土曜日|どようび}は{七時半|しちじはん}から{本編|ほんぺん}を{見|み}たよ。{予告|よこく}はその{前|まえ}に{見|み}といた。{十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに{一時停止|いちじていし}して、{早口|はやくち}の{場面|ばめん}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}した。{倍速|ばいそく}にはしてないし、{続編|ぞくへん}もまだ{見|み}てない。
バオは{着信|ちゃくしん}に{応答|おうとう}していて、{最初|さいしょ}の{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃった。{携帯|けいたい}をしまってから、もう{一度|いちど}{見|み}たよ。{小|ちい}さな{音量|おんりょう}でも{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえた。{分|わ}からない{語尾|ごび}はメモに{残|のこ}して、{毎回|まいかい}{確認|かくにん}することにした。
{次|つぎ}の{予定|よてい}は、まだ{決|き}まってない。{曜日|ようび}を{決|き}めたら{連絡|れんらく}するね。{疲労|ひろう}や{眠気|ねむけ}が{出|で}たら、{休息|きゅうそく}を{入|い}れなくちゃ。{短|みじか}い{練習|れんしゅう}なら{続|つづ}けられるかな。ミサキ

glosses.meaning: have not watched; 見ていない
missed seeing; 見逃してしまった
put away; not a てしまう contraction here
not yet settled; 決まっていない
need to include/take; 入れなくてはいけない

grammar: とく/どく vs てる/でる
じゃん and explanatory の?
watch.prompt: Optionally save a contracted line from your own clip. Write its full form and identify the speaker and listener. Listen for the ending before checking subtitles.

recycling.reason: Film-night peers use repeated casual contractions. Equipment reports, minutes and private-work documents do not belong in their conversation.

exercises.prompt: When will they start the main feature?
exercises.explain: Misaki recalls 七時半 for the main feature and Bao agrees; the scene takes place on Saturday evening.

exercises.prompt: How will they handle fast speech?
options: Pause every ten minutes and replay the stopped part
Keep watching the sequel without pausing
exercises.explain: They agree on 十分ごとに一時停止 and on rewinding and replaying the part where they stop.

exercises.prompt: Why has Bao not seen the first preview?
options: He was copying the minutes in the room
He had already seen the sequel
He was answering an incoming call
exercises.explain: Bao says 電話に出てたんだ: he was on the phone when the trailer played.

exercises.context: Form practice: you finished reading the sequel to a book. Shorten 読んでしまった to its named casual contraction.
exercises.line: {続編|ぞくへん}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}ん＿＿。
exercises.explain: 読んで ends with で: でしまった→じゃった.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named preparatory contraction of 見ておく, not the ongoing form.
exercises.line: {先|さき}に{予告|よこく}を{見|み}＿＿ね。
exercises.explain: 見ておく→見とく. 見てる describes watching/a state; 見ちゃった is past completion.

exercises.context: Your friend says they missed the preview while answering a call. Suggest replaying it before the main feature.
exercises.line: {電話|でんわ}に{出|で}てて、{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃった。
options: じゃ、{予告|よこく}はもう{全部|ぜんぶ}{見|み}たんだね。
じゃ、{続編|ぞくへん}まで{終|お}わったんだね。
じゃ、{本編|ほんぺん}の{前|まえ}にもう{一度|いちど}{見|み}よう。
exercises.explain: The first offers a replay. The others falsely treat unseen material as already watched.

exercises.meaning: Before viewing, I need to decide the rest times. Use 決めなきゃ.
exercises.explain: 決めない→決めなきゃ. This is the speaker’s obligation, not a prohibition.

exercises.prompt: What does Misaki say they did NOT watch on Saturday?
exercises.explain: She explicitly says 昨日は続編を見てない; they watched both preview and main feature.

exercises.prompt: What is Bao wondering whether he can distinguish?
options: Permission and compulsion at the workplace
The day and time already set for next week
exercises.explain: Bao says 相づちとつぶやきも区別できるかな; it’s his unresolved learning question.

exercises.prompt: How was Saturday’s audio played?
options: At a lowered but audible volume, without double speed
exercises.explain: Misaki says 台詞は聞こえた and 倍速にせず.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask a familiar friend to recall the agreed time, using the named だったっけ pattern.
exercises.line: {視聴|しちょう}は{七時半|しちじはん}から＿＿？
exercises.explain: For noun/time recall, だった+っけ. This can recall an arrangement, not only a past action.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the explanatory casual の question after the na-adjective 好き.
exercises.line: この{主役|しゅやく}が{好|す}き＿＿？
exercises.explain: 好き is na-adjectival: 好きなの？. Verbs/i-adjectives attach の directly.

exercises.context: Your friend feels sleepy. Propose taking a short rest before the next scene, without dismissing the tiredness.
exercises.line: {眠気|ねむけ}が{出|で}てきた。
options: じゃ、{眠気|ねむけ}は{全|まった}くないんだね。
じゃ、{音量|おんりょう}はもう{決|き}まったんだね。
じゃ、{次|つぎ}の{場面|ばめん}の{前|まえ}に{短|みじか}い{休息|きゅうそく}を{入|い}れよう。
exercises.explain: The first answers the reported sleepiness with a rest. The other replies deny it or change the topic.

exercises.line: {小|ちい}さくしたけど、{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえてたよ。{倍速|ばいそく}にはしてない。バオが{合図|あいず}したら、{元|もと}の{場面|ばめん}に{戻|もど}してた。
exercises.prompt: Who reports that the lines were audible and the scene was replayed on a signal?
exercises.explain: Misaki answers Kenta’s volume question and describes replaying when Bao signals.

exercises.meaning: I’ll note the ending beforehand and check it each time. Use the contracted preparatory 残しといて.
tiles: メモに{残|のこ}しといて、
exercises.explain: 残しておいて→残しといて prepares a note for later checking.

exercises.prompt: What date/time does the message report as the actual main-feature viewing?
exercises.explain: The message is sent Sunday morning, but explicitly reports Saturday seven thirty.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of their next viewing day?
options: It’s a workplace assignment on Wednesday
It has not been decided; Misaki will contact Kenta after deciding
exercises.explain: 次の予定は、まだ決まってない and 曜日を決めたら連絡する distinguish unset plans from remembered Saturday.

exercises.prompt: What did Bao do after putting away the phone?
options: Watched the sequel at double speed
exercises.explain: 携帯をしまってから、もう一度見た refers back to the missed preview.

words.example: 登場する人物を紹介します。
人称を表す言葉に注目します。
呼称が変わると、相手との関係も違って見えます。
この人物の口癖を台本で確認します。
方言は、間違った日本語ではありません。
意味を確かめるために、標準語でも言ってみます。
台本には、誰の台詞か書いてあります。

words.meaning: to perform a role; to act
words.example: 今日は侍を演じます。
短い台本の朗読をします。
配役を決めてから練習します。
今日は仮装をせず、声だけで演じます。
侍の役には、古い言い方があります。

words.meaning: warrior; member of the historical warrior class
words.example: 物語に武士が登場します。
老人の役を若い人が演じます。
姫は王国の外へ出ます。
忍者は手紙を届けます。
悪役にも、行動の理由があります。
町を救った人物が英雄と呼ばれます。

words.meaning: brave person; hero in a fantasy
words.example: 勇者は冒険に出ます。
この物語では魔法が使えます。
王国の門で手紙を渡します。
短い冒険の台本を読みます。

語尾だけで人の性別は決められません。
役の年齢と演じる人の年齢は違います。
