watch.prompt: Optionally read a notice from your own media or a real event you are considering. Mark who may participate, what must be done beforehand and any dates that apply only once. Compare the formal wording with how you would tell a friend.

recycling.reason: The relocation and workshop notices need new dates, eligibility and membership language. Recent draft/newsletter and advice words are retained only where they fit the actual scene or notice; the 27 percent target avoids inserting unrelated material into the spoken conversations.

exercises.prompt: Which two dates does Bao want to make prominent?
options: The old building’s final day and the new building’s first day
The workshop’s first and last applications
The newsletter’s last year and next year
exercises.explain: He proposes highlighting the twentieth of this month and the first of next month.

exercises.prompt: Where is the new library?
options: Beside the old building’s west door
Five minutes on foot from the station’s east exit
exercises.explain: Yamamoto states 東口から歩いて五分.

exercises.prompt: What happens to existing membership cards?
options: All holders must get new cards before next month
Only students can retain their cards
They can be used as they are
exercises.explain: Yamamoto says 今のカードをそのまま使える.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the verb form that attaches directly before に際して.
exercises.line: {会員|かいいん}カードを＿＿に{際|さい}して、{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 発行する attaches before this occasion marker; the question explicitly tests attachment.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the direct noun attachment for the taught opening marker にあたり.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{本日|ほんじつ}の{流|なが}れをご{説明|せつめい}します。
exercises.explain: 開会 attaches directly with にあたり. No を or が is inserted.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto. You agree to check the dates and map before the notice is published.
exercises.line: {日付|ひづけ}と{地図|ちず}も、{掲載|けいさい}{前|まえ}に{見|み}てくれる？
options: はい。{掲載|けいさい}{後|ご}まで、どちらも{見|み}ません。
ううん。{映画|えいが}の{予約|よやく}なら{終|お}わったよ。
はい。{掲載|けいさい}{前|まえ}に、どちらも{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts both checks and the requested timing in a polite response.

exercises.meaning: In preparing to open the new facility, we explained the outline of the plan.
tiles: {新|あたら}しい{施設|しせつ}を
{計画|けいかく}の{概要|がいよう}を
exercises.explain: The dictionary verb 開く connects to the occasion marker; 説明した supplies the whole sentence’s past tense.

exercises.prompt: When can someone no longer use the old building, before the new one opens?
options: From the twenty-first through the end of this month
From the first through the twentieth next month
Only from nine to ten on opening day
exercises.explain: The first paragraph identifies the relocation closure period.

exercises.prompt: What should someone registering for the first time bring?
options: A new card already issued by the old library
An identity document showing their own name
Only a map of the station’s west exit
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph asks for 本人の名前が確認できる身分証.

exercises.prompt: How can borrowed books be returned during the closure?
options: Borrow another book at the new building first
Attend the new facility’s introduction session
Use the return box at the old building
exercises.explain: The final paragraph allows returns via the old box, while new borrowing is unavailable.

exercises.prompt: Why does Bao think Yamamoto could attend the workshop?
options: The poster explicitly includes people who aren’t students
Every resident automatically has a reserved place
Yamamoto is required to issue new membership cards
exercises.explain: 学生に限らず、一般の方も expands the participant group; it does not remove booking.

exercises.prompt: What has Bao forgotten?
options: The notebook required for a workshop already underway
exercises.explain: He has ID but cannot find his membership card.

exercises.prompt: What will they do about borrowing books?
options: Assume ID automatically replaces the card
Leave without asking and never return
Ask the desk whether there is an exception
exercises.explain: Misaki proposes asking; if there is no exception, they can read inside. No exception is established in the scene.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the expression that includes non-students as well as students.
exercises.line: {学生|がくせい}＿＿、{一般|いっぱん}の{方|かた}も{参加|さんか}できます。
exercises.explain: に限らず expands the group; the other two restrict it.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the taught expression for an annoying coincidence on this particular day.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{会員|かいいん}カードを{忘|わす}れちゃった。
exercises.explain: The first singles out this awkward day. Not limited to today would change the scope; に限る has a different construction.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. You agree to ask the desk first, then read inside if borrowing without a card isn’t allowed.
exercises.line: {例外|れいがい}があるか、{受付|うけつけ}で{聞|き}いてみよう。
options: うん。もう{例外|れいがい}があるって{決|き}まったね。
ううん。{学生|がくせい}ならカードは{絶対|ぜったい}にいらないよ。
うん。だめだったら、{今日|きょう}は{館内|かんない}で{読|よ}もう。
exercises.explain: The first follows the plan without inventing an exception or a student rule.

exercises.meaning: We’ll announce it online as well as on notices inside the building.
tiles: {館内|かんない}の{掲示|けいじ}に{限|かぎ}らず、
exercises.explain: The first noun phrase plus に限らず expands the communication channels.

exercises.prompt: A non-student wants to attend. Which plan meets the stated conditions?
options: Book by five the preceding day and bring the booking number, notebook and pen
Come without booking because only students need reservations
Bring a membership card instead of making a reservation
exercises.explain: Eligibility extends beyond students; the same booking and required items still apply.

exercises.prompt: Does attending automatically publish the participant’s article?
options: Yes; every draft is published before the workshop closes
No; the participant can decide later whether to publish it
Only students’ articles must be published automatically
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph assigns the later decision to 本人 and rejects automatic publication.

exercises.prompt: When can workshop participants enter the second-floor room that day?
options: From the preceding day at five
exercises.explain: The final paragraph distinguishes room access from the building’s opening hours.

grammar.title: State a considered conclusion
grammar.formation: Plain proposition + と言える/と言えます. A complete noun/な-adjective proposition normally uses だ: 妥当だと言える. と言えるだろう softens the conclusion.
grammar.explanation: と言える presents a conclusion or evaluation the writer considers justified: “it is fair to say.” It uses the potential of 言う, not the passive hearsay と言われている. It does not turn the writer’s evaluation into a guarantee. Quote the whole proposition before と; use だ in a noun or な-adjective predicate when teaching a complete clause. This intermediate bridge is retrieved in N2 argument writing; publisher tags vary.
grammar.example: この経費なら、参加費は妥当だと言える。
grammar.translation: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.

examples.ja: この{経費|けいひ}なら、{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}は{妥当|だとう}だと{言|い}える。
examples.en: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.

examples.ja: {二十人|にじゅうにん}が{予約|よやく}したので、{関心|かんしん}を{集|あつ}めたと{言|い}える。
examples.en: With twenty bookings, it’s fair to say the event attracted interest.

examples.ja: {二|ふた}つの{案|あん}には{共通|きょうつう}{点|てん}があると{言|い}えるだろう。
examples.en: We could say that the two proposals have points in common.

grammar.mistake: Do not confuse 言える with the hearsay passive 言われている, or write 妥当なと言える for a complete quoted predicate.

grammar.title: An action forced by the circumstances
grammar.formation: Verb negative stem (remove ない) + ざるを得ない. する → せざるを得ない; 来る → こざるを得ない. Polite 得ません and past 得なかった are possible.
grammar.explanation: ざるを得ない means there is no practical choice but to act, often reluctantly. It is comparatively formal and useful in an explanation or written opinion. A lack of affordable space may force cancellation; it is not the same as being unable to suppress laughter. Retrieve ないわけにはいかない, which often foregrounds responsibility or an obligation. These meanings can overlap; questions request a form or give an explicit cause rather than rejecting a sensible synonym.
grammar.example: 会場が使えないため、予定を変えざるを得ない。
grammar.translation: The venue’s unavailable, so we have no choice but to change the plan.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}が{使|つか}えないため、{予定|よてい}を{変|か}えざるを{得|え}ない。
examples.en: The venue’s unavailable, so we have no choice but to change the plan.

examples.ja: {経費|けいひ}が{足|た}りず、{規模|きぼ}を{縮小|しゅくしょう}せざるを{得|え}なかった。
examples.en: We lacked funds and had to reduce the scale.

examples.en: If there’s no alternative, we’ll have to cancel this time.

grammar.mistake: する uses せざる, not しざる. Do not append ざる to a dictionary form such as 変更するざる. The double negative requires doing the action.

grammar.title: Limit a claim to just that amount or role
grammar.formation: Noun or plain verb clause + にすぎない/にすぎません; written に過ぎない. Noun + である is also possible. For a な-adjective use なだけ or である before the pattern.
grammar.explanation: にすぎない limits the importance, quantity or extent of what precedes it: “merely” or “no more than.” It is not the same as すぎる meaning excessively. A count can be “only five”; an opinion can be “just one aspect.” To avoid variable adjective attachments in early practice, use nouns, ordinary verb clauses and the explicit なだけ/である variants. It is not automatically a denial of the whole activity’s value.
grammar.example: 集めた参加費で払えるのは、経費の一部にすぎない。
grammar.translation: The participation fees cover only part of the expenses.

examples.ja: {集|あつ}めた{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}で{払|はら}えるのは、{経費|けいひ}の{一部|いちぶ}にすぎない。
examples.en: The participation fees cover only part of the expenses.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{一人|ひとり}の{参加|さんか}{者|しゃ}にすぎません。

examples.en: We’ve only put forward a proposal; nothing’s been decided.

grammar.mistake: Do not treat にすぎない as an excessive action or attach a present noun with だにすぎない. Read exactly what it limits.

grammar.title: Hear a strong conviction, not a report
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + に違いない. Noun/な-adjective stem + に違いない without present だ. Past だった clauses are possible; polite に違いありません.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the N3 conviction pattern. A speaker is strongly convinced by the situation, but に違いない itself is not a report of checking. For example, seeing umbrellas may lead someone to think it must be raining. In an argument it may express confidence about an effect; read that confidence separately from a stated outcome.
grammar.example: 傘がぬれている。外は雨に違いない。
grammar.translation: The umbrella’s wet. It must be raining outside.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}がぬれている。{外|そと}は{雨|あめ}に{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: The umbrella’s wet. It must be raining outside.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}を{見|み}つけられたら、みんな{喜|よろこ}ぶに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: If we find a venue, I’m sure everyone will be pleased.

examples.ja: あの{大|おお}きな{荷物|にもつ}は{会|かい}の{道具|どうぐ}だったに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: That large load must have been equipment for the event.

grammar.mistake: Use 静かに違いない or 雨に違いない, not 静かなに違いない or 雨だに違いない. Do not score conviction as confirmed attendance or feelings.

grammar.title: Add a further fact for emphasis
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + ばかりか; な-adjective + な/であるばかりか; noun + ばかりか/であるばかりか.
grammar.explanation: ばかりか adds another, often stronger, fact: “not only … but also ….” It is more written or emphatic than だけでなく, retrieved from N3. Both favourable and unfavourable facts are possible. Teach a factual or descriptive second clause; requests and invitations do not fit the taught use. This connector does not express a contrast or say the first point is unimportant.
grammar.example: 経費が増えたばかりか、準備の時間も足りなくなった。
grammar.translation: Not only did expenses rise, we also ran short of preparation time.

examples.en: Not only did expenses rise, we also ran short of preparation time.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}かなばかりか、{駅|えき}からも{近|ちか}い。
examples.en: The room’s not only quiet, it’s also close to the station.

examples.ja: その{案|あん}は{妥当|だとう}であるばかりか、{実行|じっこう}しやすい。
examples.en: The proposal’s not only reasonable but also easy to put into practice.

grammar.mistake: The な-adjective needs な or である here. Use a statement in the second clause, not a direct request. Do not force ばかりか versus だけでなく as exclusive answers when either fits.

dialogues.title: Can we keep the reading group affordable?
dialogues.scene: Misaki and Bao plan a small Saturday reading group at the library. The room is free, but printed material costs three thousand yen. They discuss a two-hundred-yen fee and a way to welcome first-time participants.

watch.prompt: Optionally read an opinion in your own media. Underline the main recommendation and the reason given for it. Find one limitation, condition or added fact. Save useful lines with their context; a prediction is not an observed result.

recycling.reason: This opinion unit naturally retrieves only a small fraction of recent notice and administrative targets: 原則, 題名 and the notice reference in its reading. じゃ、{全員|ぜんいん}を{永久|えいきゅう}に{無料|むりょう}にしよう。
いいね。でも、{使|つか}っていいか{先|さき}に{聞|き}こう。
exercises.explain: The first welcomes the proposal while keeping the permission step still needed.

exercises.meaning: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.
exercises.explain: The quoted judgment keeps the な-adjective predicate だ before と.

exercises.prompt: Which position best matches the writer’s main claim?
options: Combine a general fee with a chance for newcomers to try, and make the finances clear
Make every visit free regardless of who pays the expenses
Charge as much as possible because profit is the only goal
exercises.explain: The final paragraph joins transparent income/expenses and an easy first opportunity.

exercises.prompt: What condition produces the four-thousand-yen figure?
options: Ten people each paying two hundred yen
Twenty people each paying two hundred yen
Twenty people attending free of charge
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly identifies full attendance as an assumption.

exercises.prompt: If budget support is not approved, what must the writer do?
exercises.explain: The third paragraph says 別の方法を考えざるを得ない.

exercises.prompt: What will Ren do by noon?
options: Ask whether the library has a room free
Confirm that the library room is already booked
Announce that the group is permanently closed
exercises.explain: The room has not been secured. Ren will ask, then report back.

exercises.prompt: If no room can be found, how much of the programme will change?
options: Every future meeting will stop permanently
This outdoor event will be cancelled; they want to meet next month
Only the final sentence of the story will be removed
exercises.explain: Ren corrects the misleading survival wording: 今回だけ, 来月はやりたい.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao’s みんな喜ぶに違いない express?
options: A report that everybody has already approved the room
A request to close the library
Confidence about how people would feel if they get a room
exercises.explain: The room is still conditional; Bao expects a positive reaction.

exercises.context: Form practice: use にすぎない after a noun phrase.
exercises.line: {今回|こんかい}の{中止|ちゅうし}は、{予定|よてい}の{一部|いちぶ}＿＿。
exercises.explain: The noun phrase 一部 takes にすぎない directly. It limits the scope to part of the programme.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete a present noun proposition with に違いない.
exercises.line: {傘|かさ}がぬれている。{外|そと}は＿＿。
exercises.explain: A present noun attaches directly, without だ or な. This is a conviction from the wet umbrella.

exercises.context: Form practice: attach ばかりか to the な-adjective 静か.
exercises.line: その{部屋|へや}は＿＿、{駅|えき}からも{近|ちか}い。
exercises.explain: The な-adjective needs な before this connector; the next clause adds another favourable fact.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren before the call. Agree to warn people of a possible change, without claiming a room is confirmed.
exercises.line: お{昼|ひる}までに、{部屋|へや}が{空|あ}いてるか{聞|き}いてみる。
options: ありがとう。それまで、{変更|へんこう}の{可能|かのう}{性|せい}だけ{伝|つた}えておくね。
よかった。もう{屋内|おくない}の{場所|ばしょ}が{決|き}まったね。
じゃ、{来月|らいげつ}も{絶対|ぜったい}に{中止|ちゅうし}だね。
exercises.explain: The first keeps the room enquiry pending and communicates only the possible change.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer recommend?
options: Keep the outdoor event at any cost to prove commitment
Find an indoor alternative by noon, or cancel this time while keeping future plans open
End all future activity even if a room becomes available
exercises.explain: The third paragraph sets the conditional plan; the final paragraph separates continuing the group from one day’s event.

exercises.prompt: What two problems are joined by ばかりか in the first paragraph?
options: Higher entry fees and permanent abolition
A free room and a warmer forecast
Wet reading material and a long wait in the cold
exercises.explain: The clause adds waiting in the cold to being made to read wet material.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t the organisers promise an indoor event yet?
options: They have not secured a room
The writer wants to end the entire group
exercises.explain: The third paragraph explicitly says the room is not yet secured.

lessons.title: An update and a forecast
lessons.description: Read an original practice report and plan a journey from its current update.
lessons.canDo: Identify a news source, the reported state and a conditional forecast

lessons.title: A response and an accompanying change
lessons.description: Read an original local-service report, then separate the trial’s changes from what remains.
lessons.canDo: Trace a response to requests and the limits of a timetable trial

grammar.title: Name the source of a report
grammar.formation: Noun naming a source + によると/によれば. A verb clause can use 聞いたところによると. The polite reporting variant is によりますと.
grammar.explanation: The phrase identifies whose information is being reported. A source may be a statement, an article or a person’s account. The following proposition can use reported そうだ or という, or state the information directly in news writing. It does not turn a forecast into an event that has already happened. Retrieve earlier reporting language and distinguish the information-source use from causal によって.
grammar.example: 続報によると、バスは九時に運行を始めた。
grammar.translation: According to the follow-up report, the bus began operating at nine.

examples.ja: {続報|ぞくほう}によると、バスは{九時|くじ}に{運行|うんこう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: According to the follow-up report, the bus began operating at nine.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}の{話|はなし}によれば、{復旧|ふっきゅう}にはまだ{時間|じかん}がかかるそうだ。
examples.en: According to the person in charge, repairs will still take time.

examples.ja: {聞|き}いたところによると、{説明|せつめい}{会|かい}は{午後|ごご}に{変|か}わったという。
examples.en: From what I’ve heard, the briefing has moved to the afternoon.

grammar.mistake: Use a source noun directly before によると, not 新聞がによると. によると and によれば are both valid here; do not reject one to force the other.

grammar.title: Read a reported assessment
grammar.formation: Plain proposition + とみられる/とみられている. A complete noun/な-adjective predicate uses だ, as in 原因は故障だとみられる. Attributive noun labels may omit だ. Active: Xは…とみている.
grammar.explanation: News writing uses とみられる for an assessment, inference or expectation. The article may state a basis or name an assessor. It is different from reporting a confirmed reopening. とみている names someone’s assessment actively. In a casual response, say みたい or と思う rather than making every line sound like a report. The text and surrounding attribution determine whose view it is; the form alone does not mean everyone agrees.
grammar.example: 電車は明日の午前に再開するとみられる。
grammar.translation: The trains are expected to resume tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}は{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる。
examples.en: The trains are expected to resume tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: {不通|ふつう}の{原因|げんいん}は{線路|せんろ}の{被害|ひがい}だとみられる。
examples.en: Damage to the track is thought to be the cause of the interruption.

examples.ja: {事業|じぎょう}{者|しゃ}は{復旧|ふっきゅう}に{二日|ふつか}かかるとみている。
examples.en: The operator expects repairs to take two days.

grammar.mistake: Do not read 再開するとみられる as すでに再開した: expected resumption is not completed resumption. Do not combine a polite predicate 再開します directly with とみられる.

grammar.title: Find the event and the response
grammar.formation: Noun/event noun phrase + を受けて/を受け、 + subsequent response. A whole proposition can be nominalised with こと: 利用者が増えたことを受けて.
grammar.explanation: This formal news connector presents an event, request or result followed by a response or reaction. In this unit, requests lead to a timetable decision. Written を受け is the connective form. It is not merely the receipt of a package; receiving an item normally uses 受け取る. In a conversation the friends quote the article, then explain what the change means for their own journey.
grammar.example: 利用者からの要望を受けて、夜間のバスを増便する。
grammar.translation: In response to requests from users, the operator will add nighttime buses.

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}からの{要望|ようぼう}を{受|う}けて、{夜間|やかん}のバスを{増便|ぞうびん}する。
examples.en: In response to requests from users, the operator will add nighttime buses.

examples.ja: {調査|ちょうさ}{結果|けっか}を{受|う}け、{市|し}は{計画|けいかく}を{見直|みなお}した。
examples.en: In response to the survey results, the city revised its plan.

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えたことを{受|う}けて、{窓口|まどぐち}を{増設|ぞうせつ}した。
examples.en: Following an increase in users, more service counters were installed.

grammar.mistake: Nominalise a verb proposition before を: 増えたことを受けて, not 増えたを受けて. Several cause/basis connectors can fit real contexts; form tasks explicitly request this connector.

grammar.title: Read the change that accompanies another change
grammar.formation: Noun or dictionary verb (+ の) + に伴って/に伴い. Before a noun use に伴う + noun. Written に伴い is connective, not a noun modifier.
grammar.explanation: One development brings or goes with another development: a relocation and a new route, or growing use and longer waits. This can describe gradual changes or a single event; it is not limited to two quantities increasing at the same rate. It does not itself establish a measured cause. Distinguish に伴い followed by a clause from に伴う followed by a noun.
grammar.example: 図書館の移転に伴い、バスの経路を変えた。
grammar.translation: Along with the library’s relocation, the bus route was changed.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{移転|いてん}に{伴|ともな}い、バスの{経路|けいろ}を{変|か}えた。
examples.en: Along with the library’s relocation, the bus route was changed.

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えるに{伴|ともな}って、{窓口|まどぐち}で{待|ま}つ{時間|じかん}も{長|なが}くなった。
examples.en: As the number of users grew, waits at the counter also became longer.

examples.ja: {改正|かいせい}に{伴|ともな}う{変更|へんこう}{点|てん}を{案内|あんない}する。
examples.en: Explain the changes accompanying the timetable revision.

grammar.mistake: Use 改正に伴う変更 before a noun, not 改正に伴い変更. A response to requests and a change accompanying relocation are different relationships, even when other connectors overlap.

dialogues.title: The interview is across the closed section
dialogues.scene: Yui has an interview near North Station at one today. She calls Bao to ask about the rail interruption. They read the nine-thirty update and work out a bus journey.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: ねえ、{北|きた}{駅|えき}までの{電車|でんしゃ}、まだ{止|と}まってる？
lines.romaji: Nee, Kita-eki made no densha, mada tomatteru?
lines.meaning: Hey, are the trains to North Station still stopped?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {九時|くじ}{半|はん}の{続報|ぞくほう}によると、{東|ひがし}{駅|えき}から{北|きた}{駅|えき}は{不通|ふつう}だって。
lines.romaji: Kuji-han no zokuhō ni yoru to, Higashi-eki kara Kita-eki wa futsū datte.
lines.meaning: According to the nine-thirty update, the line from East Station to North Station is closed.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {今日|きょう}{一時|いちじ}の{面接|めんせつ}、{北|きた}{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くなんだよね。
lines.romaji: Kyō ichiji no mensetsu, Kita-eki no chikaku nan da yo ne.
lines.meaning: My one o’clock interview today is near North Station.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: じゃ、{代|か}わりのバスは？{九時|くじ}から{出|で}てるって{書|か}いてある。
lines.romaji: Ja, kawari no basu wa? Kuji kara deteru tte kaite aru.
lines.meaning: Then what about the replacement bus? It says it’s been running since nine.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {復旧|ふっきゅう}の{見通|みとお}しは{出|で}てる？
lines.romaji: Fukkyū no mitōshi wa deteru?
lines.meaning: Have they said when the line might be restored?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる」だって。{今日|きょう}じゃないね。
lines.romaji: “Ashita no gozen ni saikai suru to mirareru” datte. Kyō ja nai ne.
lines.meaning: It says, “Services are expected to resume tomorrow morning.” So that’s not today.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: そっか。バス、どれくらいかかる？
lines.romaji: Sokka. Basu, dore kurai kakaru?
lines.meaning: Right. How long does the bus take?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {記事|きじ}には{四十分|よんじゅっぷん}って。{駅前|えきまえ}の{広場|ひろば}から{十五分|じゅうごふん}ごとに{出|で}るみたい。
lines.romaji: Kiji ni wa yonjuppun tte. Ekimae no hiroba kara jūgofun goto ni deru mitai.
lines.meaning: The article says forty minutes. It looks like it leaves the station square every fifteen minutes.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: じゃ、{十一時|じゅういちじ}{半|はん}に{出|で}ようかな。
lines.romaji: Ja, jūichiji-han ni deyō kana.
lines.meaning: Then maybe I’ll leave at eleven-thirty.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: いいね。{今日|きょう}は{混|こ}みそうだし、{少|すこ}し{早|はや}めに。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Kyō wa komisō da shi, sukoshi hayame ni.
lines.meaning: Good idea. It could be crowded today, so give yourself a little extra time.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {助|たす}かった。{料金|りょうきん}も{同|おな}じ？
lines.romaji: Tasukatta. Ryōkin mo onaji?
lines.meaning: That helps. Is the fare the same too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん、{同|おな}じって。{会社|かいしゃ}には、バスで{行|い}くって{伝|つた}えておくと{安心|あんしん}だよ。
lines.romaji: Un, onaji tte. Kaisha ni wa, basu de iku tte tsutaete oku to anshin da yo.
lines.meaning: Yes, it says it’s the same. It might put your mind at ease to let the company know you’re taking the bus.

dialogues.title: Can we take the bus after closing?
dialogues.scene: Ren and Yui read a local report during a break at the café. The library has recently moved near East Station a month ago. An announced evening-bus trial starts next month; they check the weekdays, last bus and café closing time.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {来月|らいげつ}から、{帰|かえ}りのバスが{増|ふ}えるって。
lines.romaji: Raigetsu kara, kaeri no basu ga fueru tte.
lines.meaning: They’re adding more buses for the journey home next month.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {夜|よる}の？それ{助|たす}かる。
lines.romaji: Yoru no? Sore tasukaru.
lines.meaning: At night? That’ll help.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: うん。「{利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}の{要望|ようぼう}を{受|う}けて、{夜間|やかん}の{便|びん}を{増|ふ}やす」だって。
lines.romaji: Un. “Riyōsha no yōbō o ukete, yakan no bin o fuyasu” datte.
lines.meaning: Yes. It says, “In response to users’ requests, nighttime services will be added.”

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {図書館|としょかん}が{移転|いてん}したから、{前|まえ}より{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いもんね。
lines.romaji: Toshokan ga iten shita kara, mae yori hito ga ōi mon ne.
lines.meaning: There’ve been more people around since the library moved, haven’t there?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: 「{移転|いてん}に{伴|ともな}う{利用|りよう}の{変化|へんか}を{調|しら}べた」って{書|か}いてあるよ。
lines.romaji: “Iten ni tomonau riyō no henka o shirabeta” tte kaite aru yo.
lines.meaning: It says they looked into the changes in use accompanying the relocation.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {最終|さいしゅう}は{何時|なんじ}になるの？
lines.romaji: Saishū wa nanji ni naru no?
lines.meaning: What time will the last bus be?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {八時|はちじ}から{九時|くじ}{半|はん}に{変|か}わるみたい。{平日|へいじつ}だけだけど。
lines.romaji: Hachiji kara kuji-han ni kawaru mitai. Heijitsu dake da kedo.
lines.meaning: It looks like it’s moving from eight to nine-thirty. Only on weekdays, though.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: あ、{土日|どにち}は{今|いま}のままなんだ。
lines.romaji: A, donichi wa ima no mama nan da.
lines.meaning: Oh, so weekends stay as they are.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: そう。とりあえず{三|さん}か{月|げつ}、やってみるんだって。
lines.romaji: Sō. Toriaezu sankagetsu, yatte miru n datte.
lines.meaning: Right. They’ll try it for three months to start with.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {値上|ねあ}げはない？
lines.romaji: Neage wa nai?
lines.meaning: Will the fare go up?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {当面|とうめん}は{同|おな}じって。うちは{九時|くじ}に{閉|し}まるから、{片付|かたづ}けが{早|はや}く{終|お}われば{間|ま}に{合|あ}いそう。
lines.romaji: Tōmen wa onaji tte. Uchi wa kuji ni shimaru kara, katazuke ga hayaku owareba maniai-sō.
lines.meaning: It’ll stay the same for now. We close at nine, so we might make it if we finish cleaning up quickly.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: うん。{新|あたら}しい{時刻|じこく}{表|ひょう}、あとで{見|み}ておこう。
lines.romaji: Un. Atarashii jikokuhyō, ato de mite okō.
lines.meaning: Yes. Let’s check the new timetable later.

readings.title: A nine-thirty update on the interrupted line
paragraphs: {昨夜|さくや}の{大雨|おおあめ}で、{東|ひがし}{駅|えき}と{北|きた}{駅|えき}の{間|あいだ}を{走|はし}る{電車|でんしゃ}が{始発|しはつ}から{運休|うんきゅう}している。{九時|くじ}{半|はん}に{公表|こうひょう}された{鉄道|てつどう}{会社|がいしゃ}の{続報|ぞくほう}によると、{線路|せんろ}の{一部|いちぶ}に{水|みず}が{流|なが}れ{込|こ}み、{点検|てんけん}と{修理|しゅうり}が{続|つづ}いている。{両|りょう}{駅|えき}の{間|あいだ}は{不通|ふつう}だが、{東|ひがし}{駅|えき}より{南|みなみ}の{区間|くかん}は{通常|つうじょう}どおり{運行|うんこう}している。

{会社|かいしゃ}は{復旧|ふっきゅう}の{見通|みとお}しについて、{水|みず}が{引|ひ}いた{後|あと}の{点検|てんけん}で{大|おお}きな{損傷|そんしょう}が{見|み}つからなければ、{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}できると{説明|せつめい}している。{作業|さぎょう}は{順調|じゅんちょう}に{進|すす}んでおり、{電車|でんしゃ}は{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる。ただし、{正確|せいかく}な{時刻|じこく}は{今夜|こんや}の{発表|はっぴょう}で{案内|あんない}する{予定|よてい}だ。

{代|か}わりのバスは{今日|きょう}{九時|くじ}に{運行|うんこう}を{始|はじ}めた。{東|ひがし}{駅前|えきまえ}の{広場|ひろば}から{北|きた}{駅|えき}まで{十五分|じゅうごふん}ごとに{出発|しゅっぱつ}し、{所要|しょよう}{時間|じかん}は{約|やく}{四十分|よんじゅっぷん}。{料金|りょうきん}は{同|おな}じ{区間|くかん}の{電車|でんしゃ}と{同|おな}じで、{定期券|ていきけん}も{使|つか}える。バスは{途中|とちゅう}で{二|ふた}つの{停留所|ていりゅうじょ}に{止|と}まるが、その{場所|ばしょ}は{駅|えき}の{掲示|けいじ}で{確認|かくにん}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。

watch.prompt: Optionally use your own news text or recording. Identify who supplies the information, one stated event, one prediction, and any condition or time attached to it. Notice how people paraphrase the report in everyday speech. Save useful lines in context.

recycling.reason: The friends need a route to an interview and a later bus after a café shift. Only recent words that naturally occur in these practical conversations and readings are counted; unrelated opinion and notice vocabulary is not inserted to reach a quota.

exercises.prompt: Why does Yui need a way to North Station today?
options: She has a one o’clock interview nearby
She has an interview there tomorrow morning
She works as a railway repairer
exercises.explain: Yui says 今日一時の面接, near North Station.

exercises.prompt: Which transport is reported to have already started?
options: The interrupted trains, at nine today
The replacement bus, at nine today
A new night bus starting next month
exercises.explain: Bao reads 九時から出てる about the bus; tomorrow morning is the forecast for the trains.

exercises.prompt: What departure does Yui tentatively choose?
options: Seven in the evening by bus
exercises.explain: じゃ、十一時半に出ようかな is a tentative plan, with extra time for possible crowds.

exercises.context: Form practice: identify the company update as the information source using によると.
exercises.line: {会社|かいしゃ}の{続報|ぞくほう}＿＿、{電車|でんしゃ}はまだ{止|と}まっている。
exercises.explain: A source noun phrase attaches directly to によると.

exercises.context: Form practice: quote the complete noun proposition “resumption is tomorrow morning” with とみられる.
exercises.line: {再開|さいかい}は＿＿。
options: {明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}なとみられる
{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}だとみられる
{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}にとみられる
exercises.explain: The complete noun predicate 明日の午前だ is quoted with と. This sentence states an assessment, not that trains are already running.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Bao after hearing the forecast. You still need to travel today; choose the response that fits the update.
exercises.line: 「{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる」だって。
options: じゃ、もう{電車|でんしゃ}が{動|うご}いてるんだね。
じゃ、{今日|きょう}の{面接|めんせつ}も{来月|らいげつ}だね。
じゃ、{今日|きょう}はバスで{行|い}くね。
exercises.explain: The forecast is for tomorrow; taking the bus fits today’s interview. Nothing changes the interview date.
The source phrase precedes the proposition; とみられる follows plain 再開する. This is one authored order, not unrestricted writing.
tiles: {明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: place the source first, then say the trains are expected to resume tomorrow morning.

exercises.prompt: Which section is still running normally in the nine-thirty update?
options: The section south of East Station
The whole section between East and North Stations
Every section north of North Station
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly says 東駅より南の区間 is normal; the East–North section is closed.

exercises.prompt: What condition must be met for the expected tomorrow-morning reopening?
options: Inspection after the water recedes must find no major damage
All passengers must buy a new bus pass
exercises.explain: The second paragraph gives the condition 大きな損傷が見つからなければ. The exact time will be announced later.

exercises.prompt: Which bus detail is explicitly stated?
options: The fare is free for every passenger
The bus runs directly with no intermediate stops
The fare matches the train fare for that section and commuter passes are valid
exercises.explain: The third paragraph states equal fares and valid passes, plus two intermediate stops.

exercises.prompt: When will the later last bus apply?
exercises.explain: Ren says 来月から and 平日だけ; Yui confirms weekends stay unchanged.

exercises.prompt: How long is the initial trial?
exercises.explain: Ren says とりあえず三か月、やってみる.

exercises.prompt: Why is catching the last bus still conditional for the café staff?
options: The bus starts before the café opens
The café is already permanently closed
They close at nine and need to finish cleaning up quickly
exercises.explain: Ren says 片付けが早く終われば間に合いそう. The last bus is nine-thirty.

exercises.context: Form practice: nominalise the stated increase in users before を受けて.
exercises.line: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えた＿＿、{夜間|やかん}の{便|びん}を{増|ふ}やした。
exercises.explain: The preceding verb proposition needs こと before を受けて. The later clause states the response.

exercises.context: Form practice: modify 変更点 with に伴う after 改正.
exercises.line: {改正|かいせい}＿＿{変更|へんこう}{点|てん}を{案内|あんない}する。
exercises.explain: Use the noun-modifying form に伴う directly before 変更点. に伴い introduces a following clause.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren. You want to confirm how the weekday trial affects a Sunday journey.
exercises.line: {平日|へいじつ}だけだけど、{最終|さいしゅう}が{九時|くじ}{半|はん}になるみたい。
options: じゃ、{日曜|にちよう}も{九時|くじ}{半|はん}まで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}だね。
じゃ、{今日|きょう}から{全|すべ}てのバスが{無料|むりょう}なんだね。
じゃ、{日曜|にちよう}の{帰|かえ}りは{今|いま}の{時刻|じこく}{表|ひょう}で{考|かんが}えるね。
exercises.explain: The change applies to weekdays from next month. Weekends retain the current timetable.
に伴う modifies the noun phrase 利用の変化. This is one authored order.
tiles: {利用|りよう}の{変化|へんか}を
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: say they investigated the changes in use accompanying the relocation. Put the relocation modifier first.

exercises.prompt: What do the figures 312 and 184 describe?
options: 312 questionnaire respondents; 184 wanted more night buses
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly names respondents as people, then says 184 requested more nighttime services.

exercises.prompt: Which detail remains unchanged in the trial?
options: The weekday last bus at eight
Daytime services, weekend timetables and the library’s closing time
The total number of weekday night buses
exercises.explain: The third paragraph lists the unchanged daytime, weekend and library-closing arrangements. Three night buses are added.

exercises.prompt: What will determine the service after the trial?
options: An already-made decision to keep it permanently
A promised fare rise on the first day
Recorded use and delays during the trial, with further user feedback
exercises.explain: The last paragraph says the operator will record use and delays and decide from the results. Permanent continuation is not decided.

grammar.title: Offer an action towards the recipient
grammar.formation: お + suitable verb ます-stem + する/します. For many Sino-Japanese する verbs use ご + verbal noun + する. Prefixes have lexical exceptions, including お電話する.
grammar.explanation: Describe an action by your own side towards a respected recipient: send something to them, hold their bag or let them know. The person being respected may be a third party, not necessarily the listener. Do not turn the recipient’s action into your humble action. Not every verb accepts this template: use an established special form where appropriate, such as 伺う. Short, clear commitments are useful in email.
grammar.example: 資料は午後にお送りします。
grammar.translation: I’ll send the materials this afternoon.

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}は{午後|ごご}にお{送|おく}りします。
examples.en: I’ll send the materials this afternoon.

examples.ja: {結果|けっか}が{分|わ}かり{次第|しだい}、お{知|し}らせします。
examples.en: I’ll let you know as soon as the result is available.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}からお{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.en: The person in charge will call you.

grammar.mistake: Do not use お送りします to say the customer sends you a file. Name the actor when it is not obvious. お送りする is not the same perspective as お送りいただく.

grammar.title: State your side’s action formally
grammar.formation: ご + suitable する-verbal noun + いたす/いたします; お + suitable verb stem + いたす also occurs. ご説明いたします; お送りいたします.
grammar.explanation: いたす makes your side’s action a deferential statement to the listener. お/ご…いたす can also respect the person towards whom the act is directed. That combination is recognised usage, not automatically incorrect double keigo. In external email, 弊社 means our company and 貴社 commonly means your company; spoken 御社 is also respectful. Internal colleagues need not speak like external correspondence.
grammar.example: 弊社の担当者がご説明いたします。
grammar.translation: Our person in charge will explain it to you.

examples.ja: {弊社|へいしゃ}の{担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}がご{説明|せつめい}いたします。
examples.en: Our person in charge will explain it to you.

examples.ja: {変更|へんこう}{点|てん}をご{案内|あんない}いたします。
examples.en: I’ll explain the changes.

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}をお{送|おく}りいたします。
examples.en: I’ll send the materials to you.

grammar.mistake: For your action, use ご説明いたします, not ご説明なさいます. Do not add し after a する-verbal noun: ご説明しする is not this form.

grammar.title: Ask to perform an action yourself
grammar.formation: Verb causative て-form + いただく. 書く→書かせていただく; 見る→見させていただく; する→させていただく; 来る→来させていただく (こさせ). Question: …いただけますか.
grammar.explanation: You receive permission to carry out your own action, with a benefit or a felt benefit. In the scene, you ask to use the client’s supplied table in a proposal; the client can grant permission. In ご確認いただけますか the recipient checks; in 確認させていただけますか you ask to do the checking. This distinction is more useful than always choosing the longest wording. When permission is not relevant, a simple いたします statement may be clearer.
grammar.example: 頂いた表を提案書に使わせていただけますか。
grammar.translation: May I use the table you sent in the proposal?

examples.ja: {頂|いただ}いた{表|ひょう}を{提案|ていあん}{書|しょ}に{使|つか}わせていただけますか。
examples.en: May I use the table you sent in the proposal?

examples.ja: {許可|きょか}を{頂|いただ}いたので、{図|ず}を{使|つか}わせていただきました。
examples.en: I used the diagram with your permission.

examples.ja: {原本|げんぽん}を{確認|かくにん}させていただけますか。
examples.en: May I check the original document?

grammar.mistake: Do not confuse who acts. 確認させていただく concerns our checking; ご確認いただく concerns the recipient checking for us. Permission/benefit depend on context, not just status.

grammar.title: Request an action without deciding for the recipient
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + いただけますか/いただけませんか. Respectful regular form: お/ご + suitable stem + いただけますか. Extended business request: …いただけますでしょうか.
grammar.explanation: Acknowledge the effort, say what you need and leave the recipient a choice. ご確認いただけますか and ご確認いただけませんか are useful options. The extended いただけますでしょうか appears in business/service teaching materials; it is not universally wrong, nor automatically preferable. Put deadlines and alternatives clearly in the message. していただきます can present a settled arrangement rather than asking whether the recipient agrees.
grammar.example: お手数ですが、金曜の三時までにご返信いただけますか。
grammar.translation: Could you reply by three on Friday? Sorry for the trouble.

examples.ja: お{手数|てすう}ですが、{金曜|きんよう}の{三時|さんじ}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただけますか。
examples.en: Could you reply by three on Friday? Sorry for the trouble.

examples.ja: {難|むずか}しければ、ご{都合|つごう}をお{知|し}らせいただけませんか。
examples.en: If that’s difficult, could you let us know what works for you?

examples.ja: {添付|てんぷ}の{資料|しりょう}をご{確認|かくにん}いただけますでしょうか。
examples.en: Would you be able to check the attached materials?

grammar.mistake: Do not mark a shorter polite request wrong merely because the example uses でしょうか. Do not write ご確認させていただけますか when you mean to ask the recipient to check.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{最後|さいご}のページに、{会場|かいじょう}の{地図|ちず}を{入|い}れました。
lines.romaji: Hai. Saigo no pēji ni, kaijō no chizu o iremashita.
lines.meaning: Yes. I put the venue map on the last page.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {地図|ちず}の{字|じ}だけ、もう{少|すこ}し{大|おお}きくできますか。
lines.romaji: Chizu no ji dake, mō sukoshi ōkiku dekimasu ka.
lines.meaning: Could you make just the map lettering a little bigger?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい、{直|なお}してからお{送|おく}りします。
lines.romaji: Hai, naoshite kara ookuri shimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes, I’ll correct it, then send it.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: お{願|ねが}いします。{宛先|あてさき}は、{田村|たむら}さんのメールアドレスです。
lines.romaji: Onegai shimasu. Atesaki wa, Tamura-san no mēru adoresu desu.
lines.meaning: Thanks. Send it to Tamura-san’s email address.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ご{返信|へんしん}は、{金曜|きんよう}の{三時|さんじ}までにお{願|ねが}いしていいですか。
lines.romaji: Gohenshin wa, kinyō no sanji made ni onegai shite ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Is it okay to ask for a reply by three on Friday?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{難|むずか}しい{場合|ばあい}は、{都合|つごう}を{知|し}らせてもらいましょう。
lines.romaji: Hai. Muzukashii baai wa, tsugō o shirasete moraimashō.
lines.meaning: Yes. If that’s difficult, let’s ask them to tell us what works.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {添付|てんぷ}は、PDFの{一部|いちぶ}じゃなくて、{四|よん}ページ{全部|ぜんぶ}ですね。
lines.romaji: Tenpu wa, pī dī efu no ichibu ja nakute, yon pēji zenbu desu ne.
lines.meaning: I’ll attach all four pages, not just part of the PDF.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: そうです。{印刷|いんさつ}はまだ{頼|たの}まないでください。
lines.romaji: Sō desu. Insatsu wa mada tanomanaide kudasai.
lines.meaning: That’s right. Please don’t order the printing yet.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {確認|かくにん}が{終|お}わってからですね。
lines.romaji: Kakunin ga owatte kara desu ne.
lines.meaning: So, after the review is finished.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{料金|りょうきん}については、{私|わたし}からご{説明|せつめい}いたします。
lines.romaji: Hai. Ryōkin ni tsuite wa, watashi kara gosetsumei itashimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. I’ll explain the charges to the client.

dialogues.title: Correct the date and ask about the table
dialogues.scene: The learner phones client Tamura after noticing a wrong weekday in an email. The actual visit is Thursday at two in the client’s second-floor meeting room. They also ask permission to include Tamura’s supplied table in the proposal.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {田村|たむら}さん、メールの{日時|にちじ}に{誤記|ごき}がありました。{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません。
lines.romaji: Tamura-san, mēru no nichiji ni goki ga arimashita. Mōshiwake arimasen.
lines.meaning: Tamura-san, there was an error in the date and time in my email. I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: {水曜|すいよう}って{書|か}いてありましたね。{木曜|もくよう}の{二時|にじ}ですよね。
lines.romaji: Suiyō tte kaite arimashita ne. Mokuyō no niji desu yo ne.
lines.meaning: It said Wednesday. It’s Thursday at two, right?

lines.speaker: You

lines.meaning: Yes, Thursday at two. I’ll resend the corrected email.

lines.speaker: Tamura

lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Basho wa, uchi no nikai no kaigishitsu desu.
lines.meaning: Understood. We’ll meet in our second-floor meeting room.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Tōjitsu wa Mori to futari de ukagaimasu.
lines.meaning: Thank you. Mori and I will visit that day.

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: {案内|あんない}のPDFも{届|とど}きましたよ。{金曜|きんよう}までに{見|み}ておきます。
lines.romaji: Annai no pī dī efu mo todokimashita yo. Kinyō made ni mite okimasu.
lines.meaning: The brochure PDF arrived too. I’ll look through it by Friday.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: お{手数|てすう}をおかけします。あと、{頂|いただ}いた{表|ひょう}について、お{聞|き}きしてもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Otesū o okake shimasu. Ato, itadaita hyō ni tsuite, okiki shite mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Sorry for the trouble. May I also ask about the table you sent?

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: はい、{何|なん}でしょう。
lines.romaji: Hai, nan deshō.
lines.meaning: Yes, what is it?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {提案|ていあん}{書|しょ}に{使|つか}わせていただけますか。
lines.romaji: Teiansho ni tsukawasete itadakemasu ka.
lines.meaning: May I use it in the proposal?

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: はい、かまいません。{数字|すうじ}が{読|よ}める{大|おお}きさにしてくださいね。
lines.romaji: Hai, kamaimasen. Sūji ga yomeru ōkisa ni shite kudasai ne.
lines.meaning: Yes, that’s fine. Just make the numbers large enough to read.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {承知|しょうち}しました。{一部|いちぶ}だけでなく、{表|ひょう}{全体|ぜんたい}を{載|の}せます。
lines.romaji: Shōchi shimashita. Ichibu dake de naku, hyō zentai o nosemasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. I’ll include the whole table, not just part of it.

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: はい。それでは、{木曜|もくよう}にお{待|ま}ちしています。
lines.romaji: Hai. Sore de wa, mokuyō ni omachi shite imasu.
lines.meaning: All right. I’ll see you on Thursday.

お{手数|てすう}ですが、{内容|ないよう}をご{確認|かくにん}いただけますか。{特|とく}に、{日時|にちじ}と{会場|かいじょう}の{住所|じゅうしょ}、{地図|ちず}の{文字|もじ}の{大|おお}きさについて、ご{意見|いけん}をいただけると{助|たす}かります。{金曜|きんよう}の{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}までにご{返信|へんしん}をお{願|ねが}いしたいのですが、{難|むずか}しい{場合|ばあい}は、ご{都合|つごう}をお{知|し}らせください。

{今|いま}は{確認|かくにん}のための{資料|しりょう}ですので、{印刷|いんさつ}の{発注|はっちゅう}はまだしておりません。{部数|ぶすう}は{百部|ひゃくぶ}を{予定|よてい}しておりますが、ご{確認|かくにん}の{後|あと}で{決定|けってい}します。{料金|りょうきん}については、{森|もり}から{別|べつ}のメールでご{説明|せつめい}いたします。{今回|こんかい}の{添付|てんぷ}は{案内|あんない}だけで、{見積書|みつもりしょ}ではありません。

{添付|てんぷ}が{開|ひら}けない{場合|ばあい}は、このメールへの{返信|へんしん}でお{知|し}らせください。{別|べつ}の{形式|けいしき}で{再送|さいそう}します。{紙|かみ}の{原本|げんぽん}をお{送|おく}りいただく{必要|ひつよう}はありません。{貴社|きしゃ}のお{手元|てもと}でご{確認|かくにん}いただき、{気|き}になる{点|てん}だけ{教|おし}えていただければ{結構|けっこう}です。どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。バオ。

grammar: our action お〜する/ご〜いたす
own action with permission させていただく
recipient request いただけますか
watch.prompt: Optionally read a real email you can use. Identify the sender’s promised action, the recipient’s requested action, a date, and any alternative if that timing is difficult. Save useful complete phrases in context.

recycling.reason: The work conversation checks a brochure, a mistaken weekday and permission for a table. Only earlier terms actually present in this setting count. News and venue vocabulary is not padded into client correspondence to reach a percentage.

exercises.prompt: What does Mori ask to change before the PDF is sent?
options: Make the map lettering a little bigger
exercises.explain: Mori says 地図の字だけ、もう少し大きくできますか.

exercises.prompt: What reply time is requested, subject to the client’s availability?
exercises.explain: The learner asks 金曜の三時まで; Mori says to ask about availability if that is difficult.

exercises.prompt: What should wait until the client review finishes?
exercises.explain: Mori says 印刷はまだ頼まないでください.

exercises.context: Form practice: you will send the client the materials. Complete the お + ます-stem + します form.
exercises.line: {資料|しりょう}を＿＿。
exercises.explain: 送り is the ます-stem of 送る; the speaker sends the materials.

exercises.context: Form practice: your person in charge explains to the client. Choose the regular ご…いたします form.
exercises.line: {弊社|へいしゃ}の{担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}が＿＿。
options: ご{説明|せつめい}しするします
ご{説明|せつめい}いたします
ご{説明|せつめい}なさいます
exercises.explain: The action belongs to our side, not the customer. ご説明いたします combines recipient-directed respect with deferential speech.

exercises.context: You tell an external client that YOU will send the file this afternoon. Choose the wording that states your action respectfully.
exercises.line: {午後|ごご}にファイルを{送|おく}る。
options: {午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りください。
{午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りになります。
{午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りします。
exercises.explain: お送りします states your sending. The other options request or honour the recipient’s sending, changing who acts.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: say you will attach and send the materials.
exercises.explain: 添付して links attaching to your sending; this is one authored order.

exercises.prompt: What is attached to this review-request email?
exercises.explain: The first paragraph names all four pages; the third says it is not the quotation.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of the planned hundred copies?
options: Proposed; count and printing order follow the review
exercises.explain: 百部 is a plan, 決定 follows review and printing has not yet been ordered.

exercises.prompt: What should Tamura do if replying by Friday at three is difficult?
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly asks the client to say their availability.

exercises.prompt: Which visit is confirmed in the call?
options: Thursday at two, in the client’s second-floor meeting room
Wednesday at two, at the café
Friday at three, in Mori’s office
exercises.explain: Tamura and the learner confirm Thursday at two, then Tamura gives the room.

exercises.prompt: What does the learner ask permission to do?
options: Ask Tamura to write a new table by tonight
Use the supplied table in the proposal
exercises.explain: The learner says 提案書に使わせていただけますか; the learner uses it.

exercises.prompt: What does Tamura ask about the table?
options: Include only a tiny corner of it
Make the numbers large enough to read
exercises.explain: 数字が読める大きさにしてください states the condition.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask permission for YOU to use the client’s table. Use the causative て-form of 使う plus いただけますか.
exercises.line: {表|ひょう}を＿＿。
options: {使|つか}わせていただけますか
{使|つか}わしているいただけますか
{使|つか}うさせていただけますか
exercises.explain: 使う becomes 使わせる, then 使わせて. Permission is for the speaker’s own use.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask the CLIENT to check the attached document. Choose the regular ご…いただけますか request.
exercises.line: {添付|てんぷ}の{資料|しりょう}を＿＿。
options: ご{確認|かくにん}させていただけますか
ご{確認|かくにん}いただけますか
ご{確認|かくにん}いただきます
exercises.explain: The recipient checks for you. させていただく asks for your checking; いただきます presents it as arranged rather than asks.

exercises.context: You need an external client to reply to a request. They have not agreed yet. Choose a respectful request that leaves them a choice.
exercises.line: {金曜|きんよう}までに{返信|へんしん}する。
options: {金曜|きんよう}までに{絶対|ぜったい}{返信|へんしん}してね。
{金曜|きんよう}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただくことに{決|き}めました。
お{手数|てすう}ですが、{金曜|きんよう}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただけますか。
exercises.explain: The first asks and acknowledges effort; the others demand or unilaterally decide the client’s action. Other clear polite requests are also valid.

tiles: ご{了承|りょうしょう}を
{使|つか}わせていただきます
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: put the permission first, then say you will use the table with it.
exercises.explain: The established permission supports the speaker’s subsequent use. This is one authored order.

exercises.prompt: What was corrected rather than newly changed?
options: The written weekday; the actual time and place are unchanged
The actual visit time moved from two to three
The meeting moved from the client to the café
exercises.explain: The second paragraph distinguishes correcting 誤記 from changing time or place.

exercises.prompt: Which review timing belongs to which document?
options: Both documents by Friday at three
Proposal before Thursday’s visit; brochure reply by Friday at three
Brochure before Wednesday; proposal next month
exercises.explain: The last two paragraphs distinguish the proposal from the separately sent brochure.

exercises.prompt: Why can Bao use the table in the proposal?
options: The table was newly created by Mori
Tamura already granted permission in the call
exercises.explain: 先ほどのご了承に基づき refers back to the explicit permission.

grammar.title: Recognise a formal identification or statement
grammar.formation: Noun + でございます, a formal polite alternative to です. Existence uses ございます for ある; animate own-side presence commonly uses おります.
grammar.explanation: The caller hears a company or department name before the purpose of a call. でございます identifies it formally; it does not by itself honour a particular person. Ordinary internal conversations can use です. Distinguish identification from presence: 会議室でございます identifies the room; 会議室がございます says one exists. Earlier polite forms are retrieved here in a phone and visitor-service setting.
grammar.example: 営業部でございます。
grammar.translation: This is the sales department.

examples.ja: {営業|えいぎょう}{部|ぶ}でございます。
examples.en: This is the sales department.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}は{三階|さんがい}のC{室|しつ}でございます。
examples.en: The venue is Room C on the third floor.

examples.ja: {受付|うけつけ}に{資料|しりょう}がございます。
examples.en: The materials are at reception.

grammar.mistake: Do not mechanically add で before every ございます. Match the intended identification or existence. Historical でござる is not the default voice for a modern office.

grammar.title: Check availability before asking
grammar.formation: 恐れ入りますが + a concrete question or request. Internal availability check: 今、少しよろしいですか / 今、話してもいいですか.
grammar.explanation: 恐れ入りますが acknowledges the trouble before a request. Follow it with what you need, such as repeating a name; it is not the request by itself. A familiar internal colleague can speak more directly while remaining polite. If the person cannot talk now, agree on another time. These are useful choices rather than words required before every sentence.
grammar.example: 恐れ入りますが、もう一度お名前をお願いします。
grammar.translation: Sorry, could you give your name once more?

examples.ja: {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、もう{一度|いちど}お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.en: Sorry, could you give your name once more?

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{少|すこ}しよろしいですか。
examples.en: Do you have a moment?

examples.ja: {今|いま}は{難|むずか}しいでしょうか。{後|あと}で{掛|か}け{直|なお}します。
examples.en: Is now difficult? I’ll call again later.

grammar.mistake: Do not assume that a soft opening makes an impossible deadline acceptable. Confirm the recipient has time, and keep the request clear.

grammar.title: Introduce yourself without changing whose name it is
grammar.formation: Own name + と申します. In a call, company/team + の + own name + と申します is a conventional formal introduction.
grammar.explanation: 申す is a deferential way of saying something by your own side; と申します introduces your name to the listener. It is not the respectful verb for the client introducing themself. Internal colleagues who already know each other can simply use です. Ask a client’s name with お名前を… rather than asking them to 申す. This retrieves N4 extra-modest forms in a complete phone turn.
grammar.example: 森のチームのバオと申します。
grammar.translation: I’m Bao, from Mori’s team.

examples.ja: {森|もり}のチームのバオと{申|もう}します。
examples.en: I’m Bao, from Mori’s team.

examples.ja: {営業|えいぎょう}{部|ぶ}の{石川|いしかわ}と{申|もう}します。
examples.en: This is Ishikawa from the sales department.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はバオと{申|もう}します。
examples.en: My name is Bao.

grammar.mistake: Do not ask a client お名前は何と申しますか. That makes the client’s act deferential; お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか is a respectful alternative.

grammar.title: Refer to your colleague from the caller’s perspective
grammar.formation: To an external client: 石川は席を外しております. Neutral identifying role is possible: 課長の石川. Internally/directly: 石川課長, 今よろしいですか.
grammar.explanation: When representing your company to a client, refer to your own-side colleague without raising them above the client. おります is a deferential own-side presence form; いらっしゃいます asks about the respected other party. A job title can identify the role without acting as an honorific suffix. Internally you still address Ishikawa respectfully. Relationship and institution matter: this company convention is not a universal ban on titles in every school, family or mixed group.
grammar.example: 石川は、ただ今席を外しております。
grammar.translation: Ishikawa is away from their desk at the moment.

examples.ja: {石川|いしかわ}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}しております。
examples.en: Ishikawa is away from their desk at the moment.

examples.ja: {課長|かちょう}の{石川|いしかわ}からお{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.en: Our section manager Ishikawa will call you.

examples.ja: {石川|いしかわ}{課長|かちょう}、{今|いま}よろしいですか。
examples.en: Ishikawa-kachō, is now a good time?

grammar.mistake: Do not use 石川様はいらっしゃいます to elevate your own company’s manager to a client. Do not turn this into a rule to speak disrespectfully to the manager directly.

dialogues.title: An internal call about the demonstration

watch.prompt: Optionally listen to a workplace call you may use. Note the requested action, current arrangement and any condition before a change is confirmed. Do not infer a decision just from a courteous acknowledgement.

recycling.reason: A meeting confirmation and a caller’s request use earlier schedule, reply and telephone vocabulary where it fits. Committee headwords are supplementary genre recognition; they are not stuffed into the calls to reach the default recycling percentage.

exercises.explain: Mori joins online; Ishikawa shares the screen.

exercises.prompt: When will Bao start setting up?
exercises.explain: Bao says 九時半から準備します; this is setup, not visitor reception.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the formal identification of the sales department with でございます.
exercises.line: {営業|えいぎょう}{部|ぶ}＿＿。
exercises.explain: A department name followed by でございます identifies who answers; がございます would concern existence.

exercises.context: Form practice: say that materials are available at reception, using the formal existence form.
exercises.line: {受付|うけつけ}に{資料|しりょう}＿＿。
exercises.explain: The sentence locates existing materials, not identifies someone as materials.

exercises.context: You did not catch an external caller’s name. Choose a considerate request for repetition.
exercises.line: もう{一度|いちど}{名前|なまえ}を{言|い}ってほしい。
options: {名前|なまえ}が{悪|わる}いので、{変|か}えてください。
{恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、もう{一度|いちど}お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
exercises.explain: The first both softens and specifies the request. The second stops before asking; the third insults and changes the request.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: address your manager, then check whether now is a good time.
exercises.explain: A brief availability check works in the internal call. This is one authored order, not the only polite wording.

exercises.prompt: When does visitor reception begin?
exercises.explain: Nine-thirty is staff preparation. Visitor reception explicitly begins 九時四十五分.

exercises.prompt: How does a visitor obtain the online link?
options: Reply by three the previous afternoon; the link follows the reply
Wait for a recording after the event
exercises.explain: The third paragraph specifies the reply deadline and link delivery.

exercises.prompt: What follow-up is promised?
exercises.explain: The last paragraph promises a question-and-answer summary, not photos or video or a purchase.

exercises.prompt: What is known about Ishikawa’s return?
options: They will certainly return at ten-thirty
exercises.explain: The learner says 一時ごろの予定, not confirmed presence or a guarantee.

exercises.prompt: When does Tamura request a callback today?
exercises.explain: 一時半から二時の間 is the requested callback window, distinct from the next-week event.

exercises.prompt: What does Tamura request about next Tuesday?
options: Move the ten o’clock start to ten-thirty, or consider another day
exercises.explain: Tamura requests ten-thirty because the train arrives at ten-ten and offers another day if difficult.

exercises.context: Form practice: introduce YOUR OWN name to a client with the deferential verb 申す.
exercises.line: バオと＿＿。
exercises.explain: 申します is your deferential self-introduction; the other choices do not form it.

exercises.context: Form practice: tell an external client your own colleague Ishikawa is away. Complete the own-side deferential progressive.
exercises.line: {石川|いしかわ}は{席|せき}を{外|はず}して＿＿。
exercises.explain: 席を外しております describes your own-side colleague’s temporary absence.

exercises.context: You represent your company to an external client asking for your manager Ishikawa. Choose the own-side colleague reference.
exercises.line: {石川|いしかわ}が{今|いま}{席|せき}にいない。
options: {石川|いしかわ}{様|さま}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}していらっしゃいます。
{石川|いしかわ}さん、{今|いま}よろしいですか。
{石川|いしかわ}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}しております。
exercises.explain: The first refers to your own colleague to an outsider. The second elevates your own manager over the client; the third directly addresses Ishikawa rather than answers the client.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: identify Tamura’s message first, then say you will pass it on to Ishikawa.
exercises.explain: The learner will pass on a message, not confirm the requested new start.

exercises.prompt: What schedule remains recorded while the reply is pending?
exercises.explain: The last paragraph explicitly keeps the internal schedule at ten until there is a reply.

exercises.prompt: What should happen if today’s callback window cannot be used?
options: Call without checking during Tamura’s later meeting
exercises.explain: The second paragraph directs an email availability check, not an assumption that silence cancels the request.

exercises.prompt: What needs checking before agreeing to the new start?
options: Whether the brochure has already been printed
Mori’s availability and Room C availability
exercises.explain: The handover asks Ishikawa to check Mori and Room C before confirming the change.

lessons.title: Follow a story through short responses
lessons.description: Hear an ordinary café plan with acknowledgements, hesitation and brief overlaps.
lessons.canDo: Separate a reaction from a reason or a settled plan

lessons.title: Recover a reference and check it
lessons.description: Resolve two blue umbrellas and a return time through a clarification and an acknowledged but refused proposal.
lessons.canDo: Identify the object, owner and accepted time in short casual turns

grammar.title: A short response can keep the story going
grammar.formation: へえ reacts to new information; そうなんだ acknowledges it; なるほど often marks newly understood grounds. Follow the next clause before inferring agreement.
grammar.explanation: These short turns show the listener is following, surprised or making sense of a reason. They do not by themselves promise to do an action. The same expression can be flat, interested or sceptical depending on delivery. In these scenes, a short response sometimes begins just before the other voice finishes. Listen through it for the fact or decision that follows. This is applied listening practice with earlier forms, not a newly official N2 grammar list.
grammar.example: へえ、そんなに早く開くんだ。
grammar.translation: Oh, it opens that early?

examples.ja: へえ、そんなに{早|はや}く{開|あ}くんだ。
examples.en: Oh, it opens that early?

examples.ja: そうなんだ。じゃあ、{木曜|もくよう}にしよう。
examples.en: I see. Then let’s make it Thursday.

examples.ja: なるほど、{窓|まど}を{閉|し}めたから{静|しず}かなんだね。
examples.en: That explains it: it’s quiet because you shut the window.

grammar.mistake: A short acknowledgement does not answer every question with yes. Hear the following clause, and do not insert the same reaction after every sentence.

grammar.title: Hear the thought after a hesitation
grammar.formation: えっと / あの + a searched-for word or phrase. Sentence-opening なんか can frame a tentative impression; まあ can soften a provisional judgement.
grammar.explanation: A person looking for a time, a description or a decision may hesitate. Listen for the content after the filler rather than treating the hesitation as a new topic. なんか can also be 何か meaning something, or follow a noun in a dismissive or listing expression. Its place and the whole clause decide the reading. Fillers have several uses; these scenes give particular examples, not fixed one-word translations or a rule that all hesitation is uncertainty about truth.
grammar.example: えっと、木曜の二時なら空いてる。
grammar.translation: Um, I’m free Thursday at two.

examples.ja: えっと、{木曜|もくよう}の{二時|にじ}なら{空|あ}いてる。
examples.en: Um, I’m free Thursday at two.

examples.ja: なんか、{前|まえ}より{明|あか}るくなったね。
examples.en: It somehow feels brighter than before.

examples.ja: まあ、{二人|ふたり}なら{座|すわ}れると{思|おも}う。
examples.en: Well, I think the two of us can get seats.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate every なんか as something or every まあ as agreement. A tentative impression is not a confirmed reservation.

grammar.title: Recover the missing noun from this conversation
grammar.formation: A known noun may be left out after possessive の; adjective + の names the one with that property. A short predicate may omit a contextually clear person or object.
grammar.explanation: In a conversation about umbrellas, 青いの means the blue umbrella, while 美咲の can mean Misaki’s umbrella. Neither の tells you what the object is without context. If several objects or owners fit, ask which one. Omitting a recoverable noun is different from removing every case particle: casual speech can omit some particles, but not arbitrary parts of a place or role. In formal writing, make important roles clear. Earlier N5 の is retrieved at natural pace.
grammar.example: 傘、どれ？ 青いの。
grammar.translation: Which umbrella? The blue one.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}、どれ？ {青|あお}いの。
examples.en: Which umbrella? The blue one.

examples.ja: その{傘|かさ}、{美咲|みさき}の？
examples.en: Is that umbrella Misaki’s?

examples.ja: もう{送|おく}った？ うん、{今朝|けさ}。
examples.en: Have you sent it? Yes, this morning.

grammar.mistake: Do not assume an omitted actor is always the last named person. Resolve the current question and situation, or request clarification.

grammar.title: Check a reference and repair the misunderstanding
grammar.formation: どの…？ / …って、…？ / もう一度…？ asks about an unclear item or turn. Acknowledgement can be followed by a correction or refusal.
grammar.explanation: Friends often use a short clarification rather than repeat the whole previous sentence. Name the unclear item when asking. When Kenta says he can return the umbrella this evening, そうなんだ acknowledges that information; でも、今日は無理 then rejects the proposed time. Understanding and agreement are separate. These are context-based reply skills using known question and negative forms, not a rule to infer a refusal from every unfinished sentence.
grammar.example: 青いのって、入口の傘？
grammar.translation: By the blue one, do you mean the umbrella by the entrance?

examples.ja: {青|あお}いのって、{入口|いりぐち}の{傘|かさ}？
examples.en: By the blue one, do you mean the umbrella by the entrance?

examples.ja: そうなんだ。でも、{今日|きょう}は{無理|むり}。{明日|あした}ならいいよ。
examples.en: I see. But today won’t work. Tomorrow is fine.

examples.ja: {何時|なんじ}って{言|い}った？ {聞|き}こえなかった。
examples.en: What time did you say? I couldn’t hear it.

grammar.mistake: Acknowledging someone’s information is not permission for their proposal. Hear the following clause. When the reference stays unclear, ask rather than guessing an owner or plan.

dialogues.title: A café, a postcard and a Thursday plan
dialogues.scene: Ren tells Yui about yesterday’s visit to their old café. They choose when to go together and arrange to post a card.

lines.line: {昨日|きのう}、あのカフェ{行|い}ってきた。

lines.line: へえ。まだ{駅|えき}の{裏|うら}にあるの？
lines.romaji: Hē. Mada eki no ura ni aru no?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: うん。なんか、{前|まえ}より{明|あか}るくなってて。
lines.romaji: Un. Nanka, mae yori akaruku nattete.
lines.meaning: Yeah. It somehow felt brighter than before.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: そうなんだ。{窓|まど}、{変|か}えた？
lines.romaji: Sō nan da. Mado, kaeta?
lines.meaning: I see. Did they change the windows?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: いや、{窓|まど}は{同|おな}じ。{大|おお}きい{棚|たな}がなくなったんだって。
lines.romaji: Iya, mado wa onaji. Ōkii tana ga nakunatta n datte.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: なるほど。あれ、{光|ひかり}{遮|さえぎ}ってたもんね。
lines.romaji: Naruhodo. Are, hikari saegitteta mon ne.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: まあ、{席|せき}は{少|すく}ないけど、{二人|ふたり}なら{座|すわ}れると{思|おも}う。

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {明日|あした}、{行|い}く？

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {明日|あした}{水曜|すいよう}でしょ。{休|やす}みだよ。

lines.meaning: Tomorrow’s Wednesday, right? They’re closed.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: あ、そっか。えっと、{木曜|もくよう}の{二時|にじ}なら{空|あ}いてる。
lines.romaji: A, sokka. Etto, mokuyō no niji nara aiteru.
lines.meaning: Oh, right. Um, I’m free Thursday at two.

lines.speaker: Ren

lines.romaji: Jā, mokuyō ni shiyō. Mise no mae de ii?

lines.speaker: Ren

lines.meaning: The one for Yamamoto-san? Um, I haven’t put the address on it yet.

lines.speaker: Yui
lines.line: {住所|じゅうしょ}なら、{私|わたし}のメモにあるよ。

lines.meaning: I have the address in my notes.

lines.line: そうなんだ。じゃあ、{帰|かえ}りにポスト{寄|よ}ろう。

lines.meaning: Sounds good. Well, even if it rains, the station postbox is close.

dialogues.title: Which blue umbrella?
dialogues.scene: Kenta and Misaki sort out two umbrellas at a friend’s home. Kenta asks what Misaki meant and then checks when he can return the borrowed one.

watch.prompt: Optionally listen to your own familiar scene. Follow one exchange without the transcript, then check which short replies merely acknowledge and which settle an action. Replay a short overlap instead of guessing a missing word.

recycling.reason: These friends discuss a café and two umbrellas after three formal news/office units. 宛先 is genuinely retrieved in the postcard reading; forcing their unrelated committee or procurement vocabulary into casual turns would make the scene artificial. Older café, colour, time and loan vocabulary is reused extensively. The recent-three-unit target is deliberately reduced to three percent; supplementary conversation vocabulary stays outside the scene quota.
